games.name: 10 Card Regrets Poker
games.description: 10 Card Regrets is a split-pot poker variant. 2-5 players. 52-card deck. Players build TWO open 5-card hands simultaneously: a Low hand and a High hand. Dealt 2 cards at a time, must assign each to Low or High (irrevocable). Cards revealed after assignment. 5 dealing rounds with betting between each. Pot split: best High hand + best Low hand.

games.name: 1000 (Tysiąc)
games.description: TysiÄ…c ('Thousand') is Poland's national card game. 2-4 players. 24-card deck (9-A). Auction bidding + melding + trick-taking. Melds: K+Q same suit = 'marriage' (â™¥=100, â™¦=80, â™£=60, â™ =40). Declaring a marriage makes that suit trump. Card points: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0. Total 120. First to 1000 wins. Musik (talon) taken by bid winner.

games.name: 1000 Tysyacha
games.description: Tysyacha (Тысяча), meaning 1000 in Russian, is a trick-taking card game popular in Eastern Europe: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Poland and the Baltic states. Three players use a 24-card deck (9 through Ace). Points come from card values and marriages (King-Queen of a suit), which also set trump. First to 1000 points wins.
games.players: 3 active players (4 can play with one sitting out per hand)
games.deck: 24 cards (9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each suit)

games.name: 11 Point Black Tile
games.description: 11 Point Black Tile is a Hearts-style trick-taking game played with a double-six domino set. It uses negative scoring: the double-0 counts 4 points and each of the seven tiles in the 3-suit counts 1 point (11 points total per deal). Lower score wins. Three or four players pass three tiles left before play; the leader nominates the suit for each trick.

games.name: 110 (One Hundred and Ten)
games.description: 110 (One Hundred and Ten) is an Irish trick-taking game with bidding, related to Twenty-Five. Played with a standard 52-card deck; the first player or team to reach 110 points wins. Players score 5 points per trick. Card ranking varies by trump suit.

games.name: 2-7 Triple Draw
games.description: 2-7 Triple Draw (Deuce to Seven) is a lowball draw poker game where the lowest hand wins. Players get five cards and three drawing rounds to improve; straights and flushes count against you; aces are high. Best possible hand is 7-5-4-3-2 offsuit.

games.name: 20 dominoes
games.description: 20 dominoes can refer to domino games played with a 20-tile set or scoring to 20. When played as a Blackjack-style game, it is similar to Twenty-One dominoes: players draw tiles aiming for a total of 20 or 21 without busting, with a banker.

games.name: 21 Point Black Tile
games.description: 21 Point Black Tile is a Hearts-style domino game using a double-six set: 21 penalty points per deal. Three or four players pass three tiles left; leader nominates suit each trick. Lowest total score wins.

games.name: 27-28 dominoes
games.description: 27-28 dominoes refers to block or draw domino games using a standard double-6 set of 28 tiles (0-0 through 6-6). Players draw 7 tiles each (4 players); highest double leads. Players match a number on an open end; doubles are placed crosswise. Cannot play: draw from boneyard or pass. First to empty hand wins and scores sum of opponents' pips; or lowest hand wins if blocked.

games.name: 28 dominoes
games.description: 28 dominoes is block or draw dominoes with a double-6 set of 28 tiles. Two to five players; 7 tiles each (2-3 players) or 5 (4-5 players). Highest double leads. Match numbers on open ends; doubles placed crosswise. Block: pass if cannot play. Draw: draw from boneyard until you can play. First out wins; or lowest pips if blocked.

games.name: 28-91 dominoes
games.description: 28-91 dominoes refers to block or draw domino games played with sets of 28 tiles (double-6) up to 91 tiles (double-12). Same core rules: match numbers on open ends, doubles crosswise, first out or lowest pips if blocked. Set size and player count vary.

games.name: 3 5 7 Poker
games.description: Three-stage Guts variant: stage one 3 cards (threes wild), stage two 5 cards (fives wild), stage three 7 cards (sevens wild). At each stage players declare in or out; only player in scores a leg; multiple in then best hand wins and losers match the pot. First to three legs wins the pot.
games.duration: Variable (until one player reaches three legs)

games.name: 3-Card Brag
games.description: 3-Card Brag is Britain's premier vying (betting) card game and a direct ancestor of modern Poker. Each player receives three cards and competes for a central pot. Its most distinctive feature is the 'Blind' betting system, where a player can bet without looking at their cards for half the cost, maintaining a psychological and mechanical advantage over 'Seeing' players. It is fast, aggressive, and deeply rooted in British pub and gambling traditions.

games.name: 30 Point Black Tile
games.description: 30 Point Black Tile is a Hearts-style domino game using a double-six set: 30 penalty points per deal. Three or four players pass three tiles left; leader nominates suit each trick. Lowest total score wins. Same family as 11 Point and 21 Point Black Tile.

games.name: 31 (Scat)
games.description: 31 (Scat) is a knock game. Get 31 points in one suit (A=11, face=10, number=face value) or highest three-card hand. Draw one, discard one. Knock when confident; lowest hand loses a life. Blitz: 31 in three cards declared immediately; others lose a life. Last player with lives wins.
games.origin: Likely Italian in origin; spread through France and Britain and now popular in the USA and Britain.

games.name: 32-card Poker
games.description: 32-card Poker (French Poker) is draw poker using a 32-card stripped deck (7-A). 2-5 players. 5 cards each. Blinds, betting, draw up to 4, final betting, showdown. Key difference: Flush BEATS Full House (flushes are rarer). A can be low (A-7-8-9-10 straight valid). Suit ranking may break ties: ♥>♦>♣>♠.

games.name: 36-45 dominoes
games.description: 36-45 dominoes refers to domino games with 36 or 45 tiles, or scoring to 36/45. Typically block or draw dominoes: match numbers on open ends, doubles crosswise, first out or lowest pips if blocked. Exact rules vary by region.

games.name: 4-2-3 (Four-Two-Three)
games.description: Four-Two-Three (4-2-3) is a Guts-family poker variant. Each player is dealt four cards face-down; players declare in or out simultaneously (e.g. with a coin in fist). The dealer then deals three common cards face up. Players who stayed in form their best five-card poker hand from their four hole cards plus the three board cards; the best hand wins the pot. All who stayed in and lost must match the pot. Game ends when one player stays in alone and wins.

games.name: 4-card Brag
games.description: 4-Card Brag is a British vying/bluffing game: each player gets four cards. Hand rankings are adapted from 3-Card Brag (prials, running flushes, etc.) for four cards. Betting: ante, then match, raise, or fold. Playing blind allows double stakes. Last player or showdown; highest hand wins pot.

games.name: 4-Card Brag
games.description: 4-Card Brag is a strategic variation of standard 3-Card Brag. In this version, every player is dealt four cards and must choose the best three to form their Brag hand, discarding the fourth. This added step of hand selection significantly increases the average hand strength and reduces the luck element of the initial deal. Once the hands are set, play proceeds with the classic half-price blind betting and Brag hierarchies.

games.name: 41 Exchange
games.description: 41 Exchange is a trick-taking partnership game for four. Hearts permanent trump. 13 cards each; bid tricks (minimum 1-2); total bids must be at least 11 or redeal. Bids 1-6 score face value; 7+ score double. Fail bid = negative. Partnership wins when one partner reaches 41 points and the other has positive. Played in Middle East; related to 400 (Arba3meyeh).

games.name: 41 Syrian
games.description: 41 Syrian also known as 400 or Arba3meyeh. Four-player partnership trick-taking. 52 cards, Hearts permanent trump. 13 cards each, counter-clockwise. Bid tricks minimum 1; total bids at least 11 or redeal. Bids 1-6 score face value, 7+ double. Fail is negative. Win when one partner reaches 41 and the other positive.

games.name: 5 Card Omaha
games.description: 5 Card Omaha: five hole cards each, five community cards. Use exactly two hole and three board for best five-card hand. Pot Limit or No Limit. 2-9 players.

games.name: 5 Card Stud High-Low With a Buy
games.description: Five Card Stud High-Low with a Buy: each player gets one hole card and four face-up cards over four betting rounds. Pot split between best high hand and best low hand (typically 8-or-better). The buy is an optional mechanic allowing players to purchase an extra card or modifier; exact implementation varies by house rules.
alsoKnownAs: Five Card Stud High-Low With a Buy Poker
5 Card Stud High-Low With a Buy Poker

games.name: 5-card Brag
games.description: Five Card Brag: each player gets five cards and discards two to make a three-card hand. Hand rankings as in 3-Card Brag (prial, running flush, flush, run, pair, high card). Betting and bluffing; blind play for double stakes. British gambling game.

games.name: 5-Card Brag
games.description: 5-Card Brag is a high-powered strategic variation of standard 3-Card Brag. In this version, every player is dealt five cards and must select the best three to form their Brag hand, discarding the other two. This choice phase leads to much higher average hand rankings (Running Flushes and Prials are common) and significantly reduces the luck of the draw. Once hands are set, play proceeds with the classic half-price blind betting and Brag hierarchies.

games.name: 500 (Sicilian)
games.description: 500 Sicilian is a variant of the trick-taking game 500 adapted for the 40-card Sicilian/Italian deck (Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs; 1-7 + Fante/Cavallo/Re). Bidding for tricks + trump suit. Misère available. Adapted scoring and hand structure for 40-card deck. First to 500 points wins. Kitty/widow for bid winner.

games.name: 500 Rummy
games.description: 500 Rummy: first to 500 points wins. Melds (sets and runs) score positive; unmelded cards in hand count negative. Key twist: you may draw any card from the discard pile but must take all cards above it and meld the drawn card immediately. 2-8 players; 52 cards plus 2 jokers.

games.name: 5000 Rummy
games.description: 5000 Rummy is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in North America and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: 501 (Russian card game)
games.description: 501 is a Russian three-player card game: hybrid of 1000 (dealing, bidding) and 66 (marriage scores, fixed trump). 24-card pack; A,10,K,Q,J,9. Marriages in trump 40, non-trump 20. Bid to 501; clockwise deal and play.

games.name: 51 (card game)
games.description: 51 is a point-collection card game played in China and Japan. Players collect cards of the same suit; A-K-Q-J-10 of one suit scores 51 points. Chinese version: draw, discard, exchange; first to 500+ wins. Japanese version: pick board cards, discard; call "Stop!" with best hand; highest single-suit total wins.

games.name: 52 cards
games.description: 52 Cards is a solitaire (patience) game related to Golf and TriPeaks: clear the layout by removing cards one higher or one lower than the waste. Full 52-card deck; single player.

games.name: 55 dominoes (double-9)
games.description: 55 dominoes (double-9) is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: 55-91 dominoes
games.description: 55-91 dominoes is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.
games.deck: Domino sets (55 double-9 to 91 double-12 tiles)

games.name: 56 dominoes (2 sets)
games.description: 56 dominoes (2 sets) is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: 6 Card Omaha
games.description: 6 Card Omaha: six hole cards each, five community cards. Use exactly two hole cards and three board cards for best five-card hand. Pot Limit common; more drawing and stronger hands than 4-card Omaha. 2-9 players.

games.name: 6-Bid Solo
games.description: 6-Bid Solo: 3p trick-taking from German Tarok/Skat; popular in Salt Lake City. 36 cards; 11 each, 3-card widow. Bids: Solo (60+ pts), Heart Solo, Misère, Guarantee (74/80), Spread Misère, Call Solo (120). A-10-K-Q-J-9-8-7-6; 120 pts per round.

games.name: 6-Card Brag
games.description: 6-Card Brag is a complex partition and vying game that bridges the gap between standard Brag and 9-Card Brag. Every player is dealt six cards and must divide them into two independent three-card hands. These hands are typically played against opponents in sequence (front and back) or used to decide a single highest-rank winner. It rewards both the skill of hand optimization and the traditional bluffing and blind-betting mechanics of the Brag family.

games.name: 63 Pedro
games.description: 63 Pedro is an advanced, high-scoring variation of the traditional American trick-taking game 'Pedro' (itself a derivative of All Fours and Pitch). Played with four players in fixed partnerships, it is famous for its massive point totalsâ€”a single round contains exactly 63 points. Points are awarded for capturing specific trump cards, with the King (30 points) and the 'Pedros' (the two 5s of the trump color) being the most sought-after prizes. It is a game of aggressive bidding and high-stakes trump management.

games.name: 66 German
games.description: 66 German (Sechsundsechzig): two-player trick-taking. 24-card deck (A-10-K-Q-J-9). 6 cards each; turned card for trump. First to 66 trick points (and declare) wins the hand. Marriages (K+Q same suit) 20 or 40; close stock to force follow suit. Game to 7 match points.

games.name: 7 Bridge
games.description: Seven Bridge (7 Bridge) is a Japanese Rummy game. 2-5 players. 52-card deck. 7 cards each. Special rule: 7s need only 2-card melds (e.g., 7-7 or 6-7 is valid). Single 7 can be played as 1-card meld. Draw from stock (discard pile restricted). Lay off on any meld. Go out by melding all but last card + discard. All-at-once meld = double score.

games.name: 7 Card Draw
games.description: 7 Card Draw: each player gets seven cards, then may draw/discard (typically once) to improve. Best five-card hand wins. Less common than 5 Card Draw; often limit or pot-limit. USA.

games.name: 7 Card Stud High-Low
games.description: 7 Card Stud Hi-Lo: seven cards each (two down, four up, one down). Pot split between best high hand and best qualifying low (typically 8-or-better). Can scoop with best of both. USA.

games.name: 7 Card Stud with Wild Cards
games.description: 7 Card Stud with wild cards: same as 7 Card Stud but certain cards (e.g. deuces, one-eyed jacks) are wild. Wilds substitute for any card; hand rankings unchanged. USA; common in home games.
alsoKnownAs: Seven Card Stud with Wild Cards Poker
7 Card Stud with Wild Cards Poker

games.name: 7-card Brag
games.description: 7-card Brag: seven cards each; make three Brag hands (two of three cards, one of one) or similar layout. Back hand must beat middle, middle must beat front. Same ranks as 3-card Brag. UK.

games.name: 7-Card Brag
games.description: 7-Card Brag is a strategic partition variant of the British vying game Brag. Every player is dealt seven cards and must divide them into two independent three-card hands, leaving one card as a 'discard' (muck). This variant offers the highest level of hand optimization in the partition family, allowing players to build extremely strong combinations from their seven cards. Once partitions are set, play follows the traditional British vying structure where bluffing and 'Blind' betting are key.

games.name: 7-Toed Pete (Dominoes Variant)
games.description: Seven-Toed Pete is a connecting domino game in the Fives family played with a double-six set. Four players build a cross-shaped layout from a single spinner, scoring whenever the open ends total a multiple of five and taking extra turns for scoring plays or doubles.

games.name: 7-Truf
games.description: 7-Truf (Sieben-Truf): Germanic trick-taking game; seven as permanent or key trump (Truf = trump). Follow suit; trump when unable. Point or trick count to win. Central European.

games.name: 8-Game Mix
games.description: 8-Game Mix (HORSE-style): rotation of eight poker variants (e.g. Hold'em, Omaha Hi-Lo, Razz, Stud, Stud Hi-Lo, etc.). Each round or orbit switches game. USA; popular in mixed games.

games.name: 9-card Brag
games.description: 9-card Brag: nine cards each; make three three-card Brag hands (front, middle, back). Back must beat middle, middle must beat front. Same ranks as 3-card Brag. UK.

games.name: 91 dominoes (double-12)
games.description: 91 dominoes (double-12) is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: 99 (trick-taking)
games.description: Ninety-Nine: trick-taking with exact-trick bidding. Bid by discarding 3 cards (Clubs=3, Hearts=2, Spades=1, Diamonds=0). 3-4 players; 36 or 52 cards. Follow suit; score for making exact bid and premiums for face-up or revealed hand. Designed by David Parlett 1967-68.

games.name: Abyssinia Poker
games.description: Abyssinia is a five-card stud, high-low poker variant where players 'buy' cards from a central market. It introduces financial resource management to traditional poker mechanics.

games.name: Accordion
games.description: Accordion is a single-player patience game where all cards are laid into one row and compressed into piles by matching suit or rank. A card can move onto the pile immediately to its left or three positions to its left. The goal is to finish with one pile.
games.origin: Europe (19th century, likely England or France)

games.name: Ace-To-Five Lowball
games.description: Ace-To-Five Lowball is a draw poker variant in which the lowest hand wins. Aces are low, and straights and flushes do not count against a low hand.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

games.name: Ace-To-Six Lowball
games.description: Ace-To-Six Lowball is a lowball variant in which aces are low, but straights and flushes count against the hand.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

games.name: Ace-To-Six Lowball (Draw) Poker
games.description: Ace-To-Six Lowball (Draw) Poker is the single-draw implementation of ace-to-six lowball, where straights and flushes count against low hands.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (some tables allow one joker as a bug)

games.name: Aces Up
games.description: Aces Up is a one-deck patience game where you discard lower top cards of a suit when a higher top card of that same suit is present. The objective is to finish with only the four aces.

games.name: Aces, Straights and Flushes Poker
games.description: A seven-card stud variant where each player gets six personal cards and everyone shares a central joker as the seventh card. The joker is a bug: it can act as an ace or complete a straight or flush, but not build non-ace sets.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck plus one shared joker

games.name: Aggravation Speed
games.description: Aggravation is a two-player speed-matching game where players rapidly cover same-rank matches in expanding face-up rows.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck split into two 26-card decks

games.name: Agram
games.description: Agram is a West African last-trick game in which only the final trick decides the hand winner.

games.name: Albastini
games.description: Albastini is a sophisticated point-trick game from Tanzania, likely derived from the Portuguese game Bisca. It features unique rules such as a total absence of the follow-suit requirement and a bidding phase where players sacrifice cards to set the trump.

games.name: Alcalde
games.description: Alcalde is a unique three-player trick-taking game from Puerto Rico. It is an asymmetrical variant of Brisca where one player, the 'Alcalde' (Mayor), defends their position against two cooperating opponents. The Alcalde wields twice the cards and twice the play-power in every trick.

games.name: Algerian
games.description: Algerian (or Algerian Patience) is a grand, two-deck solitaire game noted for its complex layout and unique 'dual-direction' foundations. Unlike most solitaires that build in one direction, Algerian requires players to manage four foundations ascending from Ace and four descending from King simultaneously. With a wrapping tableau and a multi-stage redeal mechanic, it is a game of deep tactical planning and endurance.

games.name: Alkort
games.description: Alkort is a legendary Icelandic partnership game belonging to the ancient Karnöffel family. It is famous for its archaic, bizarre card rankings where Sevens are invincible when led, and the King of Diamonds reigns supreme—unless a Seven is turned against him.

games.name: All Fives (Cards)
games.description: All Fives is a specialized descendant of the All Fours family. While it retains the trick-taking and 'Begging' mechanics of its parent, it shifts the focus entirely to capturing specific point-bearing trumps, most notably the 10 and the 5.

games.name: All Fives (Dominoes)
games.description: All Fives is the quintessential American domino game. Played with a double-six set, it challenges players to create 'scoring ends' that sum to a multiple of five. It is a game of rapid math, blocking, and tactical placement.

games.name: All for One and One for All Poker
games.description: All for One and One for All is a high-churn variant of Five-Card Draw. Unlike standard poker where you draw once, here players can repeatedly exchange their entire hand or a single card through multiple rounds of betting until the deck is nearly exhausted.

games.name: All Fours
games.description: All Fours is a classic trump trick-taking game defined by four scoring elements: High, Low, Jack, and Game. This base profile follows the Trinidad structure, with related English and North American forms listed as variations.

games.name: All Fours (17th Century)
games.description: This is the earliest documented form of All Fours, as described in Charles Cotton's 'The Compleat Gamester' (1674). It laid the foundation for dozens of American and British trick-taking games, introducing the iconic 'Begging' mechanic and the four-point scoring system.

games.name: All Fours (Lancashire)
games.description: All Fours as played in Lancashire, England (notably Blackburn and the Ribble Valley), is a partnership variant that removes the 'Begging' phase found in the classic game. Instead, the leader (Pitcher) determines trumps directly, and the 'Low' point is earned by capturing the card, rather than simply having it dealt.

games.name: All Fours (North American)
games.description: North American All Fours, widely known in the 19th century as Seven Up or Old Sledge, is the classic American iteration of the English game. It introduced the 'Seven point' target and refined the 'Discarding' mechanic when the cards are run, making it a faster and more tactical game than its 17th-century ancestor.

games.name: All Fours (Trinidad)
games.description: All Fours, colloquially known as 'All Foes', is the national card game of Trinidad and Tobago. It is a highly competitive, anti-clockwise partnership game where 'hanging the Jack' (capturing the opponent's Jack) is considered the ultimate tactical victory.

games.name: All Fours (Yorkshire)
games.description: West Yorkshire All Fours is a cherished pub league tradition in Northern England, particularly centered in the Heavy Woollen District (Batley, Heckmondwike). Unlike the classic game, it uses a 'Pitch' start with no turn-up card and features unique regional etiquette such as the 'First Trick Face Up' rule.

games.name: All Threes (Dominoes)
games.description: All Threes is a classic 'point-scoring' domino game from the Muggins family. While the more common 'All Fives' focuses on multiples of five, All Threes requires players to calculate multiples of three to score. It is a game of quick mental arithmetic and positional blocking.

games.name: Alsos
games.description: Alsos is a sophisticated Hungarian trick-taking game blending Jass structure with Tarokk-style announced figures. In the core three-player form one declarer plays against the other two.

games.name: Aluette
games.description: Aluette is a four-player French trick-taking game using a 48-card Spanish-suited pack with a fixed rank order where suits are irrelevant for trick strength.

games.name: American Mahjong
games.description: American Mahjong is a North American Mahjong variant with a card-defined hand system and joker usage. It uses an expanded tile set compared with classical Chinese variants and emphasizes matching published hand patterns over unrestricted fan construction.

games.name: Amerikaner
games.description: Amerikaner is a highly popular Norwegian trick-taking game that combines elements of bidding, secret partnerships, and a kitty exchange. Despite its name, the game is uniquely Scandinavian and features a distinct 'trump-on-the-lead' mechanic where the bidder's first card determines the trump suit and their partner simultaneously.

games.name: Anaconda
games.description: Anaconda, widely known in home games as 'Pass the Trash,' is a high-action poker variant characterized by multiple passing rounds and a dramatic 'rollout' showdown. Unlike traditional poker, players actively sabotage their opponents during the passing phases, making it a game of social manipulation and tactical hand-building.

games.name: Andar Bahar
games.description: Andar Bahar is a traditional Indian banking game of pure chance from Bangalore, Karnataka. One card is dealt face up (house card); players bet on Andar (inside) or Bahar (outside). The dealer deals alternately to each pile until a card matching the house card's rank appears; that pile wins. Also known as Mangatha or Ullae Veliyae in Tamil.

games.name: Animals
games.description: Animals is a hilarious and chaotic reaction game derived from the classic Snap. While standard Snap requires players to shout 'Snap!' when ranks match, Animals requires each player to pick a specific animal and make that animal's sound (or shout its name) when a match occurs. It is a game of pure speed, observation, and auditory focus.

games.name: Anrufen
games.description: Anrufen (meaning 'to call') is an elegant Austrian trick-taking game belonging to the Marriage family. It is distinguished by its 'Call-a-Card' partner selection and a simplified scoring system where only 'Gwisse' (Aces, Tens, and the Last Trick) carry numerical value. It combines the secret partnerships of bridge with the point-collecting mechanics of MariÃ¡Å¡.

games.name: Arba'a Turub
games.description: Arba'a Turub (literally Four Packs of Cards) is a massive-scale Somali partnership game that pushes the boundaries of traditional trick-taking. Using a staggering 144-card deck and hands of 36 cards each, it combines the structural logic of Whist with an unusual 'Progressive Win' condition that requires a team to outdo their own previous performance to claim the match.

games.name: Archie (Poker)
games.description: Archie is a sophisticated Triple Draw poker variant that splits the pot between a qualifying high hand and a qualifying low hand. It is widely considered one of the 'swingiest' games in mixed-game rotations due to the strict qualifiers (usually Jacks or Better for high and 8 or Better for low).
alsoKnownAs: Jacks or Better and Eight or Better Triple Draw

games.name: Archie Poker
games.description: Archie Poker (Archie) is a triple draw high/low split poker game. Five cards each; three draw rounds with betting (small, small, big, big). Pot is split between best qualifying high hand (pair of 9s or better, house rules vary) and best qualifying low (eight or better, ace-to-five). No qualifying high allows low to scoop; no qualifiers may split or go to best hand (house rules). Considered one of the most complex poker variants because hand value shifts across draws.
games.players: 2-6 (often capped at 6 to avoid deck shortage)

games.name: Arizona 29-card Pitch
games.description: Arizona 29-card Pitch is a specialized regional evolution of the classic American game Pitch (Setback). It uses a condensed 29-card deck and incorporates an unbeatable Joker into the trump hierarchy. Played in partnerships, it rewards both the capture of legendary cards (High, Low, Jack) and the strategic management of a 5-card kitty.

games.name: Arlington
games.description: Arlington, often called Oklahoma Rummy, is a complex contract rummy game played over seven distinct hands. It features an aggressive 'wild-stealing' mechanic and a unique 'Offering' phase after every turn, making it much more interactive than standard Draw-and-Discard rummy games.

games.name: Asserufen Schafkopf
games.description: Asserufen Schafkopf (Ace-calling Schafkopf) is a four-player variant of PfÃ¤lzer Schafkopf. The game announcer calls an ace of a suit to choose a partner; the holder of that ace is the teammate but stays hidden until playing the called ace. In calling games hearts (Herz) is trump. Uses French-suited cards. Caller leads; when the called suit is led, the holder must play the called ace if possible (Unten Raus). Solo options also exist.

games.name: Asso Pigliatutto
games.description: Asso Pigliatutto ('Ace Takes All') is a variant of the classic Italian game Scopa. The defining twist is that playing an Ace allows a player to capture ALL cards on the table instantly. While it simplifies the math for beginners, it adds a layer of 'Ace-hoarding' strategy that changes the flow of the game significantly.

games.name: Asszorti
games.description: Asszorti is a Hungarian trick-taking game for three players that blends elements of Preferansz and Tarokk. Players bid to become the soloist, with the bid level determining how many cards they can exchange from the 'talon' (3, 2, 1, or none). The soloist's goal is to win at least 6 of the 11 tricks, often while attempting the challenging 'ArrivÃ¡zs'â€”winning the final three tricks.

games.name: Auction Bridge
games.description: Auction Bridge is the historic bridge variant that bridged the gap between Bridge Whist and modern Contract Bridge. Unlike modern Bridge, in Auction Bridge, all tricks won above six count toward the game score if the contract is fulfilled, making the bidding process less about strict precision and more about competition for the trump suit.

games.name: Auction Draw Dominoes
games.description: Auction Draw Dominoes is a high-stakes gambling variant of the classic Draw Dominoes game. It introduces a chip-based economy where players pay to draw tiles from the boneyard, and most uniquely, participate in a competitive auction for the final two remaining tiles in the boneyard. The winner of the hand claims the entire accumulated chip pool.
games.origin: Modern gambling variant of Draw dominoes played with chips and an auction for the last tiles, described in English-language domino circles.

games.name: Auction Forty-Fives
games.description: Auction Forty-Fives (45s, Nova Scotia style) is a partnership trick game: 4 or 6 players, 5 cards each plus 4-card kitty. Bid in 5s (min 15-20); high bidder declares trump and may exchange with kitty. First team to 120 wins. Trump: 5 highest, then J, then A of hearts (always trump). Each trick 5 points; highest trump in trick +5. Special: 30 for 60 (win all tricks); 60 for 120 when below zero. Part of the Forty-Fives and Spoil Five family; regional rules vary.

games.name: Auction Poker
games.description: Auction Poker is a dynamic Stud variant where the primary mechanic is 'buying' improved position or cards from a communal marketplace. Unlike standard poker where you are dealt what you get, Auction Poker allows players to actively purchase cards from a face-up display or the top of the deck, paying a premium to the pot to refine their hand before betting rounds.

games.name: Australian Patience
games.description: Australian Patience is a strategic solitaire game that blends the layout of Klondike with the move-logic of Scorpion. It is characterized by having all tableau cards face-up from the start, requiring the player to build down in suit. Unlike Klondike, any cards sitting on top of a card being moved are carried along, making it a game of foresight and column management.

games.name: Austrian Dominoes
games.description: Austrian Dominoes is a unique European variant traditionally played with a Double-Eight set. Its most striking features are the complete removal of all double tiles and a 'brick-layer' tableau formation where tiles are matched side-by-side rather than end-to-end. It is a strategic draw game where players value 'heavier' tiles early in the round.

games.name: Authors
games.description: Authors is a classic memory-based card game where players compete to collect complete sets (books) of four cards of the same rank. Unlike 'Go Fish,' where players ask for a whole rank, Authors requires the precision of asking for a specific card by both rank and suit. It rewards keen observation and a sharp memory of which cards have been requested and by whom.

games.name: Avinas
games.description: Avinas, which translates to 'Ram', is the Lithuanian cousin of the German Schafkopf. Played primarily in the Jurbarkas region, it is a four-player partnership trick-taking game with a highly idiosyncratic trump hierarchy that includes the Queen of Clubs and the Seven of the trump suit as the two highest cards. It is a game of community, tradition, and numerical precision.

games.name: Baccarat
games.description: Baccarat is the world's most prestigious casino banking game, synonymous with high stakes and cinematic glamour. Though famously complex in its adjudication, the game is mechanically simple for players: they bet on whether the 'Player' hand or the 'Banker' hand will achieve a total closest to nine. In its most popular form, Punto Banco, all decisions are dictated by a fixed 'Table of Play', removing all player agency after the initial bet is placed.

games.name: Baccarat Banque
games.description: Baccarat Banque (also known as Baccarat à Deux Tableaux) is the most prestigious and intellectually challenging form of Baccarat. Played at massive kidney-shaped tables in Europe's most exclusive casinos, it features a single Banker who handles the shoe and plays against two separate hands—representing the left and right sides of the table—simultaneously. It is a game of immense bankrolls, complex drawing choices, and high-altitude gambling psychology.

games.name: Baccarat Punto Banco
games.description: Baccarat Punto Banco is the most prevalent version of Baccarat in modern casinos, particularly in Las Vegas and Macau. Unlike the original French variants where players make tactical decisions, Punto Banco is strictly mechanical. The dealer handles all cards according to fixed rules, making it a pure game of chance where the player's only choice is the initial wager.
games.origin: Havana, Cuba (later spread to Las Vegas and Macau)

games.name: Báciga
games.description: Báciga is the distinct Uruguayan evolution of the Spanish fishing game 'Escoba'. While it retains the core mechanic of capturing cards that sum to 15, Báciga adds a layer of 'declarations' (hand combinations) similar to Poker or Rummy. Points are scored through table captures, 'Escobas' (clearing the table), and special three-card combos like the 'Chorizo'. It is widely celebrated in Uruguay as a faster, more combo-driven alternative to Truco.

games.name: Back Alley
games.description: Back Alley is a robust partnership trick-taking game that originated in the American military. It combines the bidding intensity of Spades with the fluctuating hand sizes of Oh Hell!. Played with two unique Jokers known as 'Bloopers', the game follows a 26-hand schedule that tests a team's ability to communicate and predict trick counts under constantly changing conditions. Its reputation is built on high-pressure bidding where missing a contract results in severe point penalties.

games.name: Backstab Fish
games.description: Backstab Fish is a high-octane, multi-deck evolution of the classic Go Fish. Designed for large groups (up to 10 players), it utilizes two full decks and four Jokers to create a chaotic environment where memory and deception are paramount. Unlike the child's version, Backstab Fish features aggressive 'Quantity Bidding' and rules that allow players to 'backstab' opponents by stealing specific duplicates or utilizing Jokers as wild 'spies'.

games.name: Badacey
games.description: Badacey is a high-skill, split-pot poker variant that combines the unique hand-building of Badugi with the classic Ace-to-Five Lowball. Players are dealt five cards and undergo three rounds of drawing to create two distinct winning combinations: a 4-card Badugi hand (all different suits and ranks) and a 5-card Lowball hand. It is a 'mixed game' favorite in high-stakes circles, prized for its complex mathematical crossovers.

games.name: Badeucy
games.description: Badeucy is a sophisticated split-pot poker variant that blends the mechanics of Badugi with Deuce-to-Seven Triple Draw. In this high-stakes favorite, players aim to build two specific low hands: a 4-card 'Badugi' (four different suits and ranks) and a 5-card Deuce-to-Seven low. Unlike its sister game Badacey, Aces in Badeucy are always high and detrimental, making the 2-3-4-5-7 'Wheel' the ultimate goal.

games.name: Badugi
games.description: Badugi is a unique and fascinating poker variant characterized by its triple-draw mechanic and four-card hand structure. Unlike traditional poker, where flushes and straights are valued, Badugi is a 'lowball' game that penalizes matching suits and ranks. The ultimate goal is to hold a 'Badugi'â€”four cards of distinct suits and distinct ranks, with the lowest possible values. It's a game of deception, probability, and ruthless discarded-card tracking.

games.name: Bagchen
games.description: Bagchen (meaning 'Great Game' or 'Bird Game') is the national domino game of Tibet. Played with a double set of Chinese dominoes (64 tiles), it is a sophisticated trick-taking game similar to the Chinese classic Tien Gow. However, Bagchen introduces a brutal 'Scorched Earth' victory condition: winning individual tricks is merely a means to an end; the only trick that truly matters is the very last one. It involves complex 'set' leading, where players can play up to four tiles at once in coordinated formations.

games.name: Bai Choi
games.description: Bai Choi is a traditional Vietnamese card-and-performance game family using dedicated Bai Choi cards and call-response play.

games.name: Bai Fen
games.description: Bai Fen (literally 'Hundred Points') is a foundational Chinese trick-taking game that serves as the progenitor to more complex multi-deck games like Tractor (Sheng Ji). Played with a single 54-card deck, it is a game of partnership survival where the Attacking team tries to capture specific point cards (5s, 10s, and Kings) while the Defending team protects their lead. It features a trump system where a trump rank is rotated and combined with jokers to create a powerful hierarchy.

games.name: Baloot
games.description: Baloot is the quintessential card game of Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, a high-strategy trick-taking contest derived from the French Belote. Played by four players in partnerships, it revolves around two primary contracts: 'Sun' (No-Trump) and 'Hokom' (Trump). The game is famous for its complex card values that shift based on the contract, and for 'Projects'â€”valued combinations like sequences and four-of-a-kinds. It is not just a game but a cultural institution, demanding intense concentration and partnership signaling.

games.name: Bam
games.description: Bam (also widely known as Pluck) is a cutthroat trick-taking game primarily for three players, though four-player partnerships exist. Its defining feature is the 'Plucking' mechanic: after the first hand, players who met their trick quotas get to steal the best cards from those who failed, creating a slippery slope where the rich get richer and the poor struggle to recover. It uses a specialized 51-card deck (removing small 2s) and features asymmetric trick targets for the dealer and opponents.

games.name: Banakil
games.description: Banakil is a popular Rummy-style game widely played in Jordan, Palestine, Syria, and Lebanon. The name is derived from 'Bankal', the Arabic term for a 'Wild Two'. Using two full decks and distinct wild card rules, Banakil features a high initial hand size (18 cards) and a counter-clockwise play direction. It is a game of meticulous organization, where players must balance the pursuit of high-value melds against the risk of holding unmatched cards if an opponent suddenly 'goes out'.

games.name: Banca
games.description: Banca (the Italian name for Baccarat) is the most widespread form of Baccarat found in modern casinos, often synonymous with Punto Banco. Unlike Chemin de Fer, the game is entirely mechanical: the Dealer (Banker) and the Player (Punto) follow strict, pre-determined drawing rules known as the 'Tableau'. Bettors do not make decisions about the cards, but instead wager on which of the two hands will total closer to nine. It is the high-roller game of choice, celebrated for its low house edge and elegant simplicity.

games.name: Bandar Q
games.description: Bandar Q is a high-speed Indonesian gambling game played with a single set of 28 dominoes. It is a 'banking' game where one player acts as the 'Bandar' (Dealer) and others wager against them. The game's name comes from 'Kiu' (9), the highest possible hand value. Each participant is dealt two dominoes, and the goal is to have a pip total whose units digit is closer to 9 than the Banker's. Famous for its simple 'Modulo-10' math and rapid turnover, it is a staple of Southeast Asian social gambling.

games.name: Băo Huáng 保皇
games.description: Băo Huáng (literally 'Protect the Emperor') is a high-stakes, asymmetric climbing game from the Shandong province of China. Played by exactly five players with a massive 168-card deck, the game is a unique blend of card shedding and social deduction. Two 'Royals' (The Emperor and the hidden Eunuch) must clear their hands before the three 'Commoners' can stop them. The heart of the game lies in the Eunuch's hidden identity, requiring the Commoners to observe card play closely to deduce who is the traitor in their midst.

games.name: Barbu
games.description: Barbu (French for 'The Bearded One', referring to the King of Hearts) is the ultimate compendium card game, a favorite among French bridge players for its strategic depth and psychological complexity. A full session consists of 28 hands, where each of the four players acts as 'Declarer' for 7 hands, choosing from 7 different contracts. The game is a marathon of adaptability, shifting from punishing negative games (where you must avoid specific cards) to high-speed positive games like 'Trump' and the layout-based 'Domino'.

games.name: Bartok
games.description: Bartok is a high-speed shedding game belonging to the Crazy Eights family, famous for its 'Meta-Game' mechanic. While it begins as a simple match-suit-or-rank contest, the winner of each round earns the right to add a new permanent rule to the game. These rules accumulate across rounds, turning a simple children's game into a complex, rule-heavy nightmare of memory and trap-setting. Unlike its more secretive cousin 'Mao', the new rules in Bartok are explicitly announced, but the sheer volume of stacking triggers quickly leads to chaos and penalties.

games.name: Baseball
games.description: Baseball is a thematic 7-Card Stud poker variant where 3s and 9s are wild, and 4s earn players extra cards. It is primarily played as a high-action 'Dealer's Choice' game in North American home poker circles. For the full technical specification, mechanical rules, and engine data, please see the master entry for Baseball Poker.

games.name: Baseball Poker
games.description: Baseball Poker is a raucous, high-action variant of 7-Card Stud that incorporates the rules and terminology of America's pastime. By designating 3s and 9s as wild cards and allowing 4s to trigger 'extra bases' (additional cards), the game dramatically increases the typical poker hand power. It is a quintessential 'Kitchen Table' poker game, favored for its massive pots and the chaos of players holding 8 or 9 cards in a showdown.

games.name: Baśka
games.description: Baśka (pronounced 'Bash-ka') is a distinctively fast-paced, 16-card trick-taking game from the Kashubian region of northern Poland. A member of the Schafkopf family, it is played with just the highest honors from a standard deck (A, 10, Q, J). The game is celebrated for its secret partnerships determined by the possession of 'Old Ones' (Black Queens) and its high-stakes solo bids.
games.deck: 16 cards (Standard deck ranks A, 10, Q, J)

games.name: Basra
games.description: Basra is the most popular card game in Egypt and widely played throughout the Levant. It is a 'Fishing' game related to Italian Casino, where players capture cards from a central pool by matching ranks or summing values. The game is named after the 'Basra' (or 'Basra Bonus'), awarded when a player clears the entire table with a single card. With simple math and high-stakes capturing mechanics (including the powerful Jack and 7 of Diamonds), it is a fast-paced game of calculation and memory.

games.name: Bastard Brag
games.description: Bastard Brag is a lively variant of Three-Card Brag that mixes the hand rankings of Brag with the card-swapping mechanics of Commerce. Instead of a purely static hand, players are dealt three cards and share access to a 'Widow' hand on the table. Players take turns swapping cards with the Widow to improve their hand until someone 'Knocks' (stops the bus) or the pot reaches a certain limit. It is a game of speed, memory, and nerve.

games.name: Bauernschnapsen
games.description: Bauernschnapsen (Viererschnapsen) is the premier four-player partnership variant of the Austrian national game Schnapsen. Played with a stripped 20-card deck, it combines the intense card-point counting of the original game with complex partnership bidding and higher stakes. Each round is a battle to reach 66 points through tricks and marriages, while the overall session is a race to reach 24 game points. Famous for its 'Stechzwang' (trump compulsion) and various special contracts like 'Gang' and 'Bauern', it is a cornerstone of Central European tavern culture.

games.name: Bauernstoss
games.description: Bauernstoss is a regional variant of Schafkopf played almost exclusively in the Palatinate (Pfalz) region of Germany. Unlike the Bavarian national game, Bauernstoss simplifies the trump structure significantly: the four Jacks are always the highest trumps, followed by the permanent trump suit (usually Hearts or Diamonds depending on the village), and there are no variable 'Solo' or 'Wenz' games. It is a pure partnership point-trick game played with high velocity and heavy 'klopfen' (knocking) to double the stakes.

games.name: Be-Ranga Double Sar
games.description: Be-Ranga Double Sar (often called just 'Double Sir' or 'Coat Piece') is the premier partnership trick-taking game of South Asia (India and Pakistan). Unlike Western whist, tricks are not collected immediately after winning. Instead, they pile up in the center (the 'Heap') and can only be captured by a player who wins TWO consecutive tricks (a 'Double Sar'). This unique mechanic creates immense tension, as a heap of 10 or 12 cards can be stolen by a single well-timed King.

games.name: Beggar My Neighbour
games.description: Beggar My Neighbour (also known as 'Strip Jack Naked') is a classic game of chance from the British 'War' family. Primarily played by children, it involves a 52-card deck distributed equally among players. The game is famous for its 'Payment' mechanic: when a face card is turned, the next player must pay a set number of cards. If another face card appears during payment, the obligation passes to the next player. It is a game of shifting fortunes where one can go from nearly winning the whole deck to being bankrupt in a few turns.
alsoKnownAs: Beat Your Neighbour Out of Doors

games.name: Beleaguered Castle
games.description: Beleaguered Castle is a classic 'Open Packer' solitaire game where all 52 cards are visible from the start. The four Aces are stripped out to form the foundations (the 'Castle') in the center, and the remaining 48 cards are dealt into eight 'Wings' (side piles) of six cards each. The player must build the foundations up by suit from Ace to King, moving cards between the wings in descending sequence regardless of suit. It is a game of pure skill and deep calculation, often compared to FreeCell but without the safety net of empty transition cells.

games.name: Belote
games.description: Belote is the national card game of France, a 32-card partnership trick-taking game descended from the Jass family. It is renowned for its unique trump ranking system where the Jack ('J' or 'Valet') and the 9 ('Neuf') become the two most powerful cards, dwarfing the Ace. Players bid to establish a trump suit, declare melds ('Tierce', 'Quarte'), and strive to reach 501 or 1000 points. The term 'Belote' specifically refers to the King and Queen of Trumps held together, a declaration that can swing the game.

games.name: Belote Coinchée
games.description: Belote Coinchée (often simply 'La Coinche') is the strategic, bidding-focused evolution of classic Belote. Unlike the standard game where players simply accept or pass a turned card, Coinche involves a full auction where partnerships bid to reach a specific score (e.g., '100 Hearts' or '120 Spades'). The defining mechanic is 'Coincher' (to double) when you believe the opponents cannot make their contract, and 'Surcoincher' (to redouble) if you are confident they can. It is widely considered the most skillful and competitive version of Belote.

games.name: Belote Découverte
games.description: Belote Découverte (Discovered/Open Belote) is a brilliant 2-player adaptation of the classic French game. It solves the issue of hidden information by dealing cards face up and face down on the table (similar to Schnapsen or German Whist variants), creating a game of perfect information and intense calculation. Players can see many of their opponent's potential moves, making it a chess-like duel of blocking and forcing.

games.name: Bergen
games.description: Bergen is a domino game for 2–4 players using a standard double-6 set (28 tiles). Players extend a single line of dominoes from both ends, scoring points when the two open ends match — two points for a 'double header' (both ends same number), three points for a 'triple header' (both ends same number, one of which is a double tile). The first player to discard all tiles scores two additional points. First to reach 15 points (2-player) or 10 points (3–4 player) wins.

games.name: Bestia
games.description: Bestia (The Beast) is a classic Italian gambling card game of the Rams family, dating back to the 18th century. It combines standard trick-taking mechanics with a high-stakes pool-betting system. Players win shares of the pot by taking tricks, but failing to win a single trick results in the 'Bestia' penalty: the player must match the entire current pot for the next round. It is a game of high tension, calculation, and bluffing, especially popular during festive seasons in Italy.

games.name: Bezique
games.description: Bezique is the aristocratic ancestor of Pinochle, a trick-taking and melding game for two players. Historically favored by Winston Churchill, it is played with a 64-card deck (two 32-card decks stripped). Players score points by declaring melds like 'Bezique' (Queen of Spades + Jack of Diamonds) and 'Royal Marriage' (King + Queen of Trumps) after winning tricks. The game is a race to 1000 points, characterized by a unique 'Trick-and-Draw' phase where hands are constantly refilled.

games.name: Bhabhi
games.description: Bhabhi (meaning 'Brother's Wife' in Hindi/Punjabi, here implying a teasing burden) is a very popular shedding game in South Asia, particularly in India and Pakistan. Known as 'Getaway' in the West, it is a game of 'active avoidance' where players race to get rid of all their cards. The last player holding cards is christened the 'Bhabhi'—the loser. The game is defined by its brutal 'Thulla' mechanic: if a player cannot follow suit, the player who currently played the highest card of the led suit must pick up the entire pile.

games.name: Bid Euchre
games.description: Bid Euchre is a North American partnership trick-taking game derived from Euchre, where instead of offering the turned-up card for trump, players bid competitively for the right to name the trump suit (or No Trump). The highest bidder must fulfill their contract of tricks, or be 'Euchred' and lose points. It bridges the gap between casual Euchre and contract games like Spades.

games.name: Bid Whist
games.description: Bid Whist is a classic American partnership trick-taking game that evolved from standard Whist. It features a competitive bidding auction where partnerships bid for the right to choose the trump suit and determine whether the ranking will be 'Uptown' (High cards win), 'Downtown' (Low cards win), or 'No Trump'. It is particularly celebrated in African-American culture, where it is played with immense skill, sophisticated signaling, and high social energy.

games.name: Bieten
games.description: Bieten (German: 'Bidding' or 'Offering') is a highly unusual gambling game from the Austrian Tyrol played with a 33-card German-suited pack including the iconic WELI wild card. Each player receives only 3 cards, and points are scored for having the best Heart card, the best Leaf card, the best pair/triple, the best sequence, and winning the last trick. Players can 'Bieten' (bet) on any of these categories, escalating the stakes, or their opponents can concede the point. It is essentially a multi-dimensional bluffing game.
games.deck: 33-card German-suited pack (William Tell or Salzburg pattern), including the WELI

games.name: Big A (打大A)
games.description: Big A (打大A, dǎ dà A) is a Chinese climbing game for exactly 5 players with variable partnerships, played with two standard 54-card decks (108 cards total including 4 Jokers). Before play, one player exposes an Ace to become the 'declarer' — the holder of the identical Ace (same rank and suit from the other deck) becomes their secret partner. Nobody knows who the partner is until they choose to reveal themselves. If the declarer holds both copies, they play alone against four opponents. Teams score based on the order in which their members empty their hands.

games.name: Big Game Dominoes
games.description: Big Game Dominoes is a western domino connecting game played with an expanded set to support larger layouts and longer tactical exchanges.

games.name: Big Three
games.description: Big Three (大三, Da San) is a strategic Chinese climbing game for 3 players from the Shaanxi province. It is closely related to games like 'Wa Keng' (Digging the Pit). In each deal, the 3s are the highest-ranking cards, and players bid in an auction to become the 'Declarer' who plays alone against the other two. The game is known for its peculiar ranking (3s high, 2s second) and the restriction that 3s, 2s, and Aces cannot be used in sequences.

games.name: Big Two
games.description: Big Two (also known as Choh Dai Di or Pusoy Dos) is the quintessential Chinese climbing card game. It features a unique ranking hierarchy where the 2 is the most powerful card and the 3 is the weakest. Players compete to empty their hands by playing increasingly higher combinations of cards, including singles, pairs, and standard five-card poker hands. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to manage their high cards (deuces) while clearing their weaker low cards through tactical passing and control of the lead.

games.name: Billitonnen
games.description: Billitonnen is a traditional Dutch domino game belonging to the 'Blind Hughie' family. Players draw their tiles but keep them face-down in a row, turning them over one at a time to play. The strong element of luck is tempered by memory—if you can remember the positions of tiles you've seen others fail to play, you gain a significant advantage. Traditionally played as light relief after a session of the more serious Dutch game Nos.

games.name: Binglao Poker
games.description: Binglao is a high-action Pot Limit Omaha (PLO) variant where the deal parameters are randomized before each hand. By rolling a six-sided die, the dealer determines the number of hole cards each player receives (4, 5, or 6) and whether the game will be played as High-only or High-Low 8-or-Better. Popularized in the Nordic poker community and featured in the Norwegian Poker Championship, it requires players to master multiple Omaha formats and adapt their ranges instantly.

games.name: Bingo (Dominoes)
games.description: Bingo is a historic domino trick-taking game for 2 players based on the card game Sixty-Six. Hailed as the 'king of domino games' in 19th-century America, it features a unique hierarchy where the double-blank tile, named 'Bingo', is the supreme trump. Players win tricks to collect point-values from the tiles, aiming to reach 70 points and claim the deal. This game predates the popular lottery-style Bingo and represents a high-skill adaptation of card mechanics to dominoes.

games.name: Bingo Card
games.description: Bingo Card (commonly known as Bango or Hoy!) is a high-energy social card game that blends the core mechanics of traditional Bingo with a standard deck of cards. Unlike the lottery version, every player holds a grid of actual playing cards, and a 'Caller' draws from a master deck. It is a game of pure chance and social interaction, often used as a fundraiser or party game because it can accommodate hundreds of players simultaneously with minimal equipment.
games.deck: Standard French Packs (Multiple required for large groups)

games.name: Biriba
games.description: Biriba (Μπιρίμπα) is Greece's most popular card game, a rich and strategic partnership rummy game. Played with two decks and four Jokers, it challenges players to form sets and runs, including at least one 'biriba' (a 7-card meld), to go out. The game is famous for its 'pot' mechanic, where players pick up a reserve hand once they empty their initial deal. It combines the deep calculation of Burraco with the high-speed timing of Canasta.

games.name: Biritch
games.description: Biritch, or Russian Whist, is the earliest known form of Bridge â€” the game that the word 'Bridge' originally referred to before Auction Bridge and Contract Bridge evolved from it. It is a 4-player partnership trick-taking game using a standard 52-card deck. Unlike Whist, no trump is turned up; instead the dealer (or dealer's partner) declares trumps or calls 'biritch' (no-trump). The dealer's partner's hand is then exposed as a 'Dummy', played by the dealer â€” the defining innovation that would eventually lead to modern Contract Bridge.

games.name: Bisca
games.description: Bisca is Portugal's national trick-taking game, a close cousin of Italian Briscola and Spanish Brisca, sharing the same A-7-K-J-Q ranking. Played with a 40-card Portuguese deck, it features a fixed trump suit revealed by turning a card after the deal, a draw-down-to-empty mechanic, and point-count scoring (61+ out of 120 card points wins). Its elegant simplicity masks rich defensive and offensive play.

games.name: Bismarck
games.description: Bismarck is a Swedish three-player trick-taking game where players score based on the number of tricks they win compared to a 'quota.' Over 12 deals, each player must play each of four different contracts exactly once as forehand: Sang (no trumps, win tricks), Pass (no trumps, avoid tricks), Spader (spades trump), and Valfri (choose your trump suit). Similar to the Polish game Mizerka.

games.name: Black Maria
games.description: Black Maria is a classic British penalty-avoidance trick-taking gameâ€”a precursor and close relative of Hearts. Players desperately avoid winning tricks containing Hearts (1 penalty point each) and especially the dreaded Queen of Spades, 'Black Maria' herself, worth 13 penalty points. Unlike most trick-taking games, there is no trump suit, and the game features a clever card-passing phase at the start of each hand.
games.deck: 52 cards (some variant remove low cards for odd-player counts)

games.name: Black Mariah
games.description: Black Mariah is an umbrella name for several Seven Card Stud poker variants that all revolve around the Queen of Spades or spades in general. In the most distinctive version, a player must hold BOTH the best poker hand AND the highest spade at showdown to win the pot. If those two conditions are met by different players, or if no one holds spades, nobody wins and the pot carries over â€” making it a potentially monster pot that grows across multiple deals.

games.name: Blackjack
games.description: Blackjack (also known as 21) is the most iconic casino banking game in the world. Players compete individually against the dealer to reach a hand value as close to 21 as possible without exceeding it (busting). Known for its combination of chance and mathematical strategy, it is the only casino game where a skilled player can systematically gain an edge over the house through basic strategy and card counting.

games.name: Blind Don
games.description: Blind Don is the strategic two-player variation of Nine-Card Don, a traditional British pub game from the All Fours family. Popular in Lancashire and South Wales, it features a unique two-part deal where players play through the entire deck in two separate phases. The game centers on capturing high-point cards, particularly the Nines and the 'Don' (Five of Trumps). It is a game of perfect memory, as the cards played in the first half reveal the exact contents of the opponent's hand in the second half.

games.name: Blind Hughie
games.description: Blind Hughie is a lighthearted domino variant where players must match tiles without knowing what they hold. Each participant keeps their tiles in a face-down row and can only flip the rightmost tile on their turn. If it matches the central line, it is played; otherwise, it is returned face-down to the left end of the row. It is a game of high luck and social energy, where a sharp memory provides the only strategic edge as tiles cycle back through the player's row.

games.name: Blind Watten
games.description: Blind Watten (Ladinisch Watten) is a fascinating South Tyrolean variation of the classic Alpine game. In this version, the Schlag (trump rank) and Trump suit are chosen in secret by the forehand and dealer, respectively. Their partners must deduce the trumps through observation of the play alone, as signaling is strictly prohibited. It transforms a lively social game into a high-stakes psychological puzzle of asymmetric information.

games.name: Block Dominoes
games.description: Block Dominoes is the foundational Western domino game and the simplest form of line play. Players take turns matching tiles from their hand to one of the two open ends of the central 'train'. If a player cannot move, they must pass—there is no drawing from a boneyard in the block variant. The round ends when someone 'dominoes' (empties their hand) or when the game is blocked. It is a game of simple arithmetic, hand management, and tactical blocking.

games.name: Block Dominoes with Spinners
games.description: Block Dominoes with Spinners is a variant of Block Dominoes where the first double played becomes a 'spinner' â€” tiles can be placed on all four sides of it, creating a cross-shaped layout with up to four open ends. This dramatically increases the number of playable positions compared to the two-end standard block game. The key question is whether ONLY the first double is a spinner, or ALL doubles are spinners.

games.name: Bluff
games.description: Bluff (also known as 'I Doubt It' or IDI) is a tactical shedding game based on deception and rank counting. Players take turns playing cards face-down, claiming they all match the current required rank. Anyone can challenge a claim; if the liar is caught, they take the entire central pile, but if the challenger is wrong, they take it instead. It is a universal social game that rewards a 'poker face' and sharp memory.

games.name: Boerenbridge
games.description: Boerenbridge ('Farmer's Bridge') is the Dutch adaptation of the international favorite 'Oh Hell!' or 'Nomination Whist'. It is an exact-bidding trick-taking game where players must predict precisely how many tricks they will win in each round. The game is played over a series of deals where hand sizes increase and then decrease ('Up and Down the River'). Known for its strategic depth and the pressure of hitting a zero-trick bid, it is a staple of Dutch social card gaming.

games.name: Bonanza Pai Gow
games.description: Bonanza Pai Gow is a casino variant of standard Chinese Pai Gow dominoes that adds two side bets â€” a Bonus bet and a Tie bet â€” alongside the traditional main wager. Played on a standard blackjack-sized table for up to 6 players, it uses Chinese dominoes, three dice, and chips. The core gameplay remains standard Pai Gow (form high and low hands from 4 tiles), but the extra betting circles make every hand a decision point, and pushes â€” which occur ~40% of the time in standard Pai Gow â€” generate payouts on the side bets.
games.origin: Australia (commercialised variant of Chinese Pai Gow)

games.name: Boomke Wies
games.description: Boomke Wies is a Belgian Whist game for four players in fixed partnerships with an auction to determine the trump suit. Players bid a number of tricks (7 to 13) they commit to winning. The highest bidder leads to the first trick and the suit of that lead becomes trump. The special bid 'Boom' (committing to win all 13 tricks) scores 5 points but costs 5 on failure. The game also features 'Meetje' â€” a fallback when no one bids, where the dealer simply chooses trumps and majority of tricks wins 1 point.

games.name: Boonaken
games.description: Boonaken is a lively Dutch Jass-family card game for 4-7 players, famously played for rounds of drinks. Its name is derived from the top three trumps: Boer (Jack), Nel (Nine), and Aas (Ace). It features a unique 'drinking game' structure where players strive to win twice to be safe, while losing twice results in buying the round. It combines standard Jass point-trick mechanics with a competitive auction and card exchange phase.

games.name: Boston
games.description: Boston is an 18th-century French trick-taking game that represents a pivotal transition from Whist to modern Bridge. Played by four individuals with a standard 52-card deck, it introduced a sophisticated bidding system where players compete for contracts ranging from winning a few tricks to 'Misère' (winning none) or 'Grand Slam' (winning all). It is famous for its complex scoring tables and the use of two decks to track game state, embodying the intellectual rigor of Enlightenment-era social card play.

games.name: Botifarra
games.description: Botifarra is the most iconic card game of Catalonia, Spain. A point-trick partnership game related to Manille, it is played with a 48-card Spanish deck where the 9 (the 'Manille') is the highest trump. It is unique for its strict 'Obligatory Trumping' rules and its bidding system, where the dealer can choose the trump or delegate the choice to their partner ('Delegar'). The game is a staple of Catalan culture, combining rigorous strategic discipline with intense social rivalry.

games.name: Bouillotte
games.description: Bouillotte is a historic 18th-century French gambling game that represents a critical evolution in the history of Poker. Emerging during the French Revolution as a derivative of Brelan, it is a fast-paced vying game for 3-5 players. It is unique for its use of a stripped pack and a 'retourné' (turned card) that can complete a player's Brelan into a Brelan Carré (four-of-a-kind). It famously introduced the concept of the 'Cave' (fixed chip stack), which restricted betting to the chips currently on the table.

games.name: Bourré
games.description: Bourré (pronounced 'boo-ray') is a high-stakes Cajun gambling game from Louisiana. A descendant of French Rams, it is a penalty trick-taking game for 2-8 players. Participants ante into a pot, receive five cards, and must win at least one trick to avoid being 'Bourréd'—a penalty that requires the player to match the entire current pot. This explosive mechanic leads to massive pots and intense psychological play, making it a legendary staple of Gulf Coast gaming culture.

games.name: BrÃºs Iceland
games.description: BrÃºs Iceland is the Icelandic partnership version of Brus, played by four players in fixed partnerships using a 36-card stripped French deck. The game focuses on timing powerful 'beating cards', managing risk with the King of hearts, and racing your team to the scoring target.
games.origin: Northern Iceland (SvarfaÃ°ardalur valley; Icelandic variant of Danish Brus)

games.name: Bräus Gotland
games.description: Bräus is an unusual partnership trick-taking game from the Swedish island of Gotland, played by two teams of two or three using a 36-card pack stripped from the standard deck.
games.deck: 36 cards (2–5 removed from a standard French-suited deck)

games.name: Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies
games.description: Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies (also known as Honeymoon Bridge variant) is a two-player adaptation of Contract Bridge. It solves the issue of missing players by using two 'Semi-Exposed' hands on the table. Each dummy consists of stacks of cards where only the top card is visible. As cards are played, the hidden cards underneath are revealed. This creates a strategic duel where players must manage their own hand while navigating the unknown elements of the table dummies.

games.name: Brisca
games.description: Brisca is the Spanish counterpart of Italian Briscolaâ€”a point-trick game played with the 40-card Spanish deck without suit-following obligation. Card ranking: Ace (11pts) > 3 (10pts) > King (4pts) > Queen (3pts) > Jack (2pts) > 7 > 6 > 5 > 4 > 2 (0pts). The trump suit is determined by a face-up card beside the stock pile. Each trick won adds to the player's score pile; the winner is first to 61 points.
games.deck: 40 cards (Spanish deck: A, 3, Re, Caballo, Sota, 7, 6, 5, 4, 2)

games.name: Briscola 151
games.description: Briscola 151 is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Briscola a 31
games.description: Briscola a 31 is a fast two-player variant of the Italian trick-taking game Briscola, played with a standard 52-card deck using Briscola card values. Players capture tricks and count card points, and the hand ends as soon as someone claims to have at least 31 points in their won tricks.

games.name: Briscola Chiamata
games.description: Briscola Chiamata ('Called Briscola') is the sophisticated 5-player variant of Briscolaâ€”widely considered the best form of the game. After each player receives 8 cards, an auction takes place in which the highest bidder privately 'calls' (names) a specific card. The player who holds that card becomes the Caller's secret partner for the hand, without revealing themselves. The other three form the opposing team. Card ranking and trump mechanics mirror standard Briscola.

games.name: Briscola Scoperta
games.description: Briscola Scoperta is an open-hand two-player variant of the Italian trick-taking game Briscola. Each player’s three-card hand and the top stock card are face up, and play uses the usual Briscola trump and point values while the buried stock cards remain unknown.

games.name: Briscolone
games.description: Briscolone is a two-player trick-taking card game without a trump suit. Players follow suit when possible and use Briscola-style point values to win tricks and accumulate a running total over several deals.

games.name: Bristol
games.description: Bristol is a patience (solitaire) card game played with a single standard 52-card deck. It is a fan-type layout in the style of La Belle Lucie, with building regardless of suit on both the foundations and the tableau, and is considered relatively easy to win.

games.name: Brouc
games.description: Le Brouc is a Swiss four-player point-trick partnership game of the marriage group, played with a 32-card French-suited pack and scoring for card points and marriages (including extended K-Q-J combinations).
games.deck: 32 cards (Standard 32: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7 in each suit)

games.name: Brus Denmark
games.description: Brus Denmark is a partnership or solo trick-taking game from the Karnöffel family in which special beating cards, sevens and certain kings outrank the rest of the deck. Players aim to win five tricks out of nine and can score bonus points by "risking" high honours that may be beaten.
games.deck: 36 cards (French pack: 6–10, J, Q, K, A in each suit)

games.name: Bruus North Friesland
games.description: Bruus North Friesland is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from North Friesland in northern Germany. It uses a 36-card French-suited pack with wildly disturbed card rankings, daring and striking bonuses, and a race to a target score tracked with matchsticks.
games.deck: 36 cards (French-suited A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each suit; 5-2 removed)

games.name: Buck Euchre
games.description: Buck Euchre is a cutthroat (non-partnership) version of Euchre for 4-6 players. Each player plays entirely for themselves. Unlike standard Euchre's fixed 4-player partnerships, Buck Euchre is a standalone player-vs-all game. The dealer selects trump by flipping the top card of the kitty, and each player may order up or pass. The player who orders wins or loses alone based on how many tricks they take.
games.deck: 32 cards (Euchre deck: 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in 4 suits; 2-8 removed)

games.name: Buddha's Folly Poker
games.description: Buddha's Folly is a stud poker variant played with match-pot betting. Each player receives five cards face down. The dealer offers one card at a time to the left; players may accept it and discard one face up to the next player, or reject and pass the card on. When a card is rejected by everyone it returns to its originator. Players then declare in or out; those in show hands and the best five-card hand wins the pot; losers who stayed in pay the match pot for the next deal.

games.name: Build-Up Dominoes
games.description: Build-Up Dominoes is a western domino connecting game that uses two double-six sets to increase tile availability for larger tables and longer hands. Players place legal matching tiles to open ends and try to manage mobility and pip exposure while progressing toward hand-end conditions.

games.name: Buki Dominoes
games.description: Buki Dominoes is an Austrian gambling domino game in which four players use a domino tile set, place stakes against a banker, and try to be the first to play all of their tiles or finish with the lowest pip total when the game blocks.

games.name: Bullshit
games.description: Bullshit (also known as BS, Cheat, or I Doubt It) is a shedding card game where players play cards face down and claim they are of a specific rank. Other players can challenge (call 'bullshit', 'cheat', or 'I doubt it') if they think the player is lying. If caught lying, the player takes the pile; if the challenge is wrong, the challenger takes the pile.

games.name: Bura
games.description: Bura is a Russian point-trick card game for 2 players that uses a 36-card deck (6 through Ace). Each player receives 3 cards and draws after each trick. The trump suit is set by the last card dealt to the non-dealer. A dramatic feature: once a player believes they have 31 or more points in hand while the stock is exhausted, they may declare 'Bura!' and those trick points are counted immediately. The target is 31 points.

games.name: Buraco
games.description: Buraco is a popular Rummy-type card game family originating in South America, played with partnerships and featuring unique mechanics like the morto (extra hand). The main variants are Brazilian Buraco (Canastra/Biriba), Italian Burraco, and Argentinean Burako (tile version). Games are played with double decks and involve melding sequences to create canastas.

games.name: Buraco Brazilian
games.description: Buraco (also known as Canastra, Biriba, or Perida) is a four-player partnership card game from Brazil related to Canasta. Players meld sequences of three or more consecutive cards of a suit, aiming to create canastas (sequences of 7+ cards). The game uses two 52-card decks with four jokers (108 cards total).

games.name: Burako Argentinean
games.description: Burako is a Canasta-like Rummy game played in Argentina using 106 numbered tiles (similar to Rummikub tiles). Four players in partnerships meld sequences (escaleras) and sets (piernas) to create canastas (7+ tile melds). The game features muertos (extra hands) picked up by first players to empty their initial hand.
games.deck: 106 tiles (two each of 1-13 in four colors + 2 jokers)

games.name: Burraco Italian
games.description: Burraco is an immensely popular Italian Rummy game related to Canasta. Four players in partnerships meld sets and sequences to create burracos (7+ card melds). The game features pozzetti (extra hands) and has been standardized by the Federazione Italiano Burraco since the 1990s.
games.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships (standard); 2-5 player individual variants exist

games.name: Burro
games.description: Burro (also known as Donkey) is a card game where players try to get rid of all their cards by following suit. The Spanish version uses a 48-card Spanish-suited pack and is closely related to the Indonesian game Cangkul. Players who cannot follow suit must draw from the stock until they find a playable card.

games.name: Busca
games.description: Busca is an Italian variation of CiapanÃ² (reverse trick-taking game) for four players. The goal is to take at least one point but avoid taking the most points. Uses a 40-card Italian or Milanese pack with unique scoring where the Ace of Coins (Pita) is worth 8 points.

games.name: Buy Your Card | Substitution Poker
games.description: Buy Your Card (also known as Substitution) is a stud poker variant where players can pay to exchange cards for better ones. Players are dealt 5 cards (2 down, 3 up) and can buy replacement cards from four options at different prices. High-low game with declaration.

games.name: Calabresella
games.description: Calabresella (also known as Terziglio) is an Italian three-player point-trick game with bidding. It is closely related to Tressette. The main aim is to capture aces and take the last trick, which is difficult because there are no trumps. The game features an unusual card order with threes as the highest cards.

games.name: Calculation (Strategy Solitaire)
games.description: Calculation (also known as Strategy or 'Broken Intervals') is a unique solitaire card game that deviates from standard 'Klondike' mechanics.
