Unlike most solitaires that build in simple 1-2-3 steps, each of the four foundation piles in Calculation builds at a different mathematical interval: Pile 1 goes 1, 2, 3...; Pile 2 goes 2, 4, 6...; Pile 3 goes 3, 6, 9...; and Pile 4 goes 4, 8, Q... It is a game of pure skill and memory where the layout of the 'Waste' piles determines victory.

games.name: Calcutta Horse Race
games.description: Horse Race: gambling card game for 3+ players. Four Aces are horses; dealer turns cards by suit and each Ace moves. Players bet on which Ace wins. Calcutta variant: auction horses then race; first and second share pool.

games.name: California Lowball
games.description: California Lowball (also known as Ace-to-Five Single Draw) is a Five Card Draw Poker variant where the lowest hand wins using ace-to-five ranking. Aces are always low, straights and flushes don't count. Best hand is A-2-3-4-5 (wheel). Often played with a joker as a wild card.

games.name: Call Bridge
games.description: Call Bridge (also known as Call Break in South Asia) is a 4-player trick-taking card game enormously popular in Nepal, India, and Bangladesh. It resembles Spades but with individual bidding â€” each player bids the number of tricks they will win, and Spades are permanent trump. Unlike exact-bid games, players must win AT LEAST their bid (over-tricks are allowed but under-tricks are penalised). It is one of the most widely played card games in Nepal.

games.name: Call Partner Rook
games.description: Four-player Rook variant using all 57 cards. Deal 13 each and 5 to the nest; players bid in multiples of 5 (dealer first). High bidder takes the nest, discards five, names trump, and calls a partner by naming a card not in hand; that card's holder is the secret partner (or bidder plays alone if holding it). Twelve tricks; follow color; Rook ranks between 11 and 10 in trump. First to 500 wins.

games.name: Calypso
games.description: Calypso is an unusual trick-taking game for 4 players in fixed partnerships, invented in Trinidad in the 1940s. Each player has their own personal trump suit (one player has Spades, another Hearts, etc.). Players build 'Calypsos' â€” complete sequences of A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 in their own trump suit â€” by winning tricks and collecting the necessary cards. Completing a Calypso scores a major bonus.
games.origin: Trinidad (invented by R.F. Foster/Ely Culbertson's circle, 1940s)

games.name: Camicia
games.description: Camicia (Italian for 'Shirt') is a simple game of pure luck for two players. It is the Italian version of Beggar My Neighbour. Players turn over cards alternately; Aces, 2s and 3s are 'attack' cards that force the opponent to play 1, 2, or 3 cards respectively. If the defender cannot play an attack card in response, the attacker wins the pile.

games.name: Canadian Salad
games.description: Canadian Salad is a North American compendium trick-taking game where six hands are played in sequence with different objectives. In each hand, players try to avoid winning certain cards or tricks that bring penalty points. Also known as Wisconsin Scramble.
games.deck: 52 cards (with some cards removed for 3, 5, or 6 players)

games.name: Canasta
games.description: Canasta is a rummy-style partnership card game played with two 52-card decks plus 4 jokers (108 cards). Jokers and 2s are wild. Players form melds of 3+ cards of the same rank. A 'canasta' (meld of 7+ cards) earns powerful bonuses. The game originated in Uruguay in 1939 and became a worldwide phenomenon rivaling Contract Bridge in the 1950s. First partnership to 5000 points wins.

games.name: Canastone
games.description: Canastone (meaning 'Large Canasta') is a three-deck version of Canasta played in Italy, also known as Italian Canasta. Uses 162 cards (three 52-card packs + 6 jokers). Features unique drawing rules (draw 2 from stock OR take discard pile + 1 from stock), variable discard pile size, and special bonuses for wild card and Ace canastas.

games.name: Cancellation Hearts
games.description: Hearts variant: matching cards in a trick cancel (no points). Different scoring from base Hearts.

games.name: Candyman
games.description: Candyman (also known as Drug Dealer) is a social deduction game using playing cards to assign secret roles. The Candyman tries to secretly wink at Buyers to sell 'candy' while the Cop tries to identify and bust the Candyman before all deals are made.

games.name: Cangkul
games.description: Cangkul is a popular Indonesian card game where players try to get rid of all their cards by following suit. The name 'Cangkul' means 'to dig with a hoe' in Indonesian, referring to digging through the stock pile for playable cards. Similar games include Burro (Spain) and Donkey (Goa).

games.name: Cap-It
games.description: Cap-It is a variation of Push (Contract Rummy family) where players compete individually over 5 rounds with increasing contract requirements. Unlike Push which uses partnerships, Cap-It is every player for themselves. Players contribute to a pot and winners collect from it each round.
games.deck: 108 cards (2Ã—52 + 4 jokers) or 162 cards (3Ã—52 + 6 jokers for 5-6 players)

games.name: Card Bingo
games.description: Card Bingo is a lottery-style card game where players try to match called cards to their hand. A caller draws cards and announces them; players turn down matching cards in their hand. First player to turn down all cards wins. Similar to traditional number Bingo but using playing cards.

games.name: Caribbean Dominoes
games.description: Caribbean dominoes: draw/block game, double-six. Four players in partnerships; play to empty hand or block. Regional rules vary (Jamaican, Haitian, etc).

games.name: Caribbean Stud Poker
games.description: Caribbean Stud Poker is a casino table game based on 5-card stud poker, played against the house (dealer) rather than against other players. Each player receives 5 cards and must choose to fold or raise after seeing one of the dealer's cards. The dealer must 'qualify' with A-K or better for the hand to play. Caribbean Stud features a progressive jackpot side bet for royal flushes and other premium hands.

games.name: Carioca
games.description: Carioca is an Argentinean Contract Rummy variant similar to Central American Loba. Played over 7 rounds with increasingly difficult contracts. Players try to meld trios (three of a kind) and escaleras (4-card straight flushes) to get rid of all cards. Features wild jokers and the ability to add to other players' melds.

games.name: Carousel
games.description: Carousel is a Manipulation Rummy game where players can rearrange existing melds on the table to create new combinations. Players draw 1-3 cards per turn and must meld after drawing 1 or 2 cards. Features jokers and a knocking mechanic to end rounds.

games.name: Carpet
games.description: Carpet is a simple and rewarding patience (solitaire) game. Four Aces form the foundations, twenty cards are laid out in a 5Ã—4 grid called the 'carpet,' and the remaining cards form a stock. The goal is to build all cards onto the foundations in suit from Ace to King.

games.name: Casino Dominican
games.description: Casino Dominican is a Royal Casino variant played in the Dominican Republic. Picture cards have numerical values (J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=1/14). Features unique building rules, sweep scoring, and special endgame scoring when nearing 21 points. Played counter-clockwise.

games.name: Casino Hold'em
games.description: Casino Hold'em Poker is a casino table game introduced in 2001 by Stephen Au-Yeung. Based on Texas Hold'em, players compete against the house (not each other). Players make an ante bet, receive two hole cards, see a three-card flop, then decide to fold or place a play bet (2x ante). Best 5-card poker hand wins.

games.name: Casino Hungarian
games.description: Hungarian Casino is a Royal Casino variant played in Hungary. Features numerical values for picture cards (J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=1/14) with unique building and capturing rules. Differs from Anglo-American Casino in several key ways.

games.name: Casino Sotho
games.description: Sotho Casino is a Royal Casino variant played in Lesotho. Similar to Swazi Casino with face-up capture piles and the ability for opponents to use top cards in builds. Features numerical values for picture cards and complex building mechanics.

games.name: Casino South African
games.description: South African Casino is a Royal Casino variant played in South Africa. Part of the African Casino family with face-up capture piles and opponents able to use top cards in builds. Features numerical picture card values and complex building mechanics.

games.name: Casino Swazi
games.description: Swazi Casino is a Royal Casino variant played in Eswatini (formerly Swaziland). Features unique building mechanics where captured cards are kept face up and top cards can be stolen by opponents for builds. Uses numerical values for picture cards (J=11, Q=12, K=13, A=1/14).

games.name: Casita Robada
games.description: Casita Robada (Stolen House) is a children's fishing game popular in Argentina. Also known as Steal the Old Man's Bundle or Rubamazzo in Italy. Players capture cards by matching ranks and can steal opponents' entire bundles by matching the top card.

games.name: Cassino
games.description: Cassino (also spelled Casino) is a classic fishing-capture card game originating in Italy and popular throughout the world. Players capture cards from a central tableau by matching rank (pairing) or arithmetic sum (combining). Special prizes exist for the Ten of Diamonds ('Big Cassino', worth 2 points) and Two of Spades ('Little Cassino', worth 1 point). The first player or team to reach 11 (or 21 in some variants) points wins.

games.name: Castle Rock Dominoes
games.description: Castle Rock Dominoes is a western domino connecting game played on a shared layout where players match open ends and aim to shed tiles efficiently over a series of hands.

games.name: Cau Robat
games.description: Cau Robat is a children's fishing game from Catalonia, Spain. Played with a Spanish 40-card deck. Features unique 'Cau' calls and capture of sequences. Somewhat similar to Ronda but with less scope for skill.

games.name: Ce Deng
games.description: Ce Deng (æ–œé’‰) is a Chinese domino game where tiles are laid with adjacent ends matching, similar to Western domino layout. Uses Chinese domino set (32 tiles; 21 unique, 11 duplicated). Best for four players; winner has fewest pips on discarded and unplayed tiles.

games.name: Cego
games.description: Cego: German Tarock from Baden; 3–4p, 54-card Cego deck (22 trumps + 32 in 4 suits). Central hand (Legage/Cego); many contracts use Legage. Developed from Ombre and Dreierles. Two-phase bidding; declarer may play from Cego (central hand); follow suit, must trump if unable to follow; 70 card points total, bidder needs 36+ to win normal contracts.

games.name: Ceki
games.description: Ceki is a traditional Peranakan and Southeast Asian money-card game family played with the 60-card Ceki deck and draw-discard style combinations.

games.name: Challenge Dominoes
games.description: Challenge Dominoes is an expanded-supply western domino connecting game played with two double-six sets. The duplicated tiles reduce early blocking and change inference, so play emphasizes robust end control, mobility, and managing pip exposure under uncertainty.

games.name: Chambéry Tarot
games.description: Early 20th century French Tarot from Chambéry, Savoy. Three to five players; with four or five, partnerships form by Solo bid or dealer calling a King. Objective: win the majority of 68 card points (52 from counting cards plus 15 tricks and the discard). Uses 78-card French Tarot; trumps rank 21 down to 1; Fool may be shown once and added to team's tricks.

games.name: Changsha Mahjong
games.description: Changsha Mahjong is a Chinese regional Mahjong variant associated with Changsha and surrounding Hunan play communities. It preserves classic draw-discard meld structure while following local rule profiles and scoring expectations.

games.name: Charlemagne
games.description: Charlemagne is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Checkmate
games.description: Checkmate: Jordan/Palestine children's game. Crazy Eightsâ€“style; play by rank or suit. Aces force another player to give you a King. Red/black Jokers match any card of that colour. First out wins.

games.name: Chemin de Fer
games.description: Chemin de Fer is the original version of Baccarat, popularized in French casinos and famously played by James Bond in the original 007 novels. Unlike its modern cousin, Punto Banco, where all moves are mechanical, Chemin de Fer is a social and strategic game where players take turns acting as the Banker and make active drawing decisions. The name, French for 'Railway', refers to how the dealing shoe travels around the table like a train.

games.name: Chicago (Swedish)
games.description: Chicago (Swedish): 2â€“4 players, 52 cards. Three phases per hand: (1) draw then claim best poker hand for points; (2) draw again, claim again; (3) draw then play tricks, no trumps; last trick scores 5. Declare Chicago to take all 5 tricks for 15 or lose 15. First to 52 wins.

games.name: Chicago Poker
games.description: Chicago Poker is a Seven Card Stud variant where the pot is split between the highest poker hand and the player holding the highest (or lowest) spade in the hole. Face-up spades do not count—only concealed spades are eligible. This creates a unique dual-objective game where players must balance traditional poker hand strength with the hunt for hidden spades.

games.name: Chicken Foot
games.description: Chicken Foot is a domino game that originated in Texas or Mexico. It is a variation of Maltese Cross played with a double-9 or larger domino set. The game gets its name from the shape formed when a double is played - the next three tiles must be played on the double, creating a chicken foot shape.
games.deck: Double-9 domino set (55 tiles) or larger

games.name: Chinese Classical Mahjong
games.description: Chinese Classical Mahjong is a traditional four-player Mahjong ruleset emphasizing classic hand structure, open information management, and fan-based scoring categories grounded in older Chinese table practice.

games.name: Chinese Patience
games.description: Chinese Patience: 2â€“4 player competitive patience. Shared foundation piles and tableau (four columns). Single-deck version of Russian Bank. First to dispose of all cards wins. Name is exotic only; not from China.

games.name: Chinese Poker
games.description: Chinese Poker (also known as Pusoy, Russian Poker, or 13 Cards) is a card game where players arrange 13 cards into three poker hands (back, middle, front) that must increase in strength. Players compare hands against each other to win units. Popular in Hong Kong, Southeast Asia, and the USA.
alsoKnownAs: Luosong Pai Jiu 羅宋牌九

games.name: Chinese Ten
games.description: Chinese Ten (Jiǎn Hóng Diǎn / 拣红点): Chinese fishing game. Play a card to capture a layout card (pairs sum to 10, or same rank for 10/J/Q/K); then flip one from deck. Related to Thai Red Frog Black Frog and Indonesian Main Merah.
alsoKnownAs: Gob Dum Gob Dang กบดำกบแดง

games.name: Chiva
games.description: Chiva: Caribbean domino game (e.g. Puerto Rico). Four players in fixed partnerships; double-6 set. Play by matching ends; doubles crosswise. Team wins by scoring 4 or 6 times in a row (characteristic Caribbean style).

games.name: Chkobba
games.description: Chkobba is a Tunisian and Algerian fishing card game closely related to the Italian game Scopa. Players capture cards from the table by matching values or making combinations that sum to the played card's value. The game is traditionally played with a 40-card Spanish deck and features the same core mechanics as Scopa, including scoring for the most cards, most coins/diamonds, the seven of coins (settebello), and achieving sweeps (chkobba).

games.name: Chor Voli
games.description: Chor Voli is a traditional Afghan partition card game where players divide their 13-card hands into up to four 3-card combinations, similar to Brag hands. These combinations are then played out in a series of showdowns starting with each player's strongest hand. The game is related to the British game Crash and the Pakistani variant Ramchi.

games.name: Chorizo
games.description: Chorizo is a Uruguayan variant of the Spanish card game Escoba, featuring additional ways to capture cards and bonus scores for declaring combinations of cards in hand. The game is known for its lively, unpredictable nature with sudden changes of fortune. Some variants replace certain combinations with BÃ¡ciga rules.

games.name: Chouine
games.description: Chouine is a traditional French trick-taking card game played mainly in and around the Loire Valley. It is primarily a two-player game, though adaptations for 3 or 4 players exist. The game combines trick-taking with declarations of combinations (marianna) that determine trumps and score bonus points. An annual Chouine World Championship is held in Lavardin.

games.name: CiapanÃ²
games.description: CiapanÃ² (also known as Traversone) is an Italian card game related to Tressette, played mainly in Tuscany and Emilia-Romagna. It is a trick-taking game for 3-5 players where the goal is to avoid taking tricks, similar to the concept of 'misÃ¨re' in other games. The game is the opposite of Tressette in that players try not to win tricks.

games.name: Cicera
games.description: Cicera (also known as Cicera Bigia or Ciccera Biccera) is an Italian fishing card game closely related to Scopa and Scopone, played in the province of Brescia using a unique 52-card Bresciane deck. The game is the reason why Bresciane playing cards are made with 52 cards rather than the standard Italian 40 cards.

games.name: Cinch
games.description: Cinch is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cincinnati
games.description: Cincinnati is a poker card game that involves betting, hand rankings, bluffing. The game originated in USA and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Cinquecento
games.description: Cinquecento is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Cirulla
games.description: Cirulla is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cirullone
games.description: Cirullone is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Clabber
games.description: Clabber is a trick-taking card game of the Jass/Belote family, uniquely popular in Evansville, Indiana and surrounding areas. It is played with a 24-card deck (Ac-9) and features complex trump rankings and a 'meld' system where card combinations like 'Dad' (3-card sequence) and 'Mule' (4 Jacks) score bonus points. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to choose trumps carefully and compete for the prestigious 'last trick' bonus. It is colloquially known as 'Dad' after its most common sequence meld.
games.deck: 24 cards (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9 of each suit)

games.name: Clag
games.description: Clag (also known as Nominations) is a British card game that originated in the Royal Air Force during World War II. The name is an acronym for 'Clouds Low Aircraft Grounded'â€”reflecting when air crews played while waiting for suitable weather. It combines Oh Hell!-style exact bidding with 22 deals including 8 special deals with unique rules (No Trumps, Misere, Blind, Twos Wild, etc.).

games.name: Classic
games.description: Classic is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Clobyosh
games.description: Clobyosh (classic Bela or Klaberjass) is considered by many experts to be the finest two-player card game in existence. It combines the Jass-style trump ranking (J-9 high) with a unique melding phase and a 'Schmeiss' (Throw-in) rule. The game is played worldwide, particularly in Jewish communities, the Netherlands, and the Balkans. It is an intense duel of hand evaluation, bluffing (in melds), and precise endgame calculation.

games.name: Clubs
games.description: Clubs is a three-player American trick-taking game from the US East Coast. Each player has a quota of 4 tricks per hand. Clubs are permanent trumps. Players score +1 per trick over quota and -1 per trick under; the first to reach +11 or -11 wins.

games.name: Cöch
games.description: CÃ¶ch (Cucco, Bergamo) is a 4p partnership trick-taking game from Italy. Special 40-card deck: Figure (Iâ€“X) and Matte. No trumps; follow suit; 10+ of 19 points to win.

games.name: Coinche
games.description: Coinche is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Collecting Dominoes
games.description: Collecting Dominoes is a western domino game where play emphasizes accumulating advantageous outcomes over a hand sequence while still operating through legal matching placements on a shared layout.

games.name: Color Okey
games.description: Color Okey is an Okey scoring variant that gives extra value to one-color completion patterns while using the same 106-tile family.

games.name: Conquian
games.description: Conquian is widely regarded as the ancestor of all Rummy games, originating in Mexico in the 19th century. It is a 2-player draw-and-meld card game played with a 40-card Spanish deck (8s, 9s, and 10s removed from a French deck). Players take turns forcing the opponent to take offered cards or themselves draw from stock, building melds of 3+ in sequence or of a kind. The first player to meld their entire 10-card hand wins.

games.name: Contract Bridge
games.description: Contract Bridge is the world's premier trick-taking card game, demanding extreme levels of logic, partnership cooperation, and psychological depth. Played by four players in two fixed partnerships, it consists of a complex auction (bidding) phase to determine the trump suit and trick goal, followed by the play of the hand where one player's cards (the dummy) are revealed. It is a game of intellectual mastery with a standardized global competitive circuit.

games.name: Contract Rummy
games.description: Contract Rummy is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in USA/UK and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Correlativa
games.description: Correlativa is a Mexican domino game in the trains family, related to Garrafina. Players build matching trains from a central double and, when blocked, draw from a boneyard until they can play or the boneyard is empty.

games.name: Cosmic Turtle
games.description: Cosmic Turtle is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Costly Colours
games.description: Costly Colours is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Coteccio
games.description: Coteccio is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Couillon
games.description: Couillon is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Coup d'Etat
games.description: Compendium game with six different hands per round: Barbu, Waterloo, Siege, Touche, Guillotine, and Dominos. The Director (dealer) chooses which hand to play; players pay penalties to the Director. The holder of the Coup card may try to overthrow the Director by achieving the hand objective; success makes them Director. Winner is the player with the most money after a number of rounds equal to the number of players.
games.deck: 32-card stripped (A-7 per suit) plus optional Coup card

games.name: Courchevel
games.description: Courchevel is an Omaha poker variant popular in France and the UK. Each player receives five hole cards and one community card is dealt face up before the first betting round. After that round, two more board cards complete the flop; then turn and river with betting after each. Players must use exactly two of their five hole cards with three board cards to make the best hand. Best hand wins the pot.

games.name: Court Piece
games.description: Court Piece is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originates from Iran or India and is popular in India, Pakistan, and the Indian subcontinent; also played in South Asia, Suriname, and the Netherlands.

games.name: Crapette
games.description: Crapette is a patience card game that involves tableau, foundations, stock. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Crash
games.description: Crash is a British partition card game (13-card Brag) in which players divide a 13-card hand into 3-card Brag hands and compare corresponding hands for points. The game originated in Britain and is played across northern England, Wales, and Scotland.

games.name: Crates
games.description: Crates is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Crazy 4 Poker
games.description: Crazy 4 Poker (Buy Your Card) is a stud poker variant where players ante, receive five cards (two down, three up), then have three rounds of buying followed by betting. Players can pay 1, 2, 3, or 4 units to replace a card from four options (three face-up cards and the top of the deck). High-low with declaration; best hand wins.

games.name: Crazy Eights
games.description: Crazy Eights is a popular shedding card game, especially beloved by children. The objective is simple: be the first player to discard all your cards. Players take turns playing cards to a central discard pile, matching either the rank or suit of the top card. The eponymous "crazy" 8s are wild cards that can be played on anything and allow the player to change the suit.

games.name: Crazy Pineapple
games.description: Crazy Pineapple is a poker card game that involves betting, hand rankings, bluffing. The game originated in USA and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Crazy Rummy
games.description: Crazy Rummy is a multi-deal rummy game in which the wild rank changes each deal (Aces wild in deal 1, Twos wild in deal 2, and so on). Players draw, meld, lay off, and discard to go out with the lowest cumulative score over the series.

games.name: Crazy Solo
games.description: Crazy Solo is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Crazy Solo
games.description: Crazy Solo (often just called 'Solo' in parts of Eastern Europe and USA) is a trick-taking card game for 3 to 12 players, though 4 is standard. It features a bidding hierarchy where players can 'Go Alone' (Solo) against the others. The game is known for its escalating bids involving specific trump suits (Hearts high) and partnership calling.
games.deck: 36-card deck (Ace-ten: A,10,K,Q,J,9,8,7,6 per suit); 30-36 cards depending on player count.

games.name: Cribbage
games.description: Cribbage is a card game card game that involves gameplay, scoring, strategy. The game originated in England (early 17th century) and has become popular in the English-speaking world.

games.name: Cribbage five-card
games.description: Cribbage five-card is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cribbage partnership
games.description: Cribbage partnership is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cribbage six-card
games.description: Cribbage six-card is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cricket
games.description: Cricket is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cuajo
games.description: Cuajo is a rummy card game of the rummy family played in the Philippines, involving melding, sets, and runs; uses a 112-card Spanish-suited deck.

games.name: Cuarenta
games.description: Cuarenta is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cuban Dominoes
games.description: Partnership block domino game for four players using a double-nine set of 55 tiles. Partners sit opposite; play proceeds counter-clockwise. Players add tiles to a line matching ends; first to empty hand or lowest pips when blocked wins the round. First team to 100 points wins the game.

games.name: CucÃ¹
games.description: CucÃ¹ is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Cuckoo
games.description: Cuckoo is a card game in which each player is dealt one card and may exchange it with the next player; the aim is to avoid holding the lowest card and losing a life. Last player left in wins. Also known as Chase the Ace and Ranter Go Round (Britain), Screw Your Neighbor (USA).

games.name: Cucumber
games.description: Cucumber is a Nordic lose-last-trick game: the goal is to avoid winning the final trick of the hand.

games.name: Cuttle
games.description: Cuttle is a 2-player card game where players use a standard 52-card deck as both resources and attacks. Each card can be played as a 'point card' (placed face-up contributing its rank to your score) or as an 'effect card' (using its special ability against the opponent). The goal is to accumulate 21 or more points in your tableau. Cuttle is one of the oldest card games still actively played in competitive circuits, with origins possibly dating to the 17th century.

games.name: Cyprus
games.description: Cyprus is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Cyprus Dominoes
games.description: Cyprus Dominoes is a regional western-domino connecting game associated with Cypriot table tradition, played by matching open ends and managing hand exit routes across a hand sequence.

games.name: Da Fu
games.description: Da Fu is a traditional Chinese money-card game played in the same money-suited ecosystem as Quan Dui and Luk Fu, emphasizing pair and sequence construction under draw-discard flow.

games.name: Daaluu
games.description: Daaluu is a Mongolian tile game family treated as its own tile family and modeled separately from western dominoes and khorol. Reference descriptions document dedicated daaluu tile compositions with zodiac and flower-style groups in regional variants.

games.name: Dacz Golf
games.description: Dacz Golf is a high-interaction variant of the classic Golf card game, belonging to the 'Power Card' family (including Cabo and Cambio). Unlike standard Golf, players can use 'Power Cards' drawn from the deck to peek at cards, swap with opponents, or manipulate the layout. The goal remains to have the lowest scoring layout, but the addition of hidden information and unexpected swaps makes it a game of memory, bluffing, and tactical timing. It is known as 'Dacz' in Poland and 'Power Golf' elsewhere.

games.name: Dai Fugo
games.description: Dai Fugo (大富豪, 'Grand Millionaire') is a Japanese climbing/shedding game for 3–8 players. Similar to President: play single cards or sets of same rank; next player must play same number of higher rank or pass. First to empty hand is Dai Fugō (Grand Millionaire); last is Dai Hinmin (Very Poor). Card exchange between rounds based on finish position.

games.name: Daifugō
games.description: Daifugō (大富豪, 'Great Millionaire') is Japan's iconic climbing card game, closely related to President/Capitalism. Players shed cards in combinations higher than the previously played combination. The hierarchy from first to go out (Daifugō = Great Millionaire) to last (Daihinmin = Great Pauper) determines a social pecking order for the next round and often involves card exchanges. The game is extraordinarily popular in Japan and known by dozens of regional variants with unique house rules.

games.name: Dancing Dragons
games.description: Dancing Dragons is a Chinese-domino connecting game in which players extend a shared layout by matching legal ends while trying to empty their hands before opponents.

games.name: Dappen Black Forest Tapp Tarock
games.description: Dappen is a complex trick-taking Tarock game for 6 or 7 players, traditional to the Upper Black Forest region of southwest Germany. It is played with Cego cards and features one player (the 'Dappener') playing alone against a team formed by all other participants, using a 12-card talon known as the 'Dapp'.

games.name: Dealer's Choice Poker
games.description: Dealer's Choice is a popular 'meta-format' for home poker games where the player in the dealer position chooses which specific poker variant will be played for that hand (or round). It emphasizes entertainment, variety, and the ability to adapt to shifting rules, ranging from standard Stud and Draw to eccentric wild-card 'invented' games.
games.deck: 52-card standard deck (often two decks of different colors)

games.name: Dehla Pakad
games.description: Dehla Pakad (Hindi for 'Collect the Tens') is a traditional Indian trick-taking card game played by four players in two fixed partnerships. It is a member of the Court Piece (Rang) family, characterized by its unique 'Double Sar' mechanic where tricks are only collected after winning two consecutive tricks. The primary goal is capturing the four tens in the deck.

games.name: Democracy
games.description: Democracy is a unique trick-taking game for 2-6 players where all players simultaneously select and reveal cards. The game features a colonial backstory where players represent powers attempting to annex an island. Cards have special rankings (5-4-3-A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6) and point values, with the goal of capturing majority points in suits to score 'tribes'.

games.name: Derda
games.description: Derda is a two-player Jass game that was once popular in Poland, particularly among currency traders, gamblers, and the underworld during the communist era. It is closely related to Clobyosh and features unique bidding mechanics and bonus scoring for sequences and special cards.

games.name: Deuce-To-Seven Lowball
games.description: Deuce-to-Seven Lowball (also called Kansas City Lowball or Billy Baxter Lowball) is a draw poker variant where the lowest hand wins. Aces are always high, straights and flushes count against the player, and the best possible hand is 7-5-4-3-2 (hence 'Deuce to Seven'). It is the exact opposite of standard high poker except for the A-2-3-4-5 rule.

games.name: Deuces and Jacks and the Man with the Axe
games.description: Deuces and Jacks and the Man with the Axe: 7-card stud variant where all 2s, all Jacks, and the King of Diamonds ('the man with the axe') are wild. Same deal as 7-card stud; many wilds create very strong hands. USA; dealer's choice.
alsoKnownAs: Deuces and Jacks and the Man with the Axe Poker

games.name: Deux Cents
games.description: Deux Cents (Two Hundred) is a point-trick card game popular in New Brunswick, Canada. Players bid for the right to choose trumps and try to win tricks containing point cards (Aces, Tens, and Fives). The game is said to be of French Acadian origin and is closely related to Rook.

games.name: Diablo
games.description: Diablo is a high-action Five Card Draw poker variant characterized by three primary mechanics: Deuces are wild, players are restricted to drawing a maximum of two cards, and most importantly, if the player who opens the betting fails to win the pot, they must 'match the pot' to create a new one for the next deal.

games.name: Dice and Dominoes
games.description: Dice and Dominoes is a western domino table game that combines domino connecting play with an auxiliary dice-driven table profile for pace or scoring. This entry models the connecting core using two double-six sets; dice effects are treated as a configurable profile layer rather than changing tile legality.
games.deck: Two double-6 domino sets (56 tiles) plus dice for the table profile

games.name: Differenzler Jass
games.description: Differenzler Jass is a Swiss bidding point-trick game where each player predicts tricks and points won, and penalties are based on the difference between bid and result.

games.name: Diloti
games.description: Diloti (Î”Î·Î»Ï‰Ï„Î®, from the verb Î´Î·Î»ÏŽÎ½Ï‰ meaning 'to declare') is the most popular and complex Greek fishing game. It combines mechanics from Kontsina and Xeri with a 'declaration' (build) system inspired by Casino. Players capture cards by matching or summing values, protected by declarations that define specific capture sets.

games.name: Dingo
games.description: Dingo is a strategic card game for four players from Cleveland, Ohio. The game features a unique 'hunt' mechanic where diamonds (rabbits) are hunted in ascending order, with hearts (dingoes) and black cards (wolves) playing special roles. Players score points based on card values and hunt outcomes.

games.name: Divide and Conquer Dominoes
games.description: Divide and Conquer Dominoes is a western domino connecting game where layout management and end-control decisions are central, as players try to shed tiles while limiting opponent response options.

games.name: Dobbm
games.description: Dobbm is a traditional trick-taking game unique to the Stubai Valley in Tyrol, Austria. It is an 'Ace-Ten' game related to Tarock and Tapp, played with a 36-card Tell-pattern deck. The name refers to the 4-card talon known as the 'Dobb'.

games.name: Dom Pedro
games.description: Dom Pedro (Pedro) is a trick-taking card game derived from Pitch. 4-7 players (often partnerships). 52-card deck, 9 dealt. Bid for trump suit. Key scoring cards: Right Pedro (5 of trumps)=5pts, Left Pedro (same-color 5)=5pts, High(A)=1, Low(2)=1, Jack=1, Game(10)=1. Total 14pts per hand. Left Pedro counts as trump. Play to 100.

games.name: Domijong
games.description: Domijong is a western domino variant that uses four double-six sets to produce a large duplicated-tile supply. This entry models the core as a connecting domino game; the enlarged supply shifts strategy toward mobility and robust end control rather than precise unique-tile inference.

games.name: Domino Cribbage
games.description: Domino Cribbage is a hybrid game for two players that adapts the rules of the classic card game Cribbage to a set of double-six dominoes. Players score points by creating combinations of tiles (pairs, runs, and sums of 15) both during play and in their remaining hands. It is traditionally played with a cribbage board for scoring.

games.name: Domino Euchre
games.description: Domino Euchre is a trump trick-taking domino game inspired by card euchre, using a double-six set and contract-style play.

games.name: Domino Golf
games.description: Domino Golf is a western domino game played on a larger set where players use standard matching placements while trying to optimize scoring outcomes over multiple hands, analogous to minimizing a golf score.

games.name: Domino Loo
games.description: Domino Loo is a trick-taking game for 2 to 4 players, adapted from the classic 17th-century card game Loo. It uses a standard set of double-six dominoes and features a unique trump-selection process along with a 'widow' hand called the Miss.

games.name: Domino Poker
games.description: Domino Poker is a draw-and-compare domino game where players form the strongest poker-style tile pattern.

games.name: Domino Roads
games.description: Domino Roads is a western connecting domino game played with two double-six sets, enabling larger tables and longer layouts. Players build a shared layout by matching open ends while managing mobility and pip exposure under duplicated-tile uncertainty.

games.name: Domino Rounce
games.description: Domino Rounce is a competitive trick-taking game for 2 to 4 players, played with a double-six set of dominoes. Similar to the card game Rounce, players start with a positive score and compete to reduce it to zero by winning tricks. It features a unique 'dummy' hand and high-penalty mechanics for failing to win tricks.

games.name: Domino Twenty-One
games.description: Domino Twenty-One is a gambling game for 2 to 5 players that adapts the mechanics of Blackjack (21) to a standard set of double-six dominoes. Players bet against a banker to reach a pip total as close to 21 as possible without exceeding it.

games.name: Dominoes
games.description: Dominoes is a family of tile-based games played with rectangular 'domino' tiles. Each domino is a rectangular tile with a line dividing its face into two square ends. Each end is marked with a number of spots (also called pips, nips, or dobs) or is blank. The back of the dominoes in a set are indistinguishable, either blank or having some common design.

games.name: Domizerka
games.description: Domizerka is a western domino connecting game played by matching open ends on a shared layout and managing hand exit routes through careful pip coverage.

games.name: Dompe
games.description: Dompe is a popular Philippine survival card game, also known as Knock Poker. It combines poker hand rankings with draw-and-discard mechanics. Players aim to build the best five-card hand and 'knock' (call Dompe) before their opponents, or win instantly with specific six-card combinations.

games.name: Don Irish
games.description: Don Irish (also known simply as Don in Ireland) is a point-trick game for four players in fixed partnerships. It is a descendant of the 17th-century game All Fours and is closely related to Dom Pedro. The game focuses on capturing specific high-value scoring cards, particularly the 'Pedros' (fives) and the nines.

games.name: Donkey (South Indian)
games.description: Donkey (known as 'Kazhuda' in Tamil/Malayalam or 'Gaadida' in Telugu) is a popular shedding card game played in South India. Unlike many Western card games where winning a trick is desirable, in Donkey, the goal is simply to get rid of your cards. Failing to follow suit results in the 'Donkey' penalty: taking all the cards from the current trick into your hand.

games.name: Doppelkopf
games.description: Doppelkopf (meaning 'Double Head') is Germany's most widely played trick-taking card game, deeply embedded in German social culture. It is played with 48 cards (double deck of 9-A in 4 suits). Crucially, partnerships are NOT fixed â€” they are determined secretly each hand by who holds the two Queens of Clubs. Players use bidding signals to find their partner. The trump suit is extensive: all Queens, all Jacks, and all Diamonds are permanent trump.
games.deck: 48 cards (2Ã— 9-A in 4 suits; 8s and lower removed)

games.name: Doppen
games.description: Doppen is an Austrian tarock trick-taking game in the Industrie und Glück family. It is played with the reduced 54-card tarock deck and focuses on contract choice, talon decisions, and efficient trump timing in three-player play.

games.name: Doscientos
games.description: Doscientos ('Two Hundred') is a highly strategic partnership domino game widely played in Spain and Latin America. It is a straight-forward matching game where all 28 tiles of a double-six set are dealt, requiring teams to carefully track played suits and manage their remaining pips to win the round and reach the target score.

games.name: Dou Dizhu
games.description: Dou Dizhu (Fight the Landlord) is a Chinese climbing game for three players. One player becomes the landlord by winning an auction (bid 1, 2 or 3) and plays alone against the other two in partnership. Players shed cards by playing singles or valid combinations; the landlord leads and each player in turn must pass or beat the previous play. Rocket (two jokers) and bomb (four of a kind) are special combinations. The first side to empty their hand wins the hand; payment is the bid amount times multipliers for bombs and rockets.
games.deck: Standard 52-card pack plus two jokers (red and black), 54 cards total.

games.name: Double Bergen
games.description: Players score for making the ends of the cross-shaped layout equal; first to 100 wins.
games.deck: Double-six set (standard); larger sets optional for variants.

games.name: Double Briškula
games.description: Double BriÅ¡kula (also known as 'Dupla BriÅ¡kula') is a variant of the popular Italian card game BriÅ¡kula/Briscola, primarily played in the coastal regions of Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Montenegro. The 'Double' refers to the unique mechanic where players hold four cards instead of three and play two cards per trick in two sub-rounds.

games.name: Double Draw (Lowball)
games.description: Double Draw (specifically Double Draw Lowball) is a poker variant that expands the traditional Draw Poker format by adding a second opportunity for players to improve their hands. While most commonly played as a 'Lowball' game (where the lowest hand wins), it can also be played for high hands. The extra draw phase significantly increases the chances of completing complex hands but also requires deeper bankroll management and bluffing skills.

games.name: Double Draw Dominoes
games.description: Double Draw is a domino line game using a double-six set. Each turn a player must play two tiles at a time, one on each end of the line, matching by suit. If unable to play, the player draws one tile from the boneyard (when not empty) and passes. The round ends when someone empties their hand (dominoes), when the game is blocked, or when everyone has passed. Lowest pip count in hand wins the round; game is played to 100 points (two-player or partnership) or 61 points (three or four players).

games.name: Double Klondike
games.description: Double Klondike is a challenging two-deck variation of the world-famous Klondike Solitaire. By using 104 cards, the game features a larger tableau of nine columns and eight foundation piles. While the fundamental rules of alternating colors and building sequences remain the same, the increased volume of cards creates more opportunities for advanced maneuvering and sequencing.

games.name: Double Sir (Court Piece)
games.description: Double Sir (also known as Double Sar or Double Sir-Bandi) is a popular and strategic variant of Court Piece (Rang) played extensively in India and Pakistan. It is a trickndtaking game for four players in fixed partnerships. The defining feature of Double Sir is that a player can only capture tricks from the table if they win two consecutive tricks, adding a layered tactical challenge to standard whist-style play.

games.name: Double Takes
games.description: Double Takes is a western domino game played with a double-15 set, using the larger value range to support long sessions and more complex end control. Players use standard matching placements while managing high-value risk and mobility across a wide range of open-end values.

games.name: Double Yukon (Solitaire)
games.description: Double Yukon is a massive, two-deck variation of the famous Yukon Solitaire. Unlike Klondike, all 104 cards are dealt into the tableau at once, with no stock or waste pile. The game is known for its 'group move' mechanic, allowing players to move any visible stack of cards regardless of their sequence, provided the base card of the stack fits the alternating-color building rule. This makes Double Yukon a deep, analytical game with high win rates for careful players.

games.name: Down and Back
games.description: Down and Back is a rare and intriguing rummy-style card game discovered in Lancashire, England. The game centers on splitndhand management: players must divide their seven cards into a four-card 'Going Down' hand and a three-card 'Coming Back' hand. With only six turns to optimize their holdings, the game is a fast-paced exercise in probability and tactical discarding.

games.name: Draw Dominoes
games.description: One of the simplest and most common domino games: form a single line by matching ends; if you cannot play, draw from the boneyard until you can play or only two tiles remain. First to empty hand or lowest pips in a blocked game wins the hand; play to 100 (2P/partnership) or 61 (3–4P).
games.deck: Double-6 domino set; 7 tiles each for 2–3 players, 6 each for 4; remainder is boneyard.

games.name: Dreeg (NÃ¼rnberger Dreck)
games.description: Dreeg (a Franconian dialect form of 'Dreck', meaning trash or muck) is a complex, multiphase card game from the Nuremberg region of Germany. It is a composite game consisting of eight distinct sub-games, all based on the mechanics of Sechsundsechzig (66). Players compete to erase 'strokes' from their slate, and the game is strictly one of elimination: in each phase, players drop out as they succeed, until only one 'loser' remains to face the next challenge.

games.name: Dreierles (Baden Tarock)
games.description: Dreierles (also known as Dreierle or Dreier) is a sophisticated trick-taking game from the Baden region of Germany, played with a 54-card Cego (Tarot) deck. It belongs to the Tarock family and is closely related to Austrian Tapp Tarock. In Dreierles, a single declarer plays against a team of opponents, utilizing a six-card 'blind' (talon) from which they draw exactly three cards to improve their hand, giving the game its name.

games.name: Dreiertarock
games.description: Dreiertarock is a three-player Austrian tarock game family using a 54-card Industrie und Glueck deck. It covers classic declarer-versus-defenders contract play and includes related branches such as Tapp and Point Tarock.

games.name: Droggn
games.description: Droggn is a rare Tyrolean trick-taking game from the Stubai Valley, historically played with a unique 66-card Tarock deck. It is a descendant of the Tarock L'Hombre family, making it distinct from more common Austrian variants like KÃ¶nigrufen. Known for its specific Tyrolean dialect terminology and the tactical use of the 'Fox' card, the game survived in the alpine villages of Fulpmes and Telfes as a testament to localized card-playing traditions.

games.name: Droggn Tarock
games.description: Droggn (a Tyrolean dialect for 'playing Tarock') is a unique three-player card game from the Stubai Valley in Austria. Unlike the major Austrian Tarock games like Königrufen, Droggn is a direct descendant of the archaic Tarok L'Hombre family. It uses a rare 66-card French-suited Tarock deck and is known for its complex trick-play and specialized Tyrolean terminology. The game was nearly extinct until recorded by card game historians in the late 1990s.

games.name: Dubbelkingen
games.description: Dubbelkingen (Double King) is the premier Flemish variation of the European compendium game known as King. Played primarily in Belgium, it is an marathon trick-taking game consisting of 20 distinct deals. The first half of the game focuses on 'Negative' contracts where players must avoid specific cards or tricks to sidestep penalty points, while the second half switches to 'Positive' contracts where players bid and seek to win tricks. Dubbelkingen adds a strategic layer by allowing players to choose their contracts based on their hand strength, rather than following a fixed sequence.

games.name: Dudák
games.description: Dudák (Czech for 'Bagpiper') is a popular Czech shedding game closely related to the Russian game Durak. Played with a 32ndcard Germanndsuited deck, the game is a contest of attrition where players must defend against 'attacks' by beating cards with higher ranks or trumps. The goal is to empty one's hand; the last player left holding cards is the loser—the Dudák.

games.name: Durak
games.description: Durak ('Fool' in Russian) is Russia's most widely played card game. The goal is to NOT be the last player holding cardsâ€”the last player is the 'Durak' (Fool). Players attack with cards; the defender must beat each attacking card with a higher card of the same suit or any trump. If unable to defend, they take all attacked cards into their hand. A 36-card deck is used (6 through Ace). After each bout, players draw to replenish to 6 cards. The Podkidnoy (passing) variantâ€”where the attack can be redirected to the next playerâ€”is the standard form.

games.name: Durak Perevodnoy (Transfer Durak)
games.description: Durak Perevodnoy (Transfer Fool) is a fast-paced and highly tactical variation of the classic Russian shedding game Durak. While it retains the core 'attack-defense' mechanics of Podkidnoy Durak, it introduces the critical ability to 'transfer' an attack. Instead of defending, a player can play a card of the same rank as the attacker's card to shift the entire burden of defense onto the next player. This creates volatile rounds where a single card lead can grow into a massive pile of cards that moves around the table until someone is unable to defend or transfer.

games.name: Durak Prostoy (Simple Durak)
games.description: Durak Prostoy (Simple Fool) is the archaic and most straightforward version of the Russian card game Durak. Predating the popular 'Podkidnoy' (throw-in) and 'Perevodnoy' (transfer) variants, it simplifies the interaction between players. In Prostoy, an attacker leads a card or a group of cards of the same rank, and the defender must either beat all of them or pick them up. There are no secondary attacks or throwing in of cards once the defense has begun, making for a faster, more linear game focused on card-for-card strength.

games.name: Durak Severnyi (Northern Durak)
games.description: Durak Severnyi (Northern Fool) is an atmospheric and high-stakes variant of the Russian card game Durak, primarily played in the Northern regions of Russia and Siberia. While it follows the standard Podkidnoy (throw-in) mechanics for the majority of the game, it contains a legendary 'sting in the tail': a late-game trump suit shift. By hiding the final trump identity until the very last card is drawn, Durak Severnyi forces players to maintain a balanced hand of all suits, as a dominant lead in the initial trump suit can instantly turn into a liability at the game's climax.

games.name: Earl of Coventry
games.description: Earl of Coventry is a classic English 'Stops' or matching round game, closely related to Snip Snap Snorum. Unlike many complex card games, it is defined by its rhythmic verbal component - players recite rhyming phrases as they match the ranks played by their opponents. The game is a fast-paced shedding contest where the primary goal is to reach the 'stop' card (the fourth card of a rank) to regain control of the lead. Historically popular as a Victorian-era parlor game, it remains a charming social exercise in rhythm and rank tracking.

games.name: Écarté
games.description: Ã‰cartÃ© (French for 'discarded') is one of the most elegant and historically significant two-player trick-taking games from France. Popularized in the early 19th century, it is famous for its unique card ranking (where the King is highest and the Ace sits between the King and Queen) and its signature 'proposal' mechanic, where players must negotiate whether to discard and draw new cards. It is a game of high tension, as refusing a proposal can lead to double penalties, making every decision a psychological contest.

games.name: Egyptian Ratscrew
games.description: Egyptian Ratscrew (ERS) is a high-energy, reflex-based card game combining War-style card playing with a social 'slapping' mechanic. Players take turns playing one card face-up to a central pile; when specific combinations appear (pairs, sandwiches, sequences, top-bottom matches, etc.), all players race to slap the pile. The fastest player takes all the pile's cards. The goal is to collect all 52 cards.

games.name: Eight Off Solitaire
games.description: Eight Off is a sophisticated and highly winnable solitaire card game that served as a direct precursor to the ubiquitous FreeCell. Its defining feature is the namesake eight 'free cells' (reserves)â€”twice the number found in its more famous descendant. However, this extra mobility is balanced by a stricter building rule: cards in the tableau must be built down by the CORRECT SUIT, rather than alternating colors. This makes Eight Off a pure game of logic and strategy where almost every deal can be solved with perfect planning.

games.name: Eighty-Eight (Texas 88)
games.description: Eighty-Eight (also known as Texas 88) is an expansive, 6-player variation of the classic Texan domino game 'Texas 42'. Played with two full sets of Double-Six dominoes, the game scales up the complexity and the math, with 88 points available in every hand. Two teams of three players compete to outbid each other and reach 500 points first. It is a game of high communication, careful tracking of identical tiles, and intense partnership coordination, making it a favorite for large gatherings in its home state.
games.deck: Two sets of Double-Six Dominoes (56 tiles total)

games.name: Eighty-Three
games.description: 83: trick-taking game; first to 83 points (or similar target) wins. Trump and follow-suit rules; point cards in tricks. Exact rules vary by region (e.g. Indian 83).

games.name: Eleusis
games.description: Eleusis is a groundbreaking card game that functions more as a simulation of scientific discovery than a traditional trick-taking or shedding game. Invented by Robert Abbott in 1956, it is a game of inductive reasoning where the rules of play are not known at the start. One player, acting as 'God' or 'Nature', secretly writes down a mathematical or logical rule governing which cards may follow others. The remaining players must intuit this rule through trial and errorâ€”observing which of their plays are accepted as 'legal' or rejected as 'illegal'â€”effectively practicing the scientific method to empty their hands.

games.name: Eléwénjewé
games.description: ElÃ©wÃ©njewÃ© (or ElÃ©wÃ©njewÃ©nÃ³mbÃ jenÃ³mbÃ ) is a traditional Nigerian 'fishing' card game primarily played in Yoruba communities. The name translates to 'eleven leaves' (or eleven elements), referencing the goal of gathering cards from a central area. Players use cards from their hand to 'scoop' cards of matching rank or sum from the table, known as the 'Palette'. It is played in both competitive 'Professional' and casual 'Amateur' formats, with the professional game featuring the strict 'Yoruba Rules' that forbid duplicate cards in a single capture.

games.name: Empat Satu (41)
games.description: Empat Satu (which means 'Forty-One' in Indonesian) is a fast-paced draw-and-discard card game popular throughout Southeast Asia. The game is a test of optimization where players manage a small 4-card hand, attempting to collect four cards of the same suit. The legendary '41' is achieved by holding an Ace and three 10-value cards of the same suit. Because hands are small and the deck is large, the game moves rapidly, often ending in just a few turns when a player 'knocks' or declares a stop.

games.name: Empat Satu (41)
games.description: Empat Satu (which means 'Forty-One' in Indonesian) is a fast-paced draw-andnd-discard card game popular throughout Southeast Asia. The game is a test of optimization where players manage a small 4-card hand, attempting to collect four cards of the same suit. The legendary '41' is achieved by holding an Ace and three 10ndvalue cards of the same suit. Because hands are small and the deck is large, the game moves rapidly, often ending in just a few turns when a player 'knocks' or declares a stop.

games.name: Encaje
games.description: Encaje, also known as Mus Francés (French Mus), is a version of the Basque game Mus adapted for 3 or 5 players. Unlike standard Mus, Encaje is played without partnerships—each player competes individually. The unique twist is that there is no winner, only a loser; the goal is to avoid being the last player with stones remaining.

games.name: English Stud
games.description: English Stud is a 7-card stud variant where players have the unique option to exchange cards during the deal. Deal and play follow standard 7-card stud, but after each betting round (following the 5-card and 6-card streets), each player can optionally exchange one card for a new one. This card exchange feature distinguishes English Stud from traditional 7-card stud.

games.name: Escoba
games.description: Escoba (Spanish for 'Broom') is the Spanish variant of Scopa, a fishing-capture game. The defining mechanic: a player captures ALL cards from the table by playing a card that, combined with the table cards, sums to exactly 15. This 'sweep' (escoba) earns bonus points. Card values: A=1, 2-7=face value, J=8, Q=9, K=10. Targets: Most cards, Most Coins, 7 of Coins (Siete Bello), and sweeps.

games.name: Euchre
games.description: Euchre is the classic American partnership trick-taking game, played with a 24-32 card deck. Its hallmark feature is the 'Bower' system: the Jack of the called trump suit (Right Bower) and the Jack of the same-colored suit (Left Bower) are the two highest trump cards. Teams of two bid for the right to name trump and must win 3 of 5 tricks; failure results in being 'Euchred' and the opponent scoring 2 points. First team to 10 points wins.
games.deck: 24 cards (9, 10, J, Q, K, A in 4 suits)

games.name: Fan Tan (Sevens)
games.description: Fan Tan, also widely known as 'Sevens', 'Domino', or 'Parliament', is a classic layout-based card game where the objective is to be the first to get rid of all your cards. Players build upon a central layout of cards, starting with the Sevens and expanding outward to the Ace and Two in each suit. It is a game of both luck and light strategy, as players can choose to hold back key 'blocking' cards to prevent opponents from playing.

games.name: Fapfap
games.description: Fapfap, known as Agram in Niger and Mali, is a simple yet strategic last-trick-only game from West Africa. Players compete to win the final trick after five rounds of play, with the unusual twist that winning earlier tricks can be a disadvantage as it forces you to lead and cede control. A stripped 35-card deck is used, with unique ranking and the removal of the Ace of Spades.

games.name: Faro
games.description: Faro is an iconic 19th-century banking game immortalized in American frontier lore as the favorite of gamblers like Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday. Known colloquially as 'Bucking the Tiger' (from the tiger illustrations on dealing boxes), it is a game of pure chance where players wager on which card ranks will be drawn from a specially-designed dealing box. Unlike poker, Faro was prized for its transparency and relatively low house edge, allowing players to track all remaining cards using a public tool called a 'Case Keeper'.

games.name: Fast Track
games.description: Fast Track is a high-energy North American race game that combines card-driven movement with a physical board of marbles or pegs. Similar in spirit to Sorry! or Ludo, Fast Track replaces dice with each player's personal deck of cards. The goal is to navigate all four marbles around the track and into a central Home Base. The game features strategic mechanics like backwards-moving 4s, split 7s (move two marbles), and a dangerous central shortcut called the 'Fast Track' that saves board space but leaves marbles vulnerable.

games.name: Ferbli
games.description: Ferbli is a traditional Hungarian vying (betting) game that was extremely popular in the 19th a- early 20th centuries. It is closely related to Poker a- is played with a 32-card German-suited deck. The game involves multiple rou-s of betting where players can 'vye' (bet) or 'pass'. Ha- rankings are based on combinations of rank a- suit, with 'Four of a Ki-' a- the 'Ba-a' (four cards of the same suit) being the most sought-after ha-s. In rural Hungary a- Transylvania, it remains a cultural staple of café life.

games.name: Fifty-Five
games.description: Fifty-Five (55) is an advanced, bidding-based variation of the Irish national card game Twenty-Five. Deeply rooted in rural Irish tradition, it is a descendant of the ancient game 'Spoil Five'. The game is famous for its intricate and 'arcane' card rankingsâ€”where the Five of Trumps is always the highest card and the Ace of Hearts is a permanent trumpâ€”and its unique requirement that players bid for the right to choose the trump suit.

games.name: Fifty-one Chinese (Wǔshíyī Diǎn)
games.description: Fifty-one Chinese (Wǔshíyī diǎn / äº”å ä¸€ç‚¹) is a strategic collection game primarily played in the northern Fujian province of China. The game is centered around point-optimization within a single suit, where players attempt to assemble a hand of five cards of the same suit that totals as close to 51 points as possible. Unlike many Western card games, Fifty-one Chinese features a dynamic 'Table Exchange' mechanic where players can swap multiple cards at once with a public pool of facendup cards.

games.name: Fifty-one Japanese (Gojūichi)
games.description: Fifty-one Japanese (Gojūichi / äº”å ä¸€) is a popular fast-paced children's and social card game in Japan. A variation of the 'Commerce' family of games, it focuses on suit-based point collection. Players interact with a public pool of five cards on the table, swapping their own cards to reach a target score of 51. The game is known for its tension-filled ending, where one player can 'Stop' the game, giving everyone else only one last chance to improve their hand.

games.name: Fifty-Six (Ambathiyaaru)
games.description: Fifty-Six (56), known locally as 'Ambathiyaaru', is a complex and highly strategic trick-taking card game popular in the Kerala region of India. An expansion of the simpler game '28', it is played with a double deck of cards and a specialized point-count system from the Jass family. The game is known for its intense bidding phase and the use of 'tables' (physical cards from the unused portion of the deck) to keep track of match scores. It is a partnership game that demands precise card counting and team-wide tactical coordination.

games.name: FilicÄƒu
games.description: FilicÄƒu (also known as FilkÃ³ or FlÄƒcÄƒu) is a classic trick-taking partnership game from the Transylvania region of Romania. It belongs to the venerable Schafkopf family of games and is distinct for its use of a 32ndcard Germanndsuited 'William Tell' pack. The name 'FilicÄƒu' translates to 'unmarried boy,' a nickname given to the Over-Knaves which serve as the game's highest trumps. The game is highly aggressive, with a scoring system focused exclusively on capturing Aces and Tens to avoid the shameful status of 'Slaves'.

games.name: FilkÃ³
games.description: FilkÃ³ is a traditional Hungarian trick-taking game popular in the Great Plain (AlfÃ¶ld) region. Closely related to the Romanian FilicÄƒu, it is a variant of the Central European Schafkopf family. The game is played with a 32ndcard Germanndsuited deck and pits two teams against each other in a battle for 'Master' status. Beyond the card play, FilkÃ³ is known for its social 'punishment' rules, where the losers (Slaves) are tasked with dealing and other minor social forfeits until they can reclaim the title of Master.

games.name: Fipsen
games.description: Fipsen is a unique northern German trick-taking game, traditionally played in the coastal regions between Hamburg and Bremen. It belongs to the 'One vs. All' family of games, similar to Nap or Skat. Fipsen is distinguished by its highly specialized 25-card deckâ€”where the 7 of Diamonds (the 'Rute') is the only card of its suit allowedâ€”and its aggressive doubling mechanics. The game is a test of risk management, where players bid on the number of tricks they can win using a limited hand of just five cards.

games.name: Fish Pitch
games.description: Fish Pitch is a documented card game with defined setup, turn flow, and scoring conditions.

games.name: Five Card Draw
games.description: Five Card Draw is the quintessential variant of Poker and was for decades the most popular form of the game played in homes and Western films. Unlike community card games like Texas Hold 'em, Five Card Draw is a 'closed' game where all cards are held privately. The game features a unique 'Draw' phase where players can discard unwanted cards and replace them with new ones from the deck, allowing for sophisticated bluffing based on the number of cards drawn.

games.name: Five Card Draw (Deuces Wild)
games.description: Five Card Draw with all twos wild. Same deal and draw as standard; deuces substitute for any card. Best hand wins.
alsoKnownAs: Five Card Draw Deuces Wild Poker

games.name: Five Card Draw With a Bug
games.description: Five Card Draw with one Joker as Bug: counts as Ace or completes straight or flush only.
alsoKnownAs: Five Card Draw with a Bug Poker
5 Card Draw with a Bug Poker

games.name: Five Card Stud
games.description: Five Card Stud is one of the earliest forms of Stud Poker, emerging in the mid-19th century. Unlike Draw Poker, Five Card Stud is an 'open' game where most of a player's hand is visible to everyone at the table. Each player receives one hidden 'hole' card and four exposed 'up' cards, with betting rounds interspersed between each deal. This creates a high-tension environment where players must calculate their strength against the visible threats in their opponents' hands.

games.name: Five Card Stud High-Low
games.description: Five Card Stud with pot split between best high hand and best qualifying low hand.

games.name: Five Card Stud Lowball
games.description: Five Card Stud Lowball is a variant of Five Card Stud where the lowest hand wins instead of the highest. Played with the same dealing structure as standard Five Card Stud (one hole card, four up cards), it uses ace-to-five lowball ranking where straights and flushes do not count against the player. The best possible hand is A-2-3-4-5 (the 'wheel').

games.name: Five Hundred
games.description: Five Hundred is a trick-taking game for four players in fixed partnerships, invented in the USA in 1904 and now the national card game of Australia. Players bid 6-10 tricks; the high bidder takes a 3-card kitty, discards 3 cards, declares trump, and attempts to win their bid. Features unique bower mechanics (Joker and jacks of matching suit as top trumps) and No Trump / Misere contract options. First partnership to reach 500+ points wins.
games.origin: USA (1904), popularized in Australia & New Zealand

games.name: Five Up Dominoes
games.description: Domino game in the Fives family. All doubles are spinners. Score when layout pip total is a multiple of 5. Play to 61 points.
games.origin: United States (California and Southwestern US; popularized by Dominic C. Armanino)

games.name: Fives and Threes dominoes
games.description: Fives and Threes is a connecting domino game in which points are scored when the open ends of the layout add up to multiples of three or five. Popular in British pubs and in the British National Dominoes Championship; play is clockwise and the first player or team to reach exactly 61 wins.

games.name: Flower and Scorpion
games.description: Flower & Scorpion is an exotic variation of the domino game Bergen, traditionally associated with North African and Middle Eastern social circles. It combines standard domino-matching mechanics with the unpredictable element of dice rolling. Before each round, two pairs of dice are rolled to determine the 'Flower' (a lucky number that grants bonuses) and the 'Scorpion' (a cursed number that imposes penalties). Players act as members of a caravan, trying to match ends of the line (The Caravan) while navigating the hazards of the Scorpion's sting.
games.deck: Double-six Dominoes (28 tiles) + 2 sets of colored dice

games.name: Follow the Queen
games.description: Follow the Queen is one of the most unpredictable and chaotic variations of Seven Card Stud. While it follows the standard Stud structure, it introduces a roving wild card mechanic that can change mid-hand. The core rule is that Queens are wild, and the rank of the card dealt immediately after a Queen (the 'Trailer') also becomes wild. This creates massive hand rankings where Five-of-a-Kind is not just possible, but frequent, and the lead can shift dramatically with a single card deal.

games.name: Fool (Milton Bradley)
games.description: Fool is a classic card game published by Milton Bradley (MB Games) that combines shedding mechanics with bluffing and social deduction. Similar to 'Cheat' or 'I Doubt It', the objective is to discard all your cards by playing them face-down and declaring their rank. However, if another player suspects you are lying, they can shout 'Fool!'. It is a fast-paced game of deception, memory, and psychological warfare.

games.name: Football
games.description: Football is a high-action Poker variant based on Seven Card Stud, themed around American Football. It is characterized by its numerous wild cards and the 'extra boost' mechanics that mirror scoring in football. In this game, 3s and 6s are wild, and 2s give an extra card when dealt face-up. It is an extremely volatile game where hand rankings frequently reach Five-of-a-Kind, making it a staple of casual Dealer's Choice poker nights.

games.name: Fortress
games.description: Fortress is a challenging open-information Solitaire (Patience) game characterized by its unique building rules and lack of a draw pile. Unlike many other solitaires, Fortress allows players to build sequences both up and down within the tableau, provided they follow suit. All cards are dealt at the start; the top card of each column is available. Empty tableau spaces may be filled with any available card. It is often cited as a game of skill rather than luck, where planning several moves ahead is essential for victory.

games.name: Forty Thieves
games.description: Forty Thieves, also known as 'Napoleon at St. Helena' or 'Roosevelt at San Juan', is a notoriously difficult and strategic two-deck Solitaire game. Requiring 104 cards, the game challenges players to organize a vast tableau of 40 cards into eight separate foundations. Unlike many solitaires, building in the tableau must be done strictly by suit and in descending order. Because the stock can only be cycled through once, and only a single card is drawn at a time, players must exercise extreme caution to avoid blocking their own win path.

games.name: Forty-Five
games.description: Forty-Five (45s) is a traditional trick-taking game with Irish roots, most famously played in Ireland and Atlantic Canada (New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Newfoundland). A simplified descendant of 'Spoil Five', the game is known for its idiosyncratic card rankings, where the 5 of trumps is the ultimate card and the Ace of Hearts is permanently the third-highest trump regardless of the suit led. The name comes from the target score of 45 points, achieved across several rounds of five-trick hands.

games.name: Forty-One Exchange
games.description: Forty-One Exchange (often known simply as '41' in Southeast Asia and Indonesia) is a high-speed draw-and-discard game centered on set collection. Unlike most card games where high cards are balanced by low ones, every player in 41 is chasing the exact same perfection: a hand of four cards of the same suit that totals exactly 41 points. It is a game of probability and speed, where players must quickly pivot their strategy as the cards they need are snatched up by opponents.

games.name: Forty-One Syrian
games.description: Forty-One Syrian (also known as '400' or 'Arba'meyeh') is the preeminent partnership trick-taking game of Syria and Lebanon. It is a derivative of Whist that features a unique betting mechanics where Hearts are permanently the trump suit and players must reach a total of exactly 41 points (or 44 in some regions) to win. The game is famous for its '11-point threshold'â€”if the collective bids of all four players don't total at least 11, the hand is declared void and re-dealt, leading to intense tactical bidding and psychological bluffing.

games.name: Four Card Poker
games.description: Four Card Poker is a popular casino table game that pits the player against the house. Similar to Three Card Poker, it is a game of decision-making and hand valuation, but with a unique twist: the dealer receives a significant card advantage (six cards to the player's five) to offset the fact that the dealer does not need to 'qualify' to play. Despite the name, players and the dealer use their best four-card hand from their respective totals, leading to a unique ranking system where Three-of-a-Kind actually beats a Flush.

games.name: Four of a Kind
games.description: Four of a Kind is a unique pokerndstyle betting game, traditionally played as a 'dealer's choice' option in home poker games. Unlike standard poker where you build a hand through drawing or communal cards, players in this game are each assigned a unique starting rank and wait for the deck to provide the matching cards. It is a game of high tension and split pots, where victory is divided between the first person to complete their set of four and the person holding the mathematically lowest hand at that moment.

games.name: Freeze Out Dominoes
games.description: Freeze-Out Dominoes is a simple children's domino game similar to the card game War. Players arrange dominoes face-down in a line and reveal tiles in turn. The player whose tile matches one of the suits shown in a trick takes all revealed dominoes. It emphasizes chance over strategy, making it ideal for young players learning domino games.

games.name: French Dominoes
games.description: French Dominoes is a cut-throat domino game from the Caribbean (particularly Jamaica) featuring a distinctive cross-shaped tile layout. Played with a double-six domino set, it requires players to form a cross pattern with tiles before extending outward, combining careful strategy with luck. The game emphasizes blocking opponents while emptying one's own hand.

games.name: Fujian Mahjong
games.description: Fujian Mahjong refers to regional Mahjong play in China's Fujian province with local scoring conventions layered on top of standard draw-discard meld play. Games typically follow the familiar wall draw and discard-claim rhythm while using table profiles for what qualifies as a winning hand and how value is computed.

games.name: Gaigel
games.description: Gaigel is a traditional trick-taking game hailing from Swabia in Southwest Germany. Closely related to the game 'Sixty-Six' (Sechsundsechzig), Gaigel is played with a double-deck of 48 cards, typically featuring the distinct German-suited WÃ¼rttemberg pattern.
