It is primarily a partnership game where the goal is to reach 101 card points through captured tricks and 'marriages' (King and Ober pairs). The game is famous for its midndgame shift, where strict following-suit rules only apply once the draw pile (Talon) is exhausted.
games.deck: Gaigel/Binokel pack (48 cards: 2x A, 10, K, O, U, 7)

games.name: Galician Tarok
games.description: Galician Tarok is a three-player historical tarock game from the Galicia region. It uses a 42-card reduced tarock structure and combines talon exchange, contract pressure, and strict trick-taking obligations.

games.name: Gallinazo
games.description: Gallinazo is a distinct domino game played in Puerto Rico and parts of Mexico, characterized by its individual play format and unique penalty scoring system. While most domino games focus on partnership play, Gallinazo forces each of the four participants to hunt for themselves. The game is named after the 'vulture' (gallinazo), perhaps referring to the way players must 'prey' on others' mistakes to avoid being the one left holding highndvalue tiles. It is culturally synonymous with social stakes, where the cumulative loser is famously tasked with buying the next round of drinks for the table.

games.name: Gambari-Kan
games.description: Gambari-Kan is the three-player variant of Kan from Aomori. One player becomes the lone kankei (solo side) against two mukankei opponents and tries to capture enough point cards in trick play.

games.name: Game to Lose
games.description: Game to Lose is a three-player reverse trick-taking game from England's West Midlands. Players try to avoid taking valuable cards, because points are bad and the first player to 121 or more loses.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck with one 13-card dummy hand each deal

games.name: Game, Flip, Flop
games.description: Game, Flip, Flop is a high-stakes variation of the American Rummy game 'Tunk' (or Tonk). Originating in Dayton, Ohio, it is famous for its three distinct betting pots: 'Game', 'Flip', and 'Flop'. While the core gameplay follows standard Rummy melding rules, the 'Flip' and 'Flop' pots introduce a side-betting element based entirely on having the lowest cards of specific suits dealt in your initial hand. It is a fast-paced gambling game where players can win pots without even playing a card.

games.name: Gān Dèng Yǎn 干瞪眼
games.description: Gan Deng Yan is a Chinese climbing and shedding game in which most responses must be exactly one rank higher than the previous combination. Players begin with small hands, draw from a talon after each trick, and try to be first to shed all cards.

games.name: Gān Dèng Yǎn 干瞪眼
games.description: Gan Deng Yan is a Chinese climbing and shedding game in which most responses must be exactly one rank higher than the previous combination. Players begin with small hands, draw from a talon after each trick, and try to be first to shed all cards.

games.name: Gaple
games.description: Gaple is a popular Indonesian block domino game played on a single train line. Players add matching tiles at either end, and if blocked they either discard a dead tile or pass depending on table rules.

games.name: Gaps
games.description: Gaps is a single-player patience game in which four rows are arranged in suit sequence from 2 through King. Four gaps are created by removing the aces, and cards can move only into legal next-rank same-suit gaps.

games.name: Garrafina
games.description: Garrafina is a Spanish train domino game in which each player extends a personal train from a central starting double. Trains become open to opponents when their owner passes, creating a tactical open or private state on every branch.

games.name: Generala
games.description: Generala is a Cameroonian multi-player elimination card game played in tricks with a 54-card deck including two jokers. Players try to shed all cards; in each game the last player with cards is eliminated from the next game of the series.

games.name: German Solo
games.description: German Solo is a four-player trick-taking game from the Ombre family with contract bidding, temporary partnerships, and a fixed high-trump structure built around matadors.
games.deck: 32-card deck (A K Q J 10 9 8 7 in each suit)

games.name: German Whist
games.description: German Whist is a two-player trick-taking game with a stock phase and an end phase. Early tricks are used to draft better cards from stock; only the second 13 tricks determine the standard hand winner.

games.name: Getaway
games.description: Getaway is a Punjabi-origin shedding game in which players race to empty their hands while avoiding pickup penalties triggered by off-suit breaks (tochoo or thulla).

games.name: Gharat
games.description: Gharat is an Iranian fishing-loot game where players match ranks to steal cards from the central play pile or from the top of opponents' capture piles.

games.name: Giltspiel
games.description: Giltspiel is a four-player fixed-partnership trump trick game from Tyrol that combines five-trick play with open betting on three figures: Gleich (sets), Hanger (sequences), and Spiel (majority of tricks).

games.name: Gin Rummy
games.description: Gin Rummy is a two-player knock-rummy game where players draw and discard to build sets and runs, then end a hand by knocking with low deadwood or going gin with no deadwood.

games.name: Ging
games.description: Ging, also called Seven Cards, is a 17th-century English declaration gambling game for four players using a 28-card stripped pack, where players claim counters for most suit points or sweeping special combinations.
games.deck: Custom 28-card pack (K Q J 10 9 8 7 in each suit)

games.name: Giog
games.description: Giog is a Malaysian multi-trick game played with Xiangqi pieces used like hidden cards, where players lead valid single or multi-piece combinations and capture tricks with the highest combination of the led type.
games.origin: Malaysia and Southeast Asian Chinese communities

games.name: Gleek
games.description: Gleek is a historical English three-player vying and trick-taking game played with a 44-card deck, combining stock bidding, ruff betting, declaration of sets, and 12-trick play.

games.name: Gnav
games.description: Gnav is a Scandinavian elimination game from the Cuckoo family. Each round players hold one hidden piece, may stand or try to swap left, and try to avoid finishing with the lowest value.
games.deck: Custom 42-piece Gnav pack (two of each rank/special piece)

games.name: Go Fish
games.description: Go Fish is a classic set-collection game where players ask opponents for ranks they already hold, then draw from stock on failure, aiming to complete the most four-of-a-kind books.

games.name: Go Stop
games.description: Go Stop is a Korean flower-card fishing game in which players capture matching month cards, build scoring combinations, and choose whether to stop for payout or go on for higher risk and reward.
games.deck: Hanafuda/Hwatu 48-card flower deck, often with optional jokers by table rule

games.name: Goita
games.description: Goita is a four-player Japanese partnership shedding game from Noto in which players answer an attack tile with a matching tile (or king wildcard) and then issue a new attack.
games.deck: 32-tile Goita set based on shogi piece types (two kings, two rooks, two bishops, four golds, four silvers, four knights, four lances, ten pawns)

games.name: Golden Ten
games.description: Golden Ten is a reverse trick-taking game using a 56-card Rook deck: players avoid red-card penalties while trying to capture the yellow ten bonus card.

games.name: Golf
games.description: Golf is a card game for two or more players where the object is to score as little as possible, like the sport. Each player has a layout of face-down cards that can be replaced by drawing from stock or discard piles. The game is commonly played over 9 or 18 deals ('holes'), with the lowest total score winning. Also known as Polish Polka, Polish Poker, Turtle (4-card), Hara Kiri (6-card), or Crazy Nines (9-card).

games.name: Golf (Eight Card)
games.description: Eight-card Golf: 2+ players, 52 cards. Each has 8 cards in layout (e.g. 2Ã—4). Draw or take discard to replace; aim for lowest point total. Same scoring as 4/6-card Golf; larger layout. Play 9 or 18 holes.

games.name: Golf (Four Card)
games.description: Four-card Golf: 2+ players, 52 cards. Each has 4 cards in a square, two visible once. Draw or take discard to replace; knock to end hand. Lowest score wins. Also Turtle, Polish Poker Four Card.

games.name: Golf (Nine Card)
games.description: Nine-Card Golf is a draw-and-discard shedding game played with a 3Ã—3 grid layout where players strategically replace cards to minimize their total score. A unique feature is the ability to score zero by collecting three cards of equal rank in a vertical column, adding a distinctive puzzle element to the Golf family.
games.deck: One or two standard 52-card decks (depending on player count)

games.name: Golf (Six Card)
games.description: Six-Card Golf is a matching game where players try to earn the lowest score over nine holes (rounds). Each player manages a six-card layout arranged in a 2x3 grid, replacing high cards with lower ones drawn from the stock or discard pile. The game's unique strategy involves balancing point reduction with the need to match cards in columns to nullify their scores.

games.name: Gong Zhu
games.description: Gong Zhu (æ‹±çŒª - 'Chase the Pig' or 'Dig Out the Pig') is an enhanced Chinese version of Hearts. Penalty cards can be exposed before play to double (or quadruple) their effects. Features special roles for the Jack of Diamonds (sheep) and Ten of Clubs (transformer). Popular among Chinese Weiqi (Go) players between tournament games.

games.name: Gonin-Kan
games.description: Gonin-Kan (äº”äººã‚«ãƒ³ - 'Five People Kan') is the most popular variation of Kan, a Japanese trick-taking game from Aomori prefecture. Played by 5-6 players using a 50-card deck (standard 52 minus three 2s plus joker). Features unique partnership formation each round based on joker and trump ace holders, with the kankei (partners) against the mukankei (non-partners).

games.name: GOPS
games.description: GOPS (short for 'Game of Pure Strategy'), also known as Goofspiel, is a celebrated card game in game theory and mathematics. It is a symmetrical contest where luck is almost entirely eliminated, as both players begin with identical sets of cards and are presented with the same sequence of 'prizes' to bid on. The game is a test of psychological reading and resource management, as players must decide which prizes are worth their highest 'bidding' cards and when to concede a small loss to save strength for a future win.

games.name: Gou Ji (Gao Ji)
games.description: Gou Ji (often transliterated as Gao Ji) is a massive, chaotic, and highly strategic climbing card game from Shandong Province, China. It is famous for using four full decks of cards mixed together (216 cards total) and is played by six players divided into two teams of three. The name 'Gou Ji' means 'Enough Level' or 'Sufficient Rank', referring to the special high-ranking combinations that trigger 'Duels' between opposing players. It is a game of chaotic bursts of action, intricate teamwork, and psychological warfare.

games.name: Gou Ji 够级
games.description: GÃ²u JÃ­ å¤Ÿçº§ is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Guadalupe
games.description: Guadalupe is a manipulation rummy game where players can reorganize existing melds on the table to form new combinations. Players draw 1-2 cards and must meld, or draw 3 cards without melding. Part of the Carousel/Machiavelli family of rummy games where table cards can be rearranged.

games.name: Guan Dan
games.description: Guan Dan (æŽ¼è›‹), also known as 'Throwing Eggs', is a popular Chinese climbing card game for four players in fixed partnerships. Teams advance through levels (2 through Ace) by winning hands. The game features unique mechanics including level cards, wild cards (hearts of the current level), and powerful bomb combinations. Originated in Huaian, Jiangsu Province.

games.name: Guan Dan 押蛋
games.description: GuÃ n DÃ n æŽ¼è›‹ is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Guiñote
games.description: Guiñote is a Tute variant for 2 to 4 players from Aragón, Navarra and Castilla. It uses the same 40-card Spanish deck and point-trick structure as Tute, but the jack and horse swap rank and point values; singing (cantes) uses king and jack; multiple 20s or 40s may be sung after a trick; and the winner of the last trick deals next.

games.name: Guo Wu Guan (過五關)
games.description: Guo Wu Guan (過五關), meaning 'Passing Five Levels', is a Chinese domino solitaire game played with a standard set of 32 Chinese dominoes. The name alludes to the phrase 'Pass five levels and cut six generals' from the Three Kingdoms novel, featuring Guan Yu. Players must strategically remove valid triplets of tiles to clear five levels and defeat six generals.

games.name: Guts
games.description: Guts is a high-stakes poker variant known for its rapidly escalating pots and simple 'in or out' decision-making. Players receive 2-3 cards and simultaneously declare whether they're 'in' (competing for the pot) or 'out' (folding). Losers must match the entire pot, causing explosive pot growth. The name refers to the bravery required to risk large sums.

games.name: Hachi-Hachi (八八)
games.description: Hachi-Hachi (八八, '88') is the most representative Japanese Hanafuda fishing game. The name refers to the par score of 88 points (one-third of the 264 total points in the deck). Played by 3-6 players with a bidding phase to determine the three active players each round. Features complex scoring with teyaku (initial hand combinations) and deki-yaku (combinations formed during play). Players can stop early if they form valuable combinations.

games.name: Haitian Dominoes
games.description: Haitian Dominoes is a 4-player partnership domino game using a double-six set. Teams race to build a 4-point streak where losing a round resets the loser score to zero.

games.name: Hana-Awase
games.description: Hana-Awase is a traditional Japanese hanafuda matching game where players capture month-matching cards and score combinations from collected sets.

games.name: Hanafuda (花札)
games.description: Hanafuda (花札, 'flower cards') are traditional Japanese playing cards comprising a 48-card deck divided into 12 suits, each representing a month and featuring a specific flower or plant. Hanafuda is not a single game but a family of games, most commonly fishing/capture games where players match cards from their hand with cards on the field. Popular games include Koi-Koi, Hachi-Hachi, and Hana-Awase. Cards are categorized as Brights, Animals, Ribbons, and Plains, with varying point values.

games.name: Hand and Foot
games.description: Hand and Foot is a popular Canasta-style rummy game typically played by four players in partnerships. Each player receives two sets of cards: a 'hand' (played first) and a 'foot' (played after the hand is depleted). The objective is to form melds and canastas (7-card melds) while managing special cards like Red Threes (bonus) and Black Threes (penalty). Features 'books' (clean and dirty canastas), minimum meld requirements that increase each round, and strategic decisions about when to go out.

games.name: Handjass
games.description: Handjass, also known as Sackjass or Butzer, is considered the most basic and fundamental form of Jass, the national card game of Switzerland. It is a trick-taking game where players compete to reach a target score (usually represented by strokes on a slate) while avoiding the 'null' (potato) - a penalty for failing to reach a minimum point threshold in a hand.
games.deck: 36-card Swiss Jass deck (Roses, Bells, Acorns, Shields)

games.name: Happy Families
games.description: Happy Families is a traditional British matching game, famously illustrated by John Tenniel. It is a progenitor to games like Go Fish and Authors. Players attempt to collect complete sets (families) of four characters by asking opponents for specific cards. If successful, they continue their turn; if not, the turn passes to the person asked.

games.name: Harbin Mahjong
games.description: Harbin Mahjong is a regional Mahjong variant associated with Harbin and wider northeast China play. It follows the standard Mahjong draw-discard loop with meld claims and a complete-hand win condition, while using local table conventions for what hands qualify and how points are assessed.

games.name: Have a Heart
games.description: Have a Heart is a classic trick-taking game from the Hearts family. Unlike most trick-taking games, the goal is to avoid winning certain cards. Hearts and the Queen of Spades carry penalty points. It is a game of evasion and strategic passing, requiring players to carefully manage their hand to avoid 'bleeding' points.

games.name: Hazari
games.description: Hazari (meaning 'One Thousand') is a highly strategic partitioning game popular in Bangladesh and Bhutan. Players receive 13 cards and must divide them into four sets (composed of 3, 3, 3, and 4 cards). These sets are then compared against opponents' sets in a fixed order. The game combines the hand-ranking logic of Brag and Teen Patti with a unique structural challenge and a long-term scoring goal of 1000 points.

games.name: Hearts
games.description: Hearts is a classic trick-taking card game belonging to the 'evasion' family. Unlike most trick-taking games, the goal is to avoid winning tricks that contain penalty cards. Each heart is 1 penalty point, and the Queen of Spades is 13. The ultimate objective is to have the lowest score, or to 'Shoot the Moon' by taking all penalty cards.

games.name: Hidden Rung
games.description: Hidden Rung (or Hidden Trump) is a popular South Asian trick-taking game, part of the Court Piece (Rang) family. It is played by four players in two fixed partnerships. The game is unique for its 'hidden' trump mechanic: the trump suit is determined by a card selected from the caller's first five cards and placed face-down, remaining unknown until a player is first unable to follow suit.

games.name: High Card Flush
games.description: High Card Flush is a popular casino table game that focuses exclusively on flushes. Unlike standard poker, straights, pairs, and other hands do not matter. The goal is simply to have more cards of the same suit in a seven-card hand than the dealer. It combines simplicity with high-payout bonus bets.

games.name: High Card Pool
games.description: High Card Pool, often called Red Dog or Slippery Sam, is a fast-paced banking game where players bet on whether a card dealt after their initial hand will match a suit in their hand and have a higher rank. It is a game of probability and betting psychology, common in both casual social settings and older casino environments.

games.name: High Fives Dominoes
games.description: High Fives Dominoes is a western domino connecting game played with a double-15 set, using the extended value range to create longer sessions and more complex end control. Players match open ends while managing mobility and high-value risk, since high numbers can amplify blocking and pip exposure outcomes.

games.name: High-Low Split Poker
games.description: High-Low Split is a fundamental poker pot-splitting mechanic rather than a standalone game. It is commonly applied to variants like Omaha and Seven Card Stud. In these games, the pot is divided into two halves: one for the best 'high' hand and one for the best qualifying 'low' hand (usually 8-or-better).

games.name: Hikikabu
games.description: Hikikabu is a traditional Japanese kabufuda gambling-card game played with the 40-card Kabufuda family, emphasizing value totals and betting decisions.

games.name: Hindersche
games.description: Hindersche (meaning 'Backwards') is a rare and traditional reverse trick-taking game played exclusively in the central Black Forest of Germany. It is an Ace-Ten game where the objective is to *avoid* taking tricks containing card points. It is noted for its antiquity, using a 36-card pack and being played anticlockwise.

games.name: Hockey
games.description: Hockey is an ingenious Canadian card game that simulates the flow of an ice hockey match. It is a 'fishing' game where two players attempt to capture cards from a central pile by matching their ranks. The game is known for its thematic terminology, including 'breakaways', 'saves', and 'goals'.

games.name: Hokm
games.description: Hokm (meaning 'Command' or 'Order') is Iran's most popular trick-taking card game. A partnership game for 4 players where the Hâkem (Ruler) declares trump after seeing only 5 cards. Teams compete to win 7 tricks per hand and 7 points to win the match. Play proceeds anticlockwise.

games.name: Hol's der Geier
games.description: Hol's der Geier (Beat the Buzzard) is a quick-fire tactical bidding game designed by the legendary Alex Randolph. Players compete to capture 'Mouse' cards (positive points) while avoiding 'Vulture' cards (negative points). It is famous for its simple ruleset that yields surprisingly deep psychological gameplay and second-guessing.
games.deck: 75 Playing cards (5 sets of 1-15), 15 Prize cards

games.name: Hola
games.description: Hola (meaning 'Nakedness' or 'Naked') is a unique Slavic trick-taking game popular among Ukrainian-Canadians and in parts of Eastern Europe. It stands out from standard Whist-like games because a trick can only be won by playing a card of the SAME rank as the lead, or by playing a wild card (7s and 2s). It shares ancestors with the Czech game Sedma.

games.name: Hollywood Garbage
games.description: Hollywood Garbage (also known as Junk Poker or Garbage) is a multi-phase social gambling game played with a massive deck (often 2-3 standard decks). It combines elements of Poker, Bingo, and simple card-matching. It is designed for large groups and operates through a sequence of phases that slowly deplete a shared pot of coins or chips.
games.deck: 2 standard 52-card decks (4-5 players); 3 or more decks (6+ players), shuffled together

games.name: Hollywood Gin
games.description: Hollywood Gin is a popular scoring variation of Gin Rummy. Instead of playing a single game, players record scores for three separate games simultaneously on a single score sheet. This format increases the strategic depth and the excitement of a match by allowing a single win to contribute to multiple game totals.

games.name: Honest John
games.description: Honest John (or Stormy Castle) is a traditional pub domino game played primarily in Lancashire, England. Unlike the standard 'line' layout of dominoes, each player builds their own line radiating from a central starting double to form a 'star' shape. The game includes a unique economic mechanic where players buy needed tiles from their opponents.

games.name: Hong Kong Mahjong
games.description: Hong Kong Mahjong is a four-player Cantonese Mahjong variant that emphasizes practical hand building and fan-based scoring. The game uses the standard Mahjong tile set and straightforward meld structure, making it one of the most widely taught regional forms.

games.name: Hoola
games.description: Hoola (or Hulla) is a popular Korean rummy game related to the Japanese game Seven Bridge. It is a fast-paced game of sets and runs, where the goal is to empty your hand. It features unique mechanics like 'Blasts' (winning with specific sevens) and 'Knocking' (claiming a win when your point total is low).

games.name: Hornafjarðarmanni
games.description: Hornafjarðarmanni is a regional Icelandic trick-taking game, a variant of the broader 'Manni' family. It is distinctively played in the Hornafjörður region of south-east Iceland. It is a three-player game using a full deck and features a unique 'Manni' (Man) - a set of face-down cards that players can exchange with their hands to optimize their play.

games.name: HORSE
games.description: HORSE is a mixed poker game format that rotates through five different poker variants in a fixed sequence. The acronym stands for Hold'em, Omaha Hi/Lo, Razz, Seven Card Stud, and Eight-or-Better (Stud Hi/Lo). Popular in major tournaments like the World Series of Poker, HORSE tests a player's versatility across multiple poker disciplines. All games are played in Fixed-Limit format.
games.duration: Variable (rotates games every round or time period)

games.name: Hosa Aba
games.description: Hosa Aba (meaning 'Trousers Down') is the Swiss-German variant of the popular European banking game 'Schwimmen' or '31'. It is a fast-paced game of card swapping where players aim to collect cards of a single suit totaling 31 points (Hosa Aba). It is traditionally played with Swiss-German suited cards in the German-speaking cantons of Switzerland.

games.name: HOSE
games.description: HOSE is a mixed poker format: four games in fixed rotation — Hold'em, Omaha (or Omaha/8), Seven-Card Stud, and Eight or Better (Stud High-Low). Played as limit; shared-card games use blinds, stud games use antes and a bring-in. USA; used in tournaments and mixed games.

games.name: Hou Zi Ba Pi
games.description: Hou Zi Ba Pi (猴子扒皮 - literally 'Monkey Stripping the Skin') is an aggressive Chinese shedding game, often considered a variant of Big Two (Choi Dai Di). It is known for its fast-paced nature and the use of the term 'Monkey' as slang for specific high cards or the act of stripping an opponent's hand of its high cards.
alsoKnownAs: Hou Zi variant of Big Two

games.name: House of Cards
games.description: House of Cards is a dual-purpose term. While it commonly refers to the physical act of building towers with playing cards, it is also a specific, traditional drawing and building game. In its game form, players compete to build virtual 'rooms' and 'stories' by matching colors and ranks to score points based on triangle formations.

games.name: Hoyle
games.description: While 'Hoyle' is best known as an authority on rules, the name is specifically synonymous with 'English Whist' - the game Edmond Hoyle first standardized. English Whist is a classic trick-taking game for four players and the direct ancestor of modern Bridge. It emphasizes memory, partnership communication, and tactical trump management.

games.name: Humbug
games.description: Humbug is a minimalist 18th-century trick-taking game for two players, representing the simplest possible adaptation of Whist. It is unique because both players are dealt the entire deck, making it a game of perfect information (after the initial overview) and a rigorous test of memory and card counting.

games.name: Hundred and Ten
games.description: Hundred and Ten (110) is the bidding version of the Irish national game 'Twenty-Five' (Spoil Five). It is a strategic trick-taking game where players bid to score up to 110 points in a single deal. It is known for its peculiar card rankings (where red and black suits rank differently) and its aggressive bidding system.

games.name: Hungarian DominÃ³ (Block)
games.description: Hungarian DominÃ³ (Block Game) is a strategic domino variant played with a Double-Six set. It is a 'block' game, meaning there is no drawing from a boneyard once play begins. Players must use the tiles in their hand to build a single linear chain, emphasizing hand management and blocking strategies to force opponents into passing their turns.

games.name: Hungarian DominÃ³ (Draw)
games.description: Hungarian DominÃ³ (Draw Game) is the more flexible counterpart to the Block variant. It introduces a 'Boneyard' (stock) of face-down tiles. If a player cannot make a legal move from their hand, they must draw from the stock until a playable tile is found. This variant typically leads to larger hands and more dynamic layout changes.

games.name: Hungarian Tarokk
games.description: Hungarian Tarokk (specifically 'Illustrated Tarokk' or 'XX-Hívás Tarokk') is the most popular form of the Tarot family in Hungary. It is a four-player partnership game using the 42-card Austrian/Hungarian Tarot pack. It is highly regarded for its sophisticated system of 'cue-bids' and its unique method of choosing partners by 'calling the XX' (the 20th trump).

games.name: Hunter
games.description: Hunter (or Young Hunter, German: JÃ¤ger) is a specialized German trick-taking game for four players. The game revolves entirely around the Jacks (the 'Youngs'), who act as both the 'Hunters' and the 'Prey'. Scoring is achieved not by winning tricks generally, but specifically by capturing or 'hitting' Jacks within tricks.

games.name: Hurrikan
games.description: Hurrikan (Hurricane) is a German fishing card game closely related to the Italian classic 'Scopa' and its Spanish cousin 'Escoba'. Players capture cards from a central layout by matching values from their hand. The game is named for the 'Hurrikan' move (a 'Sweep'), where a player captures all cards from the table in a single turn.

games.name: Husarln
games.description: Husarln is a three-player Austrian tarock game linked to the Illustrated Tarock branch. It is played with a 42-card reduced tarock pack and puts heavy pressure on trump distribution and tactical contract play.
games.deck: 42-card Industrie und Glueck tarock deck variant

games.name: Húszashívásos Tarokk
games.description: Húszashívásos Tarokk is a Hungarian Tarokk variant featuring a unique bidding system where players bid to win 20 or more tricks. It is a point-trick game with a 42-card Tarot deck, featuring complex bidding and partnership dynamics.

games.name: Húszashívásos Tarokk
games.description: Húszashívásos Tarokk ('Call Twenty Tarot') is Hungary's national card game. 4 players. 42-card Tarot deck (from 54-card Austrian Tarock). Skíz(XXII)=highest, 22 trumps + suit cards. Declarer calls Trump XX to find secret partner. Talon exchange. Need 48+ of 94 card points. Bonuses for Trull, Pagát ultimo, Volát.

games.name: Huutopussi
games.description: Huutopussi (Finnish for 'Bidding Bag') is a prestigious Finnish trick-taking game for four players in partnerships. It is an evolution of 'Marjapussi', adding a complex bidding phase where partnerships compete for the right to exchange cards and set the contract. It is famous for its 'Marriage' system, where declaring a King-Queen pair of the same suit establishes the trump and awards points.

games.name: Hwatu (Go-Stop)
games.description: Hwatu (í™”íˆ¬ - Flower Cards) refers to the 48-card Korean deck and the various 'fishing' games played with it, most notably Go-Stop (ê³ ìŠ¤í†±). It is a game of high tension and strategic risk-taking where players capture floral cards representing the 12 months to form specific combinations (Jokbo). The game is famous for the 'Go' or 'Stop' decision, where a winning player can choose to risk their points to double them or stop immediately to secure victory.

games.name: Hyakunin Isshu
games.description: Hyakunin Isshu (ç™¾äººä¸€é¦– - 'One Hundred People, One Poem Each') is a traditional Japanese card game based on a classical anthology of waka poems. It is played as a competitive game called 'Karuta'. Players must match a poem being read aloud with the correct 'grabbing' card spread out on the floor. It is a game of extreme speed, memory, and auditory processing.
games.deck: 200 cards (100 'Yomi-fuda' or Reading cards, 100 'Torifuda' or Grabbing cards)

games.name: Idiots
games.description: Idiots (better known as Shithead, Palace, or Karma) is a widespread shedding-type card game. The goal is to avoid being the last player with cards, as that person is declared the 'Idiot' (Shithead). It features a unique three-layered hand structure and several 'magic' cards that can reset, skip, or burn the discard pile.

games.name: Illustrated Tarokk
games.description: Illustrated Tarokk (Illusztrált Tarokk) is the most complex and rewarding variant of Hungarian Tarokk. While based on the 42-card 'Twenty-Calling' (Paskievics) version, it adds a massive layer of additional bonuses (Figurák) that make it a game of high-stakes declarations and daring tactical plays. In this variant, winning the basic game is often secondary to fulfilling high-value bonus contracts like 'Huszonegyfogás' (Catching the XXI).

games.name: In Between
games.description: In Between is a banking gambling game where a player bets that a third card will rank strictly between two initial cards.

games.name: Indian Poker
games.description: Indian Poker (also known as Blind Man's Bluff) is a unique poker variant where each player holds their card(s) against their forehead facing outward, so they can see all opponents' cards but not their own. Players bet based on what they see others holding, creating a game of deduction and reverse psychology.

games.name: Indian Rummy
games.description: Indian Rummy (also known as Paplu) is a popular variant of rummy played throughout India. It is a draw-and-discard game where players aim to form valid sets and sequences from 13 cards. The game requires at least two sequences, one of which must be a pure sequence (without jokers).

games.name: Indonesian Baccarat
games.description: Indonesian Baccarat (locally known as Bakarat) refers to the standard European Baccarat game as played and adapted in Indonesian card rooms and social gambling circles. It is a game of pure chance where players bet on the 'Player' or 'Banker' hands to reach a total closest to nine.

games.name: Indonesian Poker
games.description: Indonesian Poker (properly known as Capsa Susun or 'Chinese Poker') is a strategic card game where players are dealt 13 cards and must arrange them into three separate poker hands. It is extremely popular across Indonesia and Southeast Asia, combining the luck of the draw with the skill of optimal hand partitioning.

games.name: Indonesian Rummy
games.description: Remi Indonesia (or simply Remi) is a popular Indonesian distillation of classic Rummy. It is a draw-and-discard game for 2 to 4 players, emphasizing the creation of sets (three of a kind) and runs (sequences). It features a unique scoring system involving negative points for 'dead' cards and bonuses for ending the game with a 'Remi' (dumping the entire hand).

games.name: Ino-Shika-Cho
games.description: Ino-Shika-Cho (猪鹿蝶 - Boar, Deer, Butterfly) is the most iconic scoring combination ('Yaku') in the Japanese Hanafuda game Koi-Koi. It has also evolved into its own simplified sub-game played with Hanafuda cards, where players focus specifically on gathering these three 'Tane' (animal/object) cards to win the round.

games.name: Irish Don (Nine-card)
games.description: Irish Don (specifically the Nine-card variant) is a popular Irish partnership trick-taking game. It is a point-trick game where specific cards (5s, 9s, Aces, etc.) have high values. It is unique for its 'Pitching' start, where the first card led sets the trump suit, and the rules prohibiting certain partners from seeing their cards until the game begins to prevent signaling.

games.name: Irish Poker
games.description: Irish Poker is a high-energy, four-stage social drinking/betting game based on predictive card guessing. It is famous for its simple but escalating mechanics: Red or Black, Higher or Lower, Inside or Outside, and Suit. While it shares a name with Poker, it is a game of probability and penalty rather than hand rankings.

games.name: Iroha Karuta
games.description: Iroha Karuta is a traditional Japanese matching and proverb-capture game using paired reading and picture cards in the karuta tradition.

games.name: Iron Cross Poker
games.description: Iron Cross (also known as Criss-Cross or Church Poker) is a popular community-card poker variant played in 'dealer's choice' games. Five community cards are arranged in a cross pattern on the table. Each player receives two hole cards and must form the best five-card hand by combining their cards with either the vertical or horizontal line of the cross.

games.name: Italian Dominoes
games.description: Adding game with double-6 dominoes: each turn you draw from the boneyard or play a tile to the tableau, announcing the cumulative pip total. Score when the total hits exactly 30, 50, 70, or 100; first to reach or pass 50 points wins.
games.origin: Uncertain; documented in German domino books and US magazine.

games.name: Italian Poker
games.description: Poker all'italiana is a draw poker variant played with a short deck (32, 36 or 40 cards by player count). It has optional blind opening (buio), two betting rounds with a draw in between, and a non-standard hand ranking where flush beats full house and straight flushes have min-medium-max tie rules.
games.deck: Short deck: 32 cards (7 to Ace) for 4 players, 36 (6 to Ace) for 5, 40 (5 to Ace) for 6, from a standard 52-card pack.

games.name: Jacks Back (5 Card Draw)
games.description: Jacks Back: Five Card Draw with Jacks or Better to open. If no one opens, the same hand is kept and played as ace-to-five lowball, so fewer deals are thrown in. Suited to three to five players.

games.name: Jacks or Better (5 Card Draw)
games.description: Jacks or Better: Five Card Draw. You may only open betting with at least a pair of Jacks. Prevents blind opening.

games.name: Jamaican Dominoes
games.description: Jamaican dominoes: Caribbean draw game. Four players; partner or cut-throat (no partner). Double-six.

games.name: James Bond (Card Game)
games.description: James Bond is a high-speed, frantic card game that tests memory and reaction time. Unlike turn-based games, everyone plays simultaneously. Each player manages several 'books' (piles) of cards, racing to turn each book into a set of four-of-a-kind by swapping cards with a shared central pool. The first player to complete all their sets and shout 'James Bond!' wins.

games.name: Jass (Schieber)
games.description: Jass is the national card game of Switzerland, specifically the 'Schieber' variant, which is a four-player partnership trick-taking game. It features a unique 36-card deck (Acorns, Bells, Shields, Flowers) and a complex point-tracking system. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to deduce their partner's strength through 'pushing' the trump selection and careful card signaling.

games.name: Jeu de Carte Sipa
games.description: Jeu de Carte Sipa (or simply Sipa) is a popular trick-taking game in Togo and across West Africa. It is a variant of the regional game 'Spar'. The game is fast-paced and revolves around the critical importance of the final trick. The ultimate goal is to win the last trick(s), specifically with a 7, which provides significantly higher points.

games.name: Jhyap
games.description: Jhyap (also known as Yaniv or Dhumbal) is a draw-and-discard game from Nepal that has gained international popularity. Players aim to have the lowest total card value in their hand by forming sets and runs that can be discarded. When a player thinks they have the lowest hand, they call 'Jhyap' to end the round.

games.name: Jhyap Yaniv
games.description: Jhyap Yaniv (also known as Dhumbal in Nepal and Yaniv in Israel) is a unique draw-and-discard game. Unlike standard Rummy, the goal is to reduce your hand's point total to a minimum (typically 5 or 7) and then call 'Jhyap' (or 'Yaniv') to end the round. If another player has an equal or lower total, the caller is penalized, creating a tense game of memory and risk management.

games.name: Jie Long
games.description: Jie Long (接龙, connect dragon) is a Chinese domino connecting game. Players extend a single open end by playing a matching tile or discarding one face down. The player with fewest pips on discarded tiles wins; pairs settle by pip difference.
games.deck: 32 Chinese dominoes (11 civil tiles twice, 10 military tiles once; no blanks).

games.name: Jjak-mat-chu-gi
games.description: Jjak-mat-chu-gi (짝맞추기 - 'Making Pairs') is a traditional Korean domino game played with Gol-pae (bone tiles). Unlike Western dominoes where players match end-to-end, this is a 'pair-making' game where the objective is to form specific combinations (Civil and Military pairs). It is a draw-and-discard game similar in structure to Rummy but played with tiles.

games.name: Jo-Jotte
games.description: Jo-Jotte is a two-player trick-taking and melding game created by bridge expert Ely Culbertson in 1937. It is a sophisticated hybrid that combines the bidding and scoring philosophies of Contract Bridge with the card-ranking and melding mechanics of Belote and Klaberjass. Named after his wife Josephine, it was marketed as the ultimate two-player intellectual card game.

games.name: Joffre
games.description: Joffre is a traditional QuÃ©bÃ©cois trick-taking game played in the Bellechasse region of Canada. A relative of the Saskatchewan game 'Kaiser', it features a 32-card deck and two highly significant cards: the 'Joffre' (5 of Hearts, scoring +5) and the 'Kaiser' (3 of Spades, scoring -3). It is a game of high variance where one bad trick can lose the round.

games.name: Joker (Exit Game)
games.description: Joker is a competitive 'exit' game popular in Bulgaria, Israel, and Central Europe. It is similar to games like 'Scum' or 'Durak' but with a unique twist: the Joker acts as a 'cursed' card. The goal is to get rid of your cards and exit the game. However, holding the Joker prevents you from exiting, meaning you must pass it to an opponent before you can win.

games.name: Joker Karo
games.description: Joker Karo (also known as Jokern or German Rummy) is a popular Central European variant of RommÃ©. It is distinguished by its frequent use of Jokers (up to 6) and the specific rules regarding the 'Joker-Exchange', where a player can replace a melded Joker on the table with the real card from their hand. It is a game of high sequences and strategic meld-building.

games.name: Jū mǎ pāo 車馬包
games.description: Jū mǎ pāo 車馬包 is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Jū mǎ pāo 車馬包
games.description: Jū mǎ pāo (Chariot Horse Cannon) is a traditional Chinese matching and trick-taking game that uniquely utilizes the 32 pieces of a Chinese Chess (Xiangqi) set as cards. Played by 3 or 4 players, players treat the chess discs as a deck, shuffling them face-down and forming stacks. It is a game of memory, piece-value calculation, and specific combination-based captures.

games.name: Jukha
games.description: Jukha is a high-speed Israeli-Bulgarian 'hot potato' game where players compete to empty their hands by matching cards while avoiding (or passing) the unique Joker. It is a game of reflexes and nerve, as the Joker acts as a barrier to victory. It is almost identical in mechanics to the Bulgarian 'Joker' game but with specific variations in the 'Final Duel'.

games.name: Juse
games.description: Juse is a unique and high-intensity 'competitive patience' game from Sri Lanka. Unlike traditional solitaire, several players compete in real-time to build piles in the center and on each other's discard piles. It is a game of rapid pattern recognition where failure to play a 'forced' card results in a penalty (Juse!), making it a chaotic and energetic social experience.

games.name: K'ap Shap
games.description: K'ap Shap is a two-player draw-and-discard game played with Chinese dominoes. The aim is to complete a hand with one identical pair (ngán) and three pairs of tiles whose spots add up to 10 or 20 (counting the 4-2 tile as 3 spots). It is a variant of K'ap Tái Shap, documented by Culin (1895) as played in Chinese gambling houses in the USA.

games.name: K'ap Shap
games.description: K'ap Shap (also known as 'Collecting Tens' or 'Ten-Step') is a traditional Chinese rummy-style game played with Chinese dominoes. The name translates to 'to complete tens,' reflecting the core mechanic: forming pairs that sum to 10 or 20. It is a fast-paced game of matching and drawing, often played as a fast-turnaround gambling game in social clubs.
games.deck: One or more sets of Chinese Dominoes (32 tiles per set)

games.name: K'ap Tái Shap
games.description: K'ap Tái Shap (Big Collecting Tens) is an expanded version of K'ap Shap, designed for larger groups (up to 20 players) and utilizing multiple sets of Chinese dominoes (up to 8 sets). It is a high-stakes, fast-paced game where the goal is to form a specific combination of identical pairs and 10/20-sum pairs. The use of multiple sets introduces high duplication, changing the strategy from simple matching to probability-based hoarding.

games.name: Kaiser
games.description: Kaiser is a beloved Canadian trick-taking game, historically popular in Saskatchewan and the Prairie provinces. Played by four players in partnerships, it uses a unique 32-card deck featuring two highly consequential cards: the 'Kaiser' (3 of Spades, worth -3 points) and the 'Bonus card' (5 of Hearts, worth +5 points). It is a game of high variance and strategic 'dumping' of negative points.
games.deck: 32 cards (7-Ace, with 5H and 3S replacing lowest spades/hearts)

games.name: Kakeya Toranpu
games.description: Kakeya Toranpu (also known as Etori) is a unique and rare trick-taking game native to Kakeya Town, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It utilizes a standard 52-card deck but introduces a 'Master Card' called the 'Rensho' (usually the Ace of Spades). The game features fixed partnerships and a scoring system based on Go stones, representing a rare survival of localized Japanese card game culture from the Edo period influence.

games.name: Kalooki (Caribbean)
games.description: Kalooki (specifically the Caribbean or Jamaican version) is a high-stakes, 108-card contract rummy game. Played over nine rounds with increasing difficulty, it requires players to complete specific 'contracts' of sets (threes) and runs (fours). It is a central part of Caribbean social life and is known for the 'Call' mechanic where players can snatch discards out of turn.

games.name: Kalookie (British-European)
games.description: Kalookie (British/European version) is a sophisticated Rummy variant played with 106 cards. Unlike the Caribbean 'contract' version, British Kalookie typically emphasizes a points-based initial meld requirement (most commonly 51 points). It is known for its fast 'tacking' gameplay and the high value placed on Jokers, which can be 'stolen' from existing melds on the table.

games.name: Kalter Schlag
games.description: Kalter Schlag (Cold Stroke) is a traditional trick-taking game from Hamburg, Germany, closely related to the 'Ramsch' variants of Skat. Played with 32 cards by four players, it is an 'avoidance' game where the objective is to earn as few points as possible. The name refers to the sudden loss that can occur when a player's hand 'cools' or a surprise mistake leads to a massive point capture.

games.name: Kaluki (European and North American)
games.description: Kaluki (also spelled Kalooki or Kalookie) is a popular rummy variant played throughout Europe and North America. Using two standard decks plus Jokers, players aim to meld all their cards through sets and runs. The defining feature is the initial meld requirementâ€”typically 40 or 51 pointsâ€”which must be met before a player can lay down any cards. The game rewards careful hand management and the strategic use of Jokers.

games.name: Kaluki (European)
games.description: Kaluki (also spelled Kalooki) is a widely played European variant of Rummy, characterized by its use of two 52-card decks plus Jokers. Primarily played for points over multiple hands, it features a 51-point initial meld threshold and a distinctive 'Joker Exchange' rule where players can 'rescue' wild cards from the board.

games.name: Kaluki (South Africa)
games.description: Kaluki (South African version) is a high-penalty variant of Rummy popular in South Africa. Played with two decks and four Jokers, it is distinguished by its severe scoring systemâ€”Jokers are worth 50 penalty pointsâ€”which forces players to prioritize safety and risk management over aggressive melding. It is typically a 7-round game with fixed 13-card hands.

games.name: Kani (Gonin-Kan)
games.description: Kani (also known as Gonin-Kan or Etori) is a sophisticated partnership trick-taking game popular in Aomori Prefecture, Japan. Played by 5 or 6 players, it uses a 50-card deck and features a hidden partnership system where the holder of the Joker and the Ace of trumps work together (the 'Kankei') against the other three players (the 'Mukankei'). It is known for its intense card-counting and localized tournament culture.
games.deck: 50 cards (Standard 52 minus 2 of H, D, C, plus one Joker)

games.name: Kansas City Lowball
games.description: Kansas City Lowball (also known as Deuce-to-Seven Lowball) is a prestigious poker variant where the *worst* traditional poker hand wins. It uses 'Deuce-to-Seven' ranking: Aces are high and undesirable, and straights and flushes are counted against the player. The goal is to make the lowest possible five-card hand that is not a straight or flush. It is renowned for being the 'purist's lowball' and is a staple of the World Series of Poker.

games.name: Kapaga
games.description: Kapaga is a traditional Greenlandic card game belonging to the 'Crazy Eights' family. It is a fast-paced shedding game played with a standard 52-card deck. The game is known for its high interaction, specific localized penalty rules, and the central role of the '8' and 'Ace' as power cards. It is a staple social activity in Greenlandic homes and community centers.

games.name: Karnöffel
games.description: KarnÃ¶ffel is the oldest identifiable European card game, dating back to 1426. It is a trick-taking game with a unique 'chosen suit' mechanism where certain cards have special powers. The game is historically significant as the ancestor of many modern card games including the trump mechanism.

games.name: Karnöffel
games.description: KarnÃ¶ffel is arguably the oldest identifiable European card game still played today, with records dating back to 1426. It is a highly unusual trick-taking game where players are allowed to communicate freely with their partners. The game is famous for its chaotic 'Elected Suit' ranking, featuring cards with evocative names like the Joker-like 'KarnÃ¶ffel' (Unter), the 'Pope' (6), and the 'Devil' (7).
games.deck: 32 cards (Standard 32, German suits); 48-card variant also played historically.

games.name: Kasino (Finnish)
games.description: Kasino (Finnish Casino) is the most popular fishing card game in Finland. Unlike standard Casino, it uses 'Royal' capture values (J=11, Q=12, K=13) and features a unique 'In-Hand Value' system where Aces and the two Kasino cards (10D and 2S) have higher values when held in the hand than when on the table. It is a game of calculation, memory, and defensive stalling.

games.name: Kasino (Standard, International)
games.description: Kasino (Standard Casino) is the international version of the classic 'fishing' card game. Played with a standard 52-card deck, players aim to capture cards from a central table layout by matching ranks or combining values to a sum. It is a game of memory, card-counting, and tactical 'building', forming the basis for numerous regional variants like Scopa (Italy) and Nordic Casino.

games.name: Kasino (Swedish)
games.description: Kasino (Swedish Casino) is a classic fishing game played in Sweden. It uses Royal capture values (J=11, Q=12, K=13; Ace 1 or 14). Players capture table cards by matching rank or by a set that sums to the played card's value; captures are optional. First to 16 points wins. The 10 of Diamonds (Storan) and 2 of Spades (Lillan) score extra; sweeps (tabbe) and last capture (sistan) also score.

games.name: Katti
games.description: Katti (meaning 'cut' or 'bundle' in some dialects) is a traditional Indian banking and gambling game of pure chance, closely related to Andar Bahar. Originating in South India (Karnataka and Tamil Nadu), the game involves betting on which of two piles ('Andar'/Inside or 'Bahar'/Outside) will first receive a card matching the rank of a central 'House' card. It is a staple of festival gambling and modern online casinos.

games.name: Kemps
games.description: Kemps (also known as Kent or Cash) is a fast-paced partnership card game where teams try to collect four-of-a-kind and signal their partner to call 'Kemps!' The game involves secret signals, quick card exchanges, and trying to intercept opponents' signals.

games.name: Kentucky Rook
games.description: Rook variant for four in fixed partnerships. 45 cards (2s-4s removed). Bid from 100 in multiples of 5, take nest, discard five (no point cards), name trump. Trick play; Rook highest trump; 180 points per deal. First team to 500 wins.

games.name: Khanhoo
games.description: Khanhoo is a historical Chinese draw-and-discard money-card game, often cited as an ancestor in the rummy lineage, played with reduced money-card decks.
games.deck: 30-card Khanhoo money-card deck (with regional multi-deck variants)

games.name: Khorol
games.description: Khorol is a Mongolian tile game family treated as its own tile family rather than a western domino skin. It uses a dedicated khorol tile set and regional pattern rules, with placement and scoring conventions that differ from standard western domino supply assumptions.

games.name: Kierki
games.description: Kierki (Polish Hearts) is the Polish variant of the classic avoidance trick-taking game Hearts. Played by four players, it features a unique multi-hand structure where the objective changes each roundâ€”from avoiding hearts to avoiding queens, or taking no tricks at all. It is a game of high strategic depth and defensive maneuvering.

games.name: King
games.description: King is a compendium card game played in many countries including Belgium, Italy, Portugal, Russia, Turkey, Colombia, and Brazil. Despite its English name, there is no evidence it was ever played in English-speaking countries. The game consists of a series of rounds with different objectivesâ€”some negative (avoiding specific cards or tricks) and some positive (winning tricks). It is closely related to Barbu, Kierki, and Trex.
games.origin: Unknown; Russian version dates to 1920s. Popular in Belgium, Portugal, Russia, Turkey, Colombia, Brazil, Italy.

games.name: King Pedro
games.description: King Pedro is a variant of the popular American card game Pedro (also known as Cinch or 63), played primarily in the northeastern United States and Canada. It adds the King of trumps as an additional scoring card worth 5 points, making the total points available 19 per hand instead of the standard 14. It is a trick-taking game where the 5 of trumps (the Pedro) and the 5 of the same color (the Left Pedro) are the most valuable cards.

games.name: Kingen
games.description: Kingen (also known as King) is a Belgian and French trick-taking game played by four individuals. It is a 'compendium' game where a full session consists of a series of rounds with different objectivesâ€”some rounds are 'negative' (avoiding specific tricks or cards) while others are 'positive' (trying to win tricks). It is the European parent of the game Barbu.

games.name: Kings Corners
games.description: Kings Corners is a social, Solitaire-like card game played by 2 to 4 players. Unlike competitive trick-taking games, it focuses on building sequences of alternating colors onto a central cross-shaped layout. The goal is to be the first to empty your hand. It is widely considered one of the best family games for all ages due to its simple rules and visual layout.

games.name: Kláber
games.description: KlÃ¡ber (also known as KalÃ¡ber, KalabriÃ¡sz, or FelsÅ‘s KalÃ¡ber) is a popular Hungarian point-trick card game closely related to Klabberjass and other games of the Jass family. It is played with a special 32-card Hungarian deck (William Tell/Seasons pattern) featuring German suits. The game is particularly popular in DoroszlÃ³ (a town in Northern Serbia with a large ethnic Hungarian population) and among Hungarian card players. It combines trick-taking with melding combinations (sequences and sets) for scoring.

games.name: Kláber
games.description: KlÃ¡ber (also known as FelsÅ‘s or Tartli) is the Hungarian variant of the trick-taking game Klaberjass, particularly popular among ethnic Hungarians in Hungary and neighboring regions. Unlike the international two-player version, KlÃ¡ber is primarily played by four people in fixed partnerships. It features a unique Hungarian deck with seasons-based Ace imagery and William Tell characters on the knaves (Over and Under).

games.name: Klaberjass
games.description: Klaberjass (also known as Clob, Bella, or Bela) is a quintessential two-player trick-taking game that has enjoyed immense popularity for over a century. Known for its complex ranking of trumps (where the Jack and Nine are the most powerful) and the 'Bella' bonus (King and Queen of trumps), it is a game of skill, nerve, and precise point-counting. It belongs to the Jass family of games.

games.name: Klaverjassen
games.description: Klaverjassen (also spelled Klaverjas) is one of the most popular card games in the Netherlands, traditionally played in cafes, social clubs, and at home. It is a trick-taking game for four players in partnerships, characterized by its unique trump ranking (where Jack and Nine are the highest cards) and the scoring of 'roem' (bonus points for card combinations). The game has several regional variants named after Dutch cities: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht.

games.name: Kleurenwiezen
games.description: Kleurenwiezen (Belgian Colour Whist) is the national card game of Belgium. It is a highly competitive trick-taking game where players bid to decide the contract (objective) for the round. Contracts range from winning most tricks with a partner to winning all tricks solo ('Abondance') or even winning zero tricks ('MisÃ¨re'). It is characterized by its complex bidding hierarchy and the social use of specific 'whist' signals.

games.name: Kloepper
games.description: Kloepper (literally 'Knocker' or 'Kloppen') is a high-energy German card game that blends rhythm, memory, and fast reaction times. Distinct from European trick-taking games, it is primarily a social shedding or 'slap' game where the objective is to hit the center pile when specific conditions are met (similar to 'Slapjack' or 'Taco Cat Goat Cheese Pizza'). It is often played as a fast-paced drinking or party game.

games.name: Kluft
games.description: Kluft (meaning 'Gap' or 'Clique') is the Dutch variant of the popular Israeli/Nepalese card game Yaniv. It is a draw-and-discard game where the objective is to reduce the total value of cards in your hand to as low a number as possible. Once a player reaches a threshold (usually 5 points or fewer), they can call 'Kluft' to end the round and claim victory, unless they are challenged by an 'Onderkluft'.

games.name: KnÃ¼ffeln
games.description: KnÃ¼ffeln (also known as KnÃ¼ffeler) is a traditional trick-taking game from North Germany (Oldenburg and Friesland) that belongs to the ancient KarnÃ¶ffel family. It is distinct for its complex 'Elected Suit' ranking, legal partnership communication, and the use of the 'KarnÃ¶ffel' (Unter) as the master card. It is one of the oldest game formats still played in Europe.

games.name: KnÃ¼ffeln (Schafkopf Variant)
games.description: KnÃ¼ffeln is a trick-taking card game from the Schafkopf family, played primarily in parts of Germany. It shares ancestry with Bavarian Schafkopf and related games like Doppelkopf. The game features the characteristic Schafkopf elements of trump suits, partnerships, and point-based scoring, with local variations that distinguish it from its better-known cousins.

games.name: Knaves
games.description: Knaves is a fast-paced trick-taking card game for three players. It is an avoidance game where the primary objective is to gain points for tricks while avoiding the 'Knaves' (Jacks), which carry heavy negative scores. It blends traditional trick-play with the high-stakes risk-management found in games like Hearts.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (minus one card for 3 players)

games.name: Knock Poker
games.description: Knock Poker (also known as Rap Poker) is an American draw and discard game in which the aim is to collect the best five-card poker hand. Unlike traditional poker, there is no betting process of raising and folding. Instead, players draw cards from a stock pile or take the previous player's discard, with the ability to 'knock' to end the round when they believe they have the strongest hand.

games.name: Knock Rummy
games.description: Knock Rummy is a fast-paced variant of the classic Rummy family. Unlike standard Rummy where players must wait for a 'Gin' or empty their hand, in Knock Rummy any player can end the round by 'knocking' after their discard, provided they believe their unmatched card points (deadwood) are lower than their opponents'. It is a game of risk-assessment and speed.

games.name: Knock-Out Whist
games.description: Trick-taking game where players drop out when they take no tricks. Each round has one fewer card per player (7 down to 1). Trump is turned in the first hand; thereafter the winner of the previous hand chooses trumps. Last player standing wins.

games.name: Knorri (Hörri)
games.description: Knorri (also known as HÃ¶rri) is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It belongs to the 'beating' or 'avoidance' family of games (like Skitgubbe). The game is uniquely divided into two phases: a 'Collection Phase' where cards are picked up from the table based on rank-matching, and a 'Trick Phase' where players must play the cards they collected to avoid being the last person with cards in hand.

games.name: Koa
games.description: Koa is a regional Southeast Asian variant in the Ceki family using matching and sequence construction with Ceki cards.

games.name: Koi-Koi
games.description: Koi-Koi is the most popular card game played with traditional Japanese 'Hanafuda' (Flower Cards). Played between two people, it is a fishing (capture) game where players aim to form specific combinations of cards called 'Yaku'. The name 'Koi-Koi' refers to the strategic choice a player makes after forming a Yaku: either to end the round and take their points, or to call 'Koi-Koi' (Come On!) to continue play in hopes of a higher score at the risk of losing it all.
games.deck: 48-card Hanafuda deck (12 suits of 4 cards, each suit representing a month)

games.name: Koira
games.description: Koira (Finnish for 'Dog') is a traditional Finnish card game for three to eight players. It is an avoidance game belonging to the 'beating' family (like Skitgubbe). The game is famous for its social element: the loser is called the 'Dog' and may be jokingly required to bark. It is played in two distinct phases: a collection phase where card count is expanded, and an avoidance phase where players try to empty their hands.

games.name: Königrufen Graden
games.description: KÃ¶nigrufen Graden is a regional variant of KÃ¶nigrufen Tarock played in specific areas of Austria. 'Graden' refers to the graduated or tiered bidding system used in this version. It follows the core KÃ¶nigrufen mechanics with modifications to the contract structure and scoring, making it a distinct regional interpretation of Austria's favorite card game.

games.name: Königrufen Lungau Tarock
games.description: Königrufen Lungau Tarock is a streamlined version of Austrian Tarock played in the Salzburger Lungau region. It features regular tournaments and simplified rules compared to traditional Königrufen. The reduced choice of contracts and simplified card counting lead to a sharper game where valuable cards are more important relative to empty cards.

games.name: Königrufen Rußbach
games.description: KÃ¶nigrufen RuÃŸbach is a regional variant of KÃ¶nigrufen Tarock from the RuÃŸbach area of Austria. Named after the locality where it developed, this variant represents the local interpretation of Austria's national card game, with specific adaptations to contract values, bonuses, or bidding procedures that distinguish it from standard KÃ¶nigrufen.

games.name: Königrufen Tarock
games.description: KÃ¶nigrufen (German: 'Calling the King') is a four-player trick-taking card game of the tarot family, played in Austria and South Tyrol. It is the most popular tarot variant in Austria and, by 2015, had become 'the favourite card game of Austrians'. The game uses a 54-card tarock pack and features a unique bidding system where players can call a king to choose a partner, along with numerous contracts and bonuses.

games.name: Konijnen
games.description: Konijnen (Dutch for 'Rabbits') is a fast-paced, family-friendly shedding game popular in the Netherlands and Scandinavia (where it is known as 'Kanin'). The objective is to be the first to empty your hand by playing cards into numerical sequences on the table. It is known for its speed and the 'tactical shifting' rules that allow players to rearrange table piles to fit their cards.

games.name: Kontra (Finnish Jass Variant)
games.description: Kontra is a Finnish Jass game related to the broader family of trick-taking games with trump suits and point-based scoring. Played with partnerships, it features the characteristic elements of Jass games including special trump card rankings and the opportunity for opponents to double ('kontra') the stakes.

games.name: Kontra (Ristikontra)
games.description: Kontra (primarily known as Ristikontra) is an unusual Finnish trick-taking game popular in lumber camps and traditional social clubs. Played by four players in two fixed partnerships, it features a unique trick-capture rule: tricks are won by the player who plays the *last* card of the same rank as the card that led the trick. It is a game of timing and point-counting rather than suit-power.

games.name: Kontsina (Koltsina)
games.description: Kontsina (also spelled Koltsina or Kolitsina) is the primary Greek fishing card game. Played by two to four players, it is a game of capture where players aim to take cards from a central layout by matching ranks or summing values. It is deeply ingrained in Greek social life, particularly in kafenio (coffee house) culture, and is valued for its balance of luck and tactical calculation.

games.name: Kop
games.description: Kop (also known as Cop) is a traditional Polish trick-taking game that is a cultural staple of the Greater Poland (Wielkopolska) region. Played with a highly condensed 16-card deck, it is celebrated for its extreme speed and complex partnership dynamics. It is a descendant of the German Schafkopf and is the sister game to the Kashubian BaÅ›ka.

games.name: Korean Three-Player Mahjong
games.description: Korean Three-Player Mahjong is a regional three-seat adaptation of Mahjong that preserves draw-discard meld fundamentals while modifying table composition and tactical pacing for one fewer player.
games.deck: Mahjong tile set configured for three-player regional play

games.name: Kosakeln
games.description: Kosakeln is a two-player Austrian tarock trick-taking game in the Industrie und Glueck family. It is a head-to-head adaptation of the Austrian tarock tradition using a 54-card deck with strong emphasis on trump counting and precise endgame timing.

games.name: Kout Bo 6
games.description: Kout Bo 6 (or simply Koutbo6) is a high-stakes, team-based trick-taking game popular in Egypt, Kuwait, and across the Arab world. Played by two teams of three (6 players total), it utilizes 54 cards (standard 52 + 2 Jokers). It is a game of bidding, where the winning team's contract (Hokm) dictates the trump suit, and the Red and Black Jokers serve as the most powerful permanent trumps.

games.name: Kozel (Russian Goat)
games.description: Kozel (Russian for 'Goat') is a highly aggressive Russian trick-taking game played with 36 cards. It is a descendant of the German game 'Bura' and is distinguished by its unique rule allowing players to lead multiple cards of the same suit simultaneously. It is an 'Ace-Ten' game where the objective is to capture point cards, and the loser is mocked as the 'Goat'.

games.name: Kraken
games.description: Kraken is the most competitive and high-stakes variant of the Dutch national game Klaverjassen. Played by four players in two partnerships, it follows the standard 'Amsterdamse' rules but adds an aggressive bidding and doubling system ('Kraken'). In this version, the opponents can 'crack' a contract if they believe the makers will fails to win half the points, doubling the round's value. It is the preferred variant of serious Dutch Klaverjas players.

games.name: Kritisch-Watten
games.description: Kritisch-Watten (also known as Bayerisch Watten or Kritisch Warp) is a popular Alpine variant of the trick-taking game Watten, widely played in Bavaria, Tyrol (Austria), and South Tyrol. It is distinguished by the presence of 'Kritische Karten' (Criticals or Kritten)â€”permanent trumps that rank above all other cards, including the elected trump suit and rank. The game is highly social, utilizing secret signals between partners and psychological bluffing.
games.deck: 32 or 33 cards (German-suited: Heart, Leaf, Acorn, Bell)

games.name: Kruisjassen
games.description: Kruisjassen is a Dutch jass game played by four players in fixed partnerships, two against two. This format gives the game its name, which means 'cross-jass'. As played in the east of the Netherlands, it is one of the most straightforward forms of jass, simpler than the better known Klaverjassen. There is no bidding, trumps are chosen simply by turning a card at the end of the deal, and the result is determined by the value of cards taken in tricks.

games.name: Krypkasino
games.description: Krypkasino (Swedish for 'Crawl Casino') is the popular misere (avoidance) variant of the card game Casino, widely played in Sweden. Unlike standard Casino where the goal is to capture high-point cards, in Krypkasino, players aim to avoid capturing any cards, especially those with point values. It is a game of avoidance, forced capture, and tactical hand-dumping.

games.name: Krypkille
games.description: Krypkille (Swedish for 'Crawl Kille') is the misere (losing) variant of the traditional Swedish card game Kille (or Harlekin). Played with a unique 42-card Kille deck, the objective is to avoid winning tricks or being left with high-penalty cards. Unlike the gambling-focused standard Kille, Krypkille is a pure avoidance game often played in social and family settings in Scandinavia.
games.deck: 42-card Kille deck (2 of each card: Harlekin through Kuku)

games.name: Kryt'-Navalivat' (Крыть-наваливать)
games.description: Kryt'-Navalivat' (Russian for 'Covering and Piling Up') is a traditional Russian card game for two players, although it can accommodate more. It is a descendant of the 'Durak' (Fool) family, specifically influenced by 'Duraki s nakladkoy'. The game focuses on the tactical choice between beating a card (Covering) and forcing more cards onto the opponent (Piling Up). The objective is to empty your hand; the last player left with cards is the 'Fool'.

games.name: Kujong (Couillon)
games.description: Kujong (known in Belgium as Couillon) is a fast-paced trick-taking card game popular in the Low Countries (Belgium, Netherlands) and parts of Germany and Luxembourg. Played by four players in two fixed teams, it uses a 24-card deck. The game is known for its 'erasing' scoring system, where teams start with a 'tree' of 10-12 branches and aim to be the first to prune their tree to zero by winning rounds.

games.name: Kung och Adel
games.description: Kung och Adel (Swedish for 'King and Nobility') is a social card game of the 'President' or 'Asshole' family, flavored with historical Swedish social estates. Players compete to shed their cards and climb the social ladder from Bonden (The Peasant) to Kunegen (The King). The top-ranked players receive bonuses in the form of the best cards from the lower-ranked players in subsequent rounds.

games.name: Kvitlech
games.description: Kvitlech (Yiddish for 'Little Notes') is a unique Jewish card game developed in the late 18th century, primarily played by Ashkenazi Jews during the festival of Hanukkah. It is a variant of Blackjack or 21, but played with a specialized 'Kosher' deck that lacks standard suits and Christian-influenced imagery. Instead, the deck consists of 24 to 31 cards featuring simple numbers or Hebrew identifiers.
games.deck: Special Kvitlech deck (usually 24 or 31 cards, numbers only)

games.name: Kwajongen (Troeven)
games.description: Kwajongen (Flemish for 'Bad Boy' or 'Naughty Boy') is a regional trick-taking game popular in Flanders, particularly in Belgian Limburg. It is the Flemish equivalent of the Walloon game 'Couillon'. Played with a 24-card deck by four players in partnerships, it is a game of quick calculation where teams compete to 'erase' points from a starting score (often visualized as lines on a chalkboard or branches on a tree).

games.name: Kyokabu
games.description: Kyokabu is a traditional Japanese kabufuda gambling-card game played with the 40-card Kabufuda family, emphasizing value totals and betting decisions.

games.name: L'Hombre
games.description: L'Hombre (Spanish for 'The Man') is a historical three-player card game that was the most popular and prestigious card game in Europe for over two centuries (c. 1650-1850). Played with a 40-card Spanish-suited (or standard) deck, it introduced the revolutionary concept of bidding to determine the trump suit and the 'declarer' (The Hombre) who plays alone against the other two. It is the direct ancestor of games like Ombre, Quadrille, and Skat.

games.name: La Belle Lucie
games.description: La Belle Lucie (also known as Lovely Lucy or Three Shuffles and a Draw) is a classic 'Fan' type solitaire game. It is known for its high difficulty and the requirement for careful planning. Unlike Klondike, all cards are dealt face-up into 17 three-card fans, allowing the player to see the entire deck from the start. However, only the top card of each fan is playable, making card blocking a constant challenge.

games.name: La Viuda
games.description: La Viuda ('The Widow') is a Latin American poker-style game. 4-7 players. 5 cards each + 5-card widow on table. Exchange entire hand for widow, OR swap 1 card with widow, OR knock (satisfied). After knock, one final round. Worst hand loses a chip. Extra 'Viuda' chip buyback available once. Last player with chips wins all money.

games.name: LÃ³rum (Hungarian)
games.description: LÃ³rum is a classic Hungarian compendium game played with a 32-card German-suited pack. It consists of a series of diverse 'contracts' or mini-games, traditionally eight in total. Each player takes a turn as the 'declarer' who chooses the round. It is a game of variety, where players must switch from trick-avoidance (negative) to shedding (positive) strategies within a single session. It is deeply rooted in Central European cafe culture.

games.name: LÃ³rum (Slovak)
games.description: The Slovak version of LÃ³rum is a distinct trick-avoidance and bidding game, significantly different from its Hungarian namesake. Played with a 32-card German-suited deck, it focuses on 'Big' and 'Small' games where a single player often plays against a partnership of three. It is a game of high stakes and strict play rules, particularly the 'must-overtake' rule in the Small Game variant.

games.name: Lady Jane
games.description: Lady Jane is a complex two-deck solitaire game belonging to the Spider family. It is characterized by its large tableau of 10 piles and the requirement to build up eight foundations in suit. On the tableau, build down alternating colors; only same-suit sequences can be moved as a unit, requiring tactical planning to keep suits together. Stock deals 3 cards at a time to waste; one redeal allowed.

games.name: Lame Brain Pete
games.description: Lame Brain Pete is a stud poker variant belonging to the Cincinnati family of games. Players receive three hole cards and bet before four community cards are revealed one at a time. The unique twist is that the lowest-ranking exposed community card (and all cards of that rank) become wild cards, creating dynamic hand possibilities that change throughout the hand.

games.name: Lansquenet
games.description: Lansquenet (from the French spelling of German 'Landsknecht' meaning 'servant of the land') is one of the oldest recorded banking card games, dating to at least 1542. It is an extremely simple gambling game where players bet on whether a player card or the dealer's card will appear first from the deck. Purely a game of chance with no skill involved, it was notorious in European military camps and royal courts for its rapid betting and potential for large losses.

games.name: Last One
games.description: Last One (also known as Last Card) is a popular shedding-type card game from the Crazy Eights family. Played across many Commonwealth countries, particularly New Zealand and Australia, it involves players trying to empty their hands by matching cards on a central pile. The game is famous for its 'special cards' that force opponents to draw or skip turns, and the mandatory requirement to announce 'Last One' when holding a single card.

games.name: Laugavatnsmanni
games.description: Laugavatnsmanni is a popular Icelandic trick-taking game for three players, part of the 'Manni' family of games (Manni means 'little man' or 'chap'). Played over 18 rounds, each player must declare one of six different contracts in each rotation, aiming for specific trick targets. The game is unique for its use of a 4-card 'Manni' (dummy) pile that players can use to improve their hands before the round begins.

games.name: Laugh and Lie Down
games.description: Laugh and Lie Down is the earliest documented European fishing card game, dating back to 16th-century England. Played by five players, it is a game of capture where players aim to win pairs from a central pool. The game's name comes from its most famous mechanic: if a player cannot make a capture on their turn, they must discard their entire hand ('Lie Down') while the other players literally 'Laugh' at their misfortune.

games.name: Laus
games.description: Laus (German for 'Louse'), also known as 'BÃ¶se Dame' (Evil Queen) or 'Graue Laus', is a traditional German avoidance trick-taking game. Played with a 32-card German or French deck, it is a precursor to games like Hearts and Black Maria. The primary goal is to avoid capturing the Queen of Spades (the 'Louse'), which carries a heavy point penalty. Players must follow suit, aiming to dump high-value cards on their opponents.

games.name: Le Neuf
games.description: Le Neuf ('Nines') is a French-Canadian trick-taking game from Quebec/Acadian communities. 3 players (4-player variant exists). 52-card deck, 13 each + 13-card 'Chômeur' spare hand. Start at 9 points, subtract to 0. Quota = 4 tricks: each trick above -1pt, below +1pt. Rotating trump cycle: Hearts-Diamonds-Clubs-Spades-No Trump. Can swap hand with Chômeur.

games.name: Let It Ride
games.description: Let It Ride is a popular casino table game based on five-card poker. Unlike traditional poker, players do not compete against each other or the dealer; instead, they play against a fixed paytable.
