The game is unique for its betting structure: players place three equal bets and have two opportunities to 'pull back' (withdraw) one of the bets if they don't like their cards, while 'letting it ride' if they have a strong potential hand.

games.name: Leyden
games.description: Leyden is a two-player domino game named after the university city in South Holland. It is a variant of the 'Matador' family of domino games, characterized by the 'Rule of Seven'â€”players must build arms from a central spinner by matching adjacent ends so they total exactly seven. The game features special 'Matador' tiles that can be played on any end regardless of the sum rule.

games.name: Literature
games.description: Literature is a highly intellectual team-based deduction game, similar to Go Fish or Authors, but significantly more complex. Popular in Indian schools and universities (often called 'Lit'), it requires players to recall every card asked for by every player. The objective is to correctly identify and 'declare' all six cards of a specific half-suit (e.g., Low Hearts A-6 or High Clubs 9-K) to score points for the team.

games.name: Loba
games.description: Loba (Spanish for 'She-Wolf') is a popular Rummy-style card game widely played in Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, and across South America. Similar to Continental Rummy and Carioca, it is played over multiple rounds with increasing difficulty. Players aim to form specific combinations of 'Juegos' (Sets) and 'Escaleras' (Sequences). It is known for its fast pace and the inclusion of Jokers as powerful wildcards.

games.name: Logic
games.description: Logic is a highly strategic deduction-based card game for four players in two teams. It is a game of perfect information (eventually), where players must deduce the identity and position of cards in their opponents' hands. Unlike traditional trick-taking games, 'Logic' is more akin to a competitive version of Mastermind or Hanabi, requiring careful observation of partners' clues and opponents' guesses.
games.deck: 24 cards (A-Q from two suits, e.g., Hearts and Spades)

games.name: London Lowball
games.description: London Lowball is a specific variant of Seven Card Stud played for the 'Low' hand, essentially similar to Razz but traditionally played in London card rooms with Pot-Limit or Spread-Limit structures. The goal is to make the worst possible five-card poker hand out of seven cards dealt. In London rules, the Ace is always low, and straights and flushes do not count against the player, making A-2-3-4-5 the 'nuts' (best possible hand).

games.name: Longana
games.description: Longana is a vibrant and strategic Cuban domino game, often described as 'Domino Solitaire' for teams. Played with a double-nine set (55 tiles), it is famous for its 'arm' (train) mechanic where players build individual sequences extending from a central 'Spinner'. It is a game of blocking and opportunity, where players can force opponents to 'open' their arms, allowing others to dump unwanted tiles on them.

games.name: Lora
games.description: Lora is a highly popular and versatile compendium card game from the Balkans (Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia, and Montenegro). Played with a 32-card German-suited or French deck by four players, it consists of a series of rounds, most of which are 'Negative' games (avoidance) where players aim to avoid winning specific cards or tricks. It is famous for its 'all-or-nothing' nature and is a staple of cafe social life in Southeast Europe.

games.name: Losing Loadum
games.description: Losing Loadum (or Losing Lodam) is an intriguing ancestor of the Hearts family, dating back to 16th-century England. It is a 'penalty trick' game where the objective is to avoid winning specific high-value cards called 'Loaders'. The game is unique for its elimination mechanic: any player reaching 31 points is immediately 'out'. It also features a rare 'hidden trump' system where trumps are determined only when a player first fails to follow suit.

games.name: Lost Heir
games.description: Lost Heir is a historical bidding and trick-taking game that gained massive popularity in the late 19th century in North America. Produced by McLoughlin Brothers (and later Milton Bradley), it features a custom deck where suits are named after major cities (e.g., New York, Boston, Chicago, Philadelphia). The game centers around two pivotal cards: the 'Lost Heir' (bonus points) and the 'Wrong Boy' (penalty points). It combines the bidding strategy of Pinochle with the capture mechanics of Authors.

games.name: Low Hole (Wild Card Stud)
games.description: Low Hole is an action-packed 'dealer's choice' Poker variant played as Seven Card Stud. Its defining characteristic is the 'Low Hole' wild card rule: the lowest-valued card in each player's individual 'hole' (face-down cards) is wild for that specific player. Because your wild card can change as you receive new hole cards, it creates high-variance gameplay and massive winning hands.

games.name: Luk Fu (Six Tigers)
games.description: Luk Fu (å…­è™Ž), literally 'Six Tigers', is a traditional Hakka Chinese trick-taking game played with a unique money-suited deck of 38 cards. It is a highly complex and fast-paced game where players compete to be the first to capture six 'Fu' (tigers/tricks). The game features 'Aged Cards' (cards that become unbeatable) and special multi-trick combinations like 'Five Tigers Emerge From the Mountain' (Ng Fu Ha San).

games.name: Lupfen
games.description: Lupfen is a traditional trick-taking card game from Switzerland and Southern Germany. It is closely related to the game of 'Schafkopf' and 'Watten' but is played with a unique 36-card deck and features a distinctive auction system where players bid for the right to choose the trump suit and play solo against the other players. The game emphasizes precise card play and strategic bidding.

games.name: Machiavelli
games.description: Machiavelli is a sophisticated Italian card game of the Rummy family, named after the political philosopher NiccolÃ² Machiavelli for its tactical complexity and the ability to 'manipulate' the board. Unlike standard Rummy where melds are static once played, players in Machiavelli can dismantle, rearrange, and recombine any cards already on the table to help them play cards from their hand. It is practically identical to the game Rummikub but played with standard cards.

games.name: Madiao
games.description: Madiao is a historical Chinese money-card game with trick-taking and gambling structure, traditionally played with a dedicated 40-card money-suited deck.

games.name: Madrasso
games.description: Madrasso is a classic Venetian trick-taking game played in partnerships. It is a member of the 'Tressette' family but features a trump suit, making it a bridge between Tressette and Briscola. Known for its specific point target (777 points) and the 'exchange' of the trump indicator card, it is the quintessential game of the Veneto region of Italy. It requires careful hand management and a strong memory of point-cards already played.

games.name: Magarac (Donkey)
games.description: Magarac (literally 'Donkey') is a high-speed, lighthearted card-passing game popular in Croatia, Serbia, and the wider Balkan region. Similar to the Western game 'Spoons' or 'Pig', it is a game of reaction and physical speed. Players pass cards around the table attempting to collect four of a kind, after which a frantic 'slam' follows to avoid being the last person noticed.
games.deck: Standard cards adapted to player count

games.name: Mah Jong (Traditional Chinese)
games.description: Mah Jong (éº»å°‡) is a game of skill, strategy, and calculation, and it involves a degree of chance. While traditionally played with tiles, it is also frequently played with specialized 'Mahjong Cards'. Originating in China, it is played by four players. The game is similar to Rummy in that the goal is to build combinations (Sets and Runs) from a hand of 13 cards/tiles to achieve a 'Mahjong' with a 14th card.

games.name: Mahjong (Japanese Riichi)
games.description: Japanese Mahjong, or Riichi Mahjong, is the most competitively evolved form of the Chinese classic. It is characterized by the 'Riichi' mechanicâ€”a declaration of being one card away from winningâ€”and the 'Dora' system of bonus point cards. It is a highly defensive and strategic game where 'not losing' (avoiding dealing into an opponent's hand) is as important as winning.

games.name: Mahjong Official Rules (MCR)
games.description: Mahjong Official Rules, often called MCR, is a standardized competition-focused Mahjong ruleset. It keeps classic Mahjong draw-discard structure while using a formalized scoring catalog for consistent tournament adjudication.

games.name: Main Merah
games.description: Main Merah (Indonesian for 'Playing Red') is a traditional fishing card game popular in Indonesia. It is a variant of the broader 'Fishing' family (like Scopa or Kou-Shuu) but with a specific focus on color. In this game, only the RED cards (Hearts and Diamonds) have point value, leading to a unique secondary economy where players prioritize capturing red cards while using black cards as purely functional tools.

games.name: MakaÃ³ (Hungarian Shedding)
games.description: MakaÃ³ (often referred to as 'Mak-Var' in regional contexts) is the most popular shedding card game in Hungary and much of Central Europe. It is the tactical ancestor of games like Uno and Crazy Eights. Using a standard 32-card or 52-card deck, players attempt to discard all their cards while using powerful action cards to penalize opponents. The game's name comes from the requirement to shout 'MakaÃ³!' when one card remains.

games.name: Malaysian Mahjong
games.description: Malaysian Mahjong is a Southeast Asian Mahjong profile with expanded bonus and joker-style tiles in many common sets. It uses a larger 160-tile composition and local scoring conventions.

games.name: Malilla
games.description: Malilla is a point-trick game for four players in fixed partnerships, popular in Mexico and originating in Spain. Played with a 40-card Spanish deck, the Seven is the highest card (Malilla), ranking above Ace. Partners score card points (7=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one per trick; first team to 35 cumulative points wins. Trump is set by the dealer's last card turned face up.

games.name: Maltese Cross
games.description: Maltese Cross is a domino game played with a double-six set. It takes its name from the tableau layout that resembles a Maltese Cross. The game features a unique two-phase setup where players first build four arms around a central spinner, then add doubles crosswise to complete the cross shape before regular play continues.

games.name: Mambassa
games.description: Mambassa is a lively Italian card game played on the coast of the Marche province. It is a four-card variant of Petrangola (also known as 31), where players aim to collect cards of high value in a single suit, with a maximum of 41 points. The game features a unique 'monte' (table cards) exchange mechanic and knocking system similar to Schwimmen.

games.name: Maniglia
games.description: Maniglia (also spelled Mariglia) is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from Sardinia, Italy. Known as 'Bridge Sardo' (Sardinian Bridge) for its depth of strategy, it belongs to the Manille family of games. The Seven is the highest and most valuable card of each suit, giving the game its name ('maniglia' means handle or lever).

games.name: Manillen
games.description: Manillen is a popular point-trick card game played extensively in West Flanders, Belgium. Derived from the French game Manille (which came from Spanish Malilla), it features the unique 'Manille' (10) as the highest card in each suit. The game is known for its simple rules but deep strategic possibilities, especially the 'Ik ga mee' (I go along) doubling mechanic.

games.name: Manni
games.description: Manni (meaning 'little man' or 'chap') is the national card game of Iceland, played with three players and a 48-card deck. The game features a unique 'Manni' - a spare hand of four cards dealt to the table that the declarer can use to improve their hand. With four different contracts (Grand, Spades, Other, and Nullo), players must play each contract once during the 12-deal game.
games.deck: 52-card pack (Trjámann: 16 each, 4 to Manni). Basic Manni uses 48 cards (twos removed), 12 each, 12 Manni.

games.name: Mao
games.description: Mao is a unique card game known for its extreme secrecy and metagame elements. It is the most famous of the 'secret rule' games, where the only rule that may be explained to a new player is: 'The rules of Mao cannot be told.' New players must learn the rules through trial and error, as they are penalized (by drawing cards) for every infraction. Each winner of a round also gets to create a new secret rule for the next round, meaning the game evolves indefinitely.

games.name: Marafon-Beccaccino
games.description: Marafon (also known as Beccaccino) is the 'King of Romagna Card Games', a sophisticated partnership trick-taking game played with a 40-card Italian deck. It combines the precise point-structure of Tressette (where 3s and 2s are high) with the power of a Trump suit. Famous for its 'silent play' etiquette and complex signaling system, it demands perfect memory and seamless teamwork. A match typically races to 41 points, with bonuses for holding the 'Cricca' (the top three trumps).

games.name: Mariaccio
games.description: Mariaccio is a spirited Italian card game from the Neapolitan tradition, specifically a variation of Briscola. It is also known as 'Marianna' or 'Mariaggia' (when played with open cards). The defining feature is the 'Marriage' (Mariaccio)â€”a King and Knight of the same suitâ€”which grants bonus points. It is a game of high targets, usually requiring 250 points to win, making it a longer and more tactical experience than standard Briscola.

games.name: Mariagenspiel (Mariage)
games.description: Mariagenspiel is the historical ancestor of the vast 'Marriage' family of card games, which includes global hits like Sixty-Six, Schnapsen, Pinochle, and Belote. Its name literally means 'Marriage Game', referring to the core mechanic: earning bonus points by holding and declaring a King and Queen of the same suit. It is a trick-taking game where players must balance the pursuit of card points with the opportunistic timing of their marriages.

games.name: Marianna
games.description: Marianna is a fast-paced Italian partnership card game, widely considered a strategic evolution of Briscola. Played by four players in two fixed teams, it is unique because the 'Trump' suit is not predetermined by the dealer. Instead, the first team to declare a 'Marianna' (a King and Knight of the same suit) simultaneously scores bonus points and chooses the trump suit for the remainder of the round. This dynamic makes the start of every hand a high-speed race to find and declare a marriage.

games.name: Mariáš
games.description: Mariáš is the national card game of the Czech Republic and Slovakia, derived from the historical Mariagespiel. It is a highly competitive trick-taking and bidding game typically played by three players with a 32-card German-suited deck. The game involves complex bidding for different contracts (Standard, Seven, Betl, Durch) and is famous for its strict play rules: you must follow suit, you must trump, and you must win the trick if possible.

games.name: Mariglia
games.description: Mariglia is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from Sardinia, Italy, particularly popular in the North around Sassari, Olbia, and Nuoro. Known as 'Bridge Sardo' (Sardinian Bridge) for its strategic depth, it belongs to the Manille family where the Seven is the highest and most valuable card. The game allows open communication between partners, making it unique among trick-taking games.

games.name: Marjapussi
games.description: Marjapussi is a four-player point-trick game from southern Finland. The name means 'bag of berries' but derives from the French 'mariage' (marriage of King and Queen), reflecting the game's unique mechanic where the trump suit is determined during play by declaring a marriage. Unlike its bidding variant Huutopussi, Marjapussi has no bidding - teams simply score based on points made in play.

games.name: Marjolet
games.description: Marjolet is an elegant two-player card game from southwest France, and the direct ancestor of Bezique and Pinochle. Played with a 32-card French deck, it combines trick-taking with melding, featuring the unique 'Marjolet' (trump Jack) that can be melded with different Queens. The game is known for its tactical depth despite simple rules.

games.name: Marquise (Solitaire)
games.description: Marquise (often associated with the Marquise de Pompadour) is an elegant, historical French solitaire game played with a 32-card piquet deck. It is a game of patience and careful sequence building, reflecting the aristocratic pastimes of the 18th-century French court. Unlike modern Klondike, it is a tighter, more deterministic puzzle due to the smaller deck size and specific building constraints.

games.name: Marriage (Nepali)
games.description: Marriage is a three-pack Rummy game popular in Nepal (especially Kathmandu valley) and Bhutan, and by the Nepali diaspora. Played with 156 cards (three standard 52-card decks), each player receives 21 cards. Wild cards (tiplu, poplu, jhiplu) are determined during play. Players form sets of three: tunnela (three identical cards), pure sequence (three consecutive same suit), or trial (three same rank, different suits); the first to complete three pure sets chooses the tiplu (main wild). The first to arrange all cards into valid sets and discard wins the hand; scoring uses maal points and payments.
games.deck: 156 cards (three standard 52-card packs; no printed jokers)

games.name: Marriage Rummy
games.description: Marriage Rummy (also known simply as Marriage) is a complex Rummy-style game popular in Nepal, Bhutan, and parts of Northern India. Played with three standard 52-card decks, each player receives 21 cards. The game features a unique 'Wild Card' system (Tiplu, Poplu, Jhiplu) and requires players to form three initial pure sets before they can 'see the joker' and use wild cards.
games.deck: 156 cards (Three standard 52-card decks, no jokers printed)

games.name: Matador
games.description: Matador (meaning 'killer' or bullfighter) is a unique domino game from Spain with special matching rules. Unlike standard dominoes where matching numbers touch, in Matador the touching ends must add up to seven. The 'matador' tiles (0-0, 1-6, 2-5, 3-4) can be played on any end, giving the game its name. Also known as 'Russian Dominoes' or 'Kardinal domino' in some regions.

games.name: Matador (Card Game Condition)
games.description: In the context of European card games, 'Matador' is not always a standalone game, but a term used to describe the most powerful cards in a game (typically trumps). Most famously used in the **Ombre** family (Ombre, Quadrille) and the **Skat** family, Matadors are cards that belong together as a sequence of high-power tokens. They often trigger specific scoring bonuses or 'payment' rules where the loser must pay the winner for every Matador held.

games.name: Match Pot Poker
games.description: Match Pot Poker is a dramatic high-stakes poker variant where players must match the entire pot when dealt a face-up 3 (the 'Strike'). This creates massive pot escalation and intense decision points. The game combines elements of Baseball Poker with an even more severe penalty structure, making it a favorite for adrenaline-seeking home game players.

games.name: Mate
games.description: Mate is a traditional Italian fishing card game played with a 40-card Italian deck. Players capture cards from a central layout by matching values, with special scoring for capturing the 'Mate' cards (Kings). It is a game of memory and timing, where players must remember which cards have been played to maximize their captures.

games.name: Matgo (Korean Go-Stop)
games.description: Matgo is the quintessential two-player variant of 'Go-Stop', a popular Korean fishing game played with Hwatu ('Flower Cards'). Using a 48-card deck where each group of four represents a month/flower, players attempt to capture cards to form scoring combinations (Yaku). The name 'Matgo' distinguishes the 2-player competitive style from the 3-player 'Go-Stop'. It is arguably the most popular mobile and online game in South Korea.

games.name: Mattazza
games.description: Mattazza is a traditional Italian trick-avoidance game, often described as a chaotic and humorous variant of the 'Loser Wins' family. Played with a 40-card Italian deck, the goal is specifically to NOT be the best or the worst player in terms of points captured. It is a game of social sabotage and precise point management, where being average is the key to survival.

games.name: Mattis
games.description: Mattis (also known as Skitgubbe in Sweden) is a unique two-phase card game popular in Scandinavia. The first phase involves collecting cards by winning tricks, while the second phase reverses the objective - players try to get rid of their collected cards by beating opponents' cards. The last player holding cards loses. It is a game of strategic timing and card management.

games.name: Mauscheln
games.description: Mauscheln (also known as 'Maus' or 'Lurk') is a traditional German gambling and trick-taking game popular in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Similar to games in the 'Rams' family, it focuses on the choice to either 'Sneak' (Mauscheln)—committing to win at least two tricks—or 'Pass' to avoid a penalty. It is famous for its fast rounds, rapidly escalating pots, and the high-stakes risk of the 'Bête' (a penalty equal to the entire pot).

games.name: Maw
games.description: Maw is a historic trick-taking card game that was popular in 16th century Britain and Ireland. It is the ancestor of the Irish game Spoil Five and other related games. Played with a distinctive 52-card deck where the 5 and 9 of trumps have special powers, Maw features unique ranking orders and the ability to renege (not follow suit) under specific circumstances.

games.name: Mediatore
games.description: Mediatore is an Italian trick-taking game for four players, closely related to Tressette. It features a unique bidding system where the final bidder plays alone against a team of three, or chooses a partner by calling a card. The game uses a 40-card Italian deck and includes a 'monte' of undealt cards that can improve the bidder's hand.

games.name: Meksiko
games.description: Meksiko is the most popular trick-taking game in Serbia, played by three players with a 32-card deck. It is an Auction Whist variant where players bid on the number of tricks they will take, with the highest bid 'Meksiko' being an undertaking to win all tricks without the talon and with no trumps. The game combines bidding strategy with precise trick-taking play.

games.name: Memory
games.description: Memory (Concentration) is a domino adaptation of the card game Pelmanism. All double-6 tiles are laid face down in a 4×7 grid. On your turn you turn up two tiles; if they total 12 you remove them and take another turn; otherwise you turn them face down and the next player goes. The first to capture 50 tiles (25 pairs) or an agreed total wins. It is a test of memory.

games.name: Mendikot
games.description: Mendikot is a trick-taking card game from India, particularly popular in the western states of Maharashtra and Gujarat. It is a partnership game where the objective is to win tricks containing tens. The name comes from Gujarati where 'mendi' refers to the zero in '10' and 'kot' means a decisive victory where opponents score nothing.

games.name: Mënsch
games.description: MÃ«nsch is a Swiss Jass game for four players in partnerships. It belongs to the Jass family of games popular in Switzerland and surrounding regions. The game features the 'Mensch' (Queen of Clubs) as a permanent highest trump, similar to other games in the Ombre/Solo family. Players bid for the right to choose trumps and must make their contract.

games.name: Mënsch (Luxembourgish Trick-Taking)
games.description: MÃ«nsch is a traditional trick-taking game from Luxembourg, belonging to the Ombre/Solo family of European card games. Played by four players with a 32-card deck, it features the 'Mensch' (the Queen of Clubs) as the permanent highest trump card, regardless of the declared suit. It is a game of shifting alliances where a bidder can choose to play alone (Solo) or call a partner to help them win a majority of tricks.

games.name: Mentiroso (Liar)
games.description: Mentiroso (Spanish for 'Liar') is the Hispanic world's definitive version of the global bluffing game 'Cheat' or 'I Doubt It'. Played with the 40-card Spanish deck, it is a game of shedding and deception. Players discard cards face-down and claim their rank; if an opponent believes the player is lying, they shout 'Â¡Mentiroso!'. It is a cultural staple in Spain and Latin America, often played in families to teach social observation and poker-face maintenance.

games.name: Mexican Stud
games.description: Mexican Stud (also Mexican Sweat): 7-card stud variant where each player's lowest hole card is wild for that player. Same deal as 7-card stud; wild card can change as new hole cards are dealt. USA; dealer's choice.

games.name: Mexican Train
games.description: Mexican Train is a popular domino game played mainly in the USA. It is best for four or more players and uses a double-twelve domino set. Players build trains of dominoes from a central hub, with each player having their own personal train and a shared 'Mexican Train' that anyone can play on. The game combines strategic tile placement with careful hand management.

games.name: Michigan Rummy (Newmarket, Boodle)
games.description: Michigan Rummy (also known as Newmarket, Boodle, or Stops) is a classic American family game that combines elements of sequence-based shedding with a wagering layout. Players compete to be the first to play all their cards (Shedding) while simultaneously trying to play specific 'Money Cards' (Ace of Hearts, King of Clubs, etc.) that correspond to pots on the game board. It is one of the most famous 'three-games-in-one' style tabletop classics.

games.name: Mighty
games.description: Mighty is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Mille Bornes
games.description: Racing card game for 2–6 players. Each hand is a race to 1000 km (or 700 km in 2–3 player with optional extension). Players play distance cards to advance; opponents play hazards (Accident, Out of Gas, Flat Tire, Stop, Speed Limit) which are countered by remedies and prevented by safeties. First to reach the target distance wins the hand. Game ends when one side reaches 5000 cumulative points.

games.name: Milo
games.description: Milo is a partnership domino game played in Africa and parts of Indonesia. It uses the same equipment and basic play as Latin Partnership Dominoes, but with different scoring: the winning partnership gets one point for domino; if blocked, the partnership with the smallest total of pips on their tiles gets one point; if the tile that made domino causes both ends of the train to end in the same suit, the partnership scores two points (called a Milo). A game is five points.

games.name: Minchiate
games.description: Minchiate (also known as Germini or Gallerini) is a historic Italian trick-taking game played with a unique 97-card Tarot deck. Invented in Florence in the 16th century, it was once one of the most popular games in Italy. The game features complex scoring for 'versicole' (card combinations) and a unique 'Fola' system where players can exchange cards before play.

games.name: Minette (Minet)
games.description: Minette (or Minet) is a traditional 18th-century French card game for two players. It is a point-trick game played with a 32-card Piquet deck, sharing similarities with games like Ã‰cartÃ© and Mariage. It is notable for its 'Exchanges' phase and the focus on capturing specific high-value cards while navigating the constraints of a small deck.

games.name: Minibridge
games.description: Minibridge is a simplified version of Contract Bridge, developed specifically to introduce beginners to the logic of trick-taking and card play without the daunting complexity of bridge bidding. It replaces the auction phase with a straightforward High Card Point (HCP) count. It is widely used by bridge federations globally (like the EBU and ABF) as an educational tool, focusing on the tactical interaction between declarer and the dummy.

games.name: Minimisere
games.description: Minimisere is an original trick-taking card game designed by David Parlett. It is a game of 'controlled winning and losing', where the objective is to win a specific number of tricks (e.g., three or four)â€”or none at allâ€”but avoiding the middle ground and, crucially, avoiding winning everything. It is a tactical game that rewards precise hand evaluation and the ability to 'dump' high cards into other players' tricks.

games.name: Minobasco (Shokoba)
games.description: Minobasco (often associated with the name 'Shokoba') is a specialized, modern variant of the traditional Italian fishing game 'Escoba' (or Scopa). It is unique for its use of colorful plastic 'Gemstones' as scoring tokens and its simplified point-capture rules aimed at a faster, more competitive pace. Like Scopa, players use cards from their hand to capture sums of cards from the table, but with an emphasis on 'Shokoba'â€”clearing the entire table for a bonus point.
games.deck: Standard 40-card Italian or specialized Minobasco deck

games.name: Mississippi Mud
games.description: Mississippi Mud: 7-card stud variant where the first and fourth upcards dealt to each player are wild for that player. Same deal as 7-card stud; two designated upcards act as wilds. USA; dealer's choice.

games.name: Mitaines
games.description: Mitaines is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Mitigatti (Gatti)
games.description: Mitigatti (also known as Gatti) is a traditional Italian trick-taking game played with a Tarot deck (Tarocchi). Popular in the Piedmont and Liguria regions, it is a complex game involving 78 cards, including 21 trumps and the Joker-like 'Matto'. It features a unique 'Bargaining' phase where players can negotiate to end a hand early based on their card strength, and scoring is based on both captured tricks and specific card combinations (declarations).
games.deck: 78-card tarot deck; historically Italian-suited Tarocco Piemontese, but by the Nice 1930 source often played with French-suited tarot cards

games.name: Mittlere Jass
games.description: Mittlere Jass is an unusual Swiss Jass game for three players. It is a point trick game where the basic objective is to avoid ending up with the middle score. The game features dynamic trump determination - the first suit played that cannot be followed becomes trumps for the rest of the hand. It is played with sticks (which players try to win) and potatoes (which players try to avoid).

games.name: Mizerka
games.description: Mizerka is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Mizerka (Polish Trick-Taking)
games.description: Mizerka is a popular Polish trick-taking game for three players, played with a standard 52-card deck. It is a game of 'Contracts', where each player must eventually choose to play through six distinct game types (four suits, No Trump, and the eponymous 'Mizerka'â€”a misere avoidance contract). It features a unique 'Partial Deal' bidding phase and a talon exchange that allows players to refine their hands. It is highly strategic, requiring players to balance their aggressive and defensive contracts throughout 18 total rounds.

games.name: Moghul Ganjifa
games.description: Moghul Ganjifa is a traditional South Asian trick-taking game family played with the 96-card Mughal ganjifa deck and circular-suited court structure.

games.name: Molotow Jass
games.description: Molotow Jass is a Swiss Jass game for four players, derived from Mittlere Jass. It uses the same dynamic trump determination (first void play establishes trumps) but adapts the scoring for four players. The game features unique scoring where the middle two players can end up with potatoes while the highest and lowest scorers get sticks.

games.name: Money
games.description: Money is a two-player card game found in several Arab countries including Jordan, Syria, and Egypt. Players hold their cards in a face-down stack and must play the top card at each turn. The game combines elements of fishing games (capturing matching cards) with a unique 'money' system where picture cards (Kings, Queens, Jacks) are set aside and used to buy cards when a player runs out.

games.name: Money (Traditional Capture Game)
games.description: Money is a traditional two-player card game popular in Arab nations such as Jordan, Syria, and Egypt. It is a high-speed capture game that uses a standard deck modified by separating the face cards (the 'Money') from the numeral cards. Players compete to capture numeral cards from a central pile by matching their values, while simultaneously using their 'Bank' of picture cards as currency to buy cards from their opponent. The goal is to accumulate all the cards in the game.

games.name: Montana Domino Rummy
games.description: Montana Domino Rummy is a western domino rummy-style game typically played with multiple double-six sets to provide sufficient tile supply. This entry models the shared tile family and supply using four double-six sets; the rummy-style sequencing and layout objectives are expressed as a table profile layered on top of the tile set.

games.name: Mort (La Morte)
games.description: Mort (also known as La Morte) is a specialized trick-taking card game for 3 to 5 players, traditionally played with a modified Tarot deck. Created by Matt Haller, it combines the structural depth of Bridge and Tarot with a unique 'Specialist' mechanic centered around the 'La Morte' card (the 13 of Trumps). It involves complex bidding, the ability to 'Drop Out' of a hand to avoid points, and a high penalty for being 'Fuori dal Tempo' (out of time) on the final trick.

games.name: Mpourloto
games.description: Mpourloto (also spelled Bourloto) is a Greek trick-taking game closely related to French Belote. It is played by four players in partnerships using a 32-card deck. The game features bidding for trumps, declaring melds for bonus points, and a unique scoring system where the trump makers must outscore their opponents or lose all points to them ('mesa').

games.name: Mulle
games.description: Mulle (also known as Swedish Casino or Nordic Casino) is a fishing card game popular in Sweden and Finland. It is a variant of the international Casino game family, where players capture cards from a central layout by matching values. The game features unique Nordic scoring rules and special values for certain cards.

games.name: Mura
games.description: Mura is an unusual Hungarian card game for four players. It is a trick-avoidance game where players try not to win tricks, but with a twist: only certain cards (figures) have value, and winning tricks without figures is actually beneficial. The game uses a 32-card Hungarian deck with unique ranking.

games.name: Mus
games.description: Mus is a popular Spanish game of Basque origin, played by four players in partnerships. It is unusual among vying games in that it is played without money and with partnerships. The game involves drawing cards and betting on who has the best hand in four categories: Grande (high), Chica (low), Pares (pairs), and Juego (game). It features extensive bluffing and a complex system of signals.

games.name: Mushi
games.description: Mushi is a traditional hanafuda family game focused on matching and capture tempo using the standard 48-card flower deck.

games.name: Mustamaija
games.description: Mustamaija is a Finnish card game whose name translates to 'Black Maria'. It is a beating game of the multiple attack type where the aim is to avoid being left holding the Queen of Spades when all other players have run out of cards. Though often considered a children's game, the tactical play is interesting enough for adults to enjoy.

games.name: Myllymatti
games.description: Myllymatti is a Finnish card game that is the ancestor of the Swedish game Skitgubbe and the Norwegian game Mattis. It is a two-phase game: first players collect cards by winning tricks, then they try to get rid of those cards by beating opponents' cards. The last player holding cards loses.

games.name: Nap
games.description: Nap (short for Napoleon) is a classic English trick-taking game that gained massive popularity in Britain during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It is a quick, high-stakes game where players bid on how many of their five cards they can win in a trick-based battle against everyone else. Known for its escalating bidding tiers named after Napoleonic battles (Wellington, BlÃ¼cher) and its simple yet ruthless scoring system.

games.name: Nap (Napoleon)
games.description: Nap (short for Napoleon) is a classic English trick-taking game that gained massive popularity in Britain during the 19th and early 20th centuries. It is a quick, high-stakes game where players bid on how many of their five cards they can win in a trick-based battle against everyone else. It is known for its escalating bidding tiers named after Napoleonic battles (Wellington, BlÃ¼cher) and its simple yet ruthless scoring system.

games.name: Napalm
games.description: Napalm (Whipsaw/3-5-7) is a multi-stage poker variant emphasizing bluffing. 4-7 players. 52-card deck. Three stages: Stage 1 (2 cards, best high), Stage 2 (+3 community, best LOW 5-card), Stage 3 (+2 more, best HIGH 5-card). Each stage: declare 'yes/no' if you think you have best hand. Single yes=token. Multiple yes=side bets. First to collect 5 tokens wins the pot.

games.name: Neeznáá Dah Yíjihí
games.description: NeeznÃ¡Ã¡ Dah YÃ­jihÃ­ (Navajo Tens) is a traditional Navajo fishing card game where players compete to capture cards from a central layout by making combinations that sum to 10. It is a culturally significant game that has been passed down through generations in Navajo communities, combining elements of memory, arithmetic, and strategic card play.

games.name: Neeznáá Dah Yíjihí
games.description: Neeznáá Dah Yíjihí (Navajo Tens) is a traditional Navajo fishing card game where players compete to capture cards from a central layout by making combinations that sum to 10.

games.name: Neighbor Games
games.description: Neighbor Games is a vying card game where players compare hand values or make declarations to determine the winner. Players compete through strategic card play and bluffing to win the pot or achieve the highest hand ranking.

games.name: Neunzehnerrufen
games.description: Neunzehnerrufen is a four-player Austrian tarock partnership game in the Industrie und Glueck family. It uses a 54-card deck and distinguishes itself by calling Tarock XIX in partner contracts rather than calling a king.

games.name: Nickels (Three Thirteen)
games.description: Nickels (also known as Three Thirteen or 65) is a progressive Rummy-style card game played over 11 distinct rounds. The game starts with three cards dealt to each player and ends with thirteen cards in the final round. It is known for its shifting 'Wild Card' rule, where the rank corresponding to the number of cards dealt becomes wild for that specific round. It is a game of patience, set-building, and risk-management, where the goal is to have the lowest cumulative score.

games.name: Nijū-kyū (Japanese 29)
games.description: Nijū-kyū (Twenty-Nine) is a tactical Japanese card game focused on cumulative addition and card capture. Played with a standard deck, the objective is to be the player who plays a card that brings the total on the table exactly to twenty-nine. The player who hits the target 'sweeps' the table and collects the cards as scoring points. It is a game of subtraction-logic, card counting, and opportunistic 'sniping' of the target total.

games.name: Nine Card Brag
games.description: Nine Card Brag (often called 'Crash') is the final evolution of the multi-card Brag family. Players are dealt nine cards and must divide them into three independent three-card hands. These hands are compared against opponents' corresponding hands in three separate 'showdowns' (front, middle, and back). It combines the traditional British Brag hand rankings with the partition complexity of Chinese Poker, creating a high-stakes duel of distribution and nerve.

games.name: Nine Card Don
games.description: Nine Card Don is a trick-taking card game where players compete over nine rounds. Players are dealt cards and compete to win tricks or achieve specific scoring objectives based on game rules.

games.name: Nine Five Two
games.description: Nine Five Two is a Canadian variation of Sergeant Major (8-5-3), a trick-taking game for three players with rotating targets. Each player has a specific trick quota: dealer needs 9, left opponent needs 5, right opponent needs 2. Players exchange cards based on overtricks/undertricks from previous hands. The game combines trick-taking skill with strategic card exchange.

games.name: Nine Five Two (9-5-2)
games.description: 9-5-2: trick-taking game; name may refer to card ranks or deal (e.g. 9, 5, 2 cards). Trump and follow suit; point or trick count to win. Played in India and elsewhere.

games.name: Nine-Card Don
games.description: Nine-Card Don (also known as Big Don or Welsh Don) is a traditional British pub game for four players in fixed partnerships. It is a descendant of the 17th-century game All Fours. Unlike the Irish version, only nine cards are dealt to each player, leaving a significant portion of the deck unseen, which adds a layer of uncertainty and boneyard-tracking to the strategy.
games.origin: United Kingdom (specifically North West England and South Wales)

games.name: Ninety-eight
games.description: 98: adding game. Play one card to a central pile and announce new total. A-9 add face value; 10 subtracts 10; J/Q no change; K sets pile to 98. Avoid exceeding 98; first to push total over 98 loses. Often played as drinking game.

games.name: Ninety-Nine (adding game)
games.description: 99 (adding game): play cards to a central pile; A=1 or 11, 2-9=face, 10=-10, J/Q=0, K=99 or reset. Avoid exceeding 99; first to push over loses. Similar to 98. USA/UK.

games.name: Niu Niu (Ox-Ox, Bullfighting)
games.description: Niu Niu (literally 'Ox Ox') is a popular gambling card game originating from Southern China and widely played in Southeast Asia. It is a banking game where players receive five cards and must split them into a three-card set (totaling a multiple of 10) and a two-card hand. The value of the two-card hand determines the strength of the 'Ox'. It is known for its fast pace, significant multipliers on high hands, and its ubiquity in Asian casinos and social gatherings.

games.name: NLK
games.description: NLK is a Hungarian beating/shedding card game for 4-9 players in two phases. Phase One: players accumulate cards by drawing from a talon and giving away cards that fit on opponents' stacks (next rank higher). Phase Two: players try to shed their accumulated cards by beating cards in tricks. The last player holding cards loses.
games.deck: Variable (32-52 cards depending on player count)

games.name: NLK (Czech Beating Game)
games.description: NLK (Czech variant) is a unique two-phase beating and shedding game from the Czech Republic. It combines elements of 'accumulation' (Phase One) and 'beating' (Phase Two). Players first build stacks of cards by placing one rank higher than the opponent's top card, and then use these accumulated cards to play a trick-beating game where the goal is to empty your hand.
games.deck: Variable (32 to 52 cards depending on players)

games.name: No Peek Poker
games.description: No Peek Poker is a variant of Indian Poker (also known as Blind Man's Bluff) where players hold their single card against their forehead without looking at it, so all other players can see it except themselves. It combines elements of poker betting with the unique mechanic of playing blind to your own card while seeing everyone else's.

games.name: Nobble
games.description: Nobble is a trick-taking card game where players compete to win tricks according to game rules. Players must manage cards and achieve scoring objectives through strategic play.

games.name: Noddy
games.description: Noddy is a 16th-century English card game and the direct ancestor of Cribbage. It is the oldest identifiable card game with the Cribbage gaming structure. Played with a distinctive board for scoring, it features the familiar combination of pegging, fifteens, pairs, runs, and flushes that would later be refined into modern Cribbage.

games.name: Nomination Whist
games.description: Nomination Whist (commonly known as Oh Hell!) is an exact-bidding trick-taking game where players must predict exactly how many tricks they will win. The game features a unique dealing pattern that goes 'up and down the river'â€”starting with 1 card each, increasing to the maximum, then decreasing back to 1. The scoring rewards exact bids with a 10-point bonus plus tricks taken.

games.name: Noms
games.description: Noms (Nomination Whist / Small Ships Rules) is a 4-player British trick-taking game with secret partnerships. Players bid from 10 upward, and the winner nominates a card to determine their secret partner (revealed when played). Features MisÃ¨re and MisÃ¨re Ouverte bids, and the unique rule that cards are NOT shuffled between handsâ€”only cut.

games.name: Nos
games.description: Nos is a Chilean Jass-type game related to the Austrian/Bavarian game Zehnern. It is a point-trick game where players aim to win tricks containing valuable cards, with special scoring for the last trick and specific card combinations.

games.name: Oh Hell
games.description: Oh Hell (also known as Oh Hell!) is a classic trick-taking card game that emphasizes precision bidding over raw power. Unlike most trick-takers where you try to win as many tricks as possible, the goal is to win exactly the number of tricks you bid. It is famous for its 'River' structure, where hand sizes increase and decrease throughout the game, and its 'Hook' rule that prevents every player from being successful simultaneously.

games.name: Oicho-Kabu
games.description: Oicho-Kabu is a traditional Japanese kabufuda gambling-card game played with the 40-card Kabufuda family, emphasizing value totals and betting decisions.

games.name: Okey
games.description: Okey is the quintessential Turkish tile game of the Rummy family. Played with 106 wooden or plastic tiles numbered 1-13 in four colors, players draw and discard to form sets and runs. A face-up indicator tile determines which tiles act as wild jokers. The first to complete a valid 14-tile hand wins the round.
games.deck: 106 tiles (1-13 in four colors, 8 each; 2 false jokers)

games.name: Okey 101
games.description: Okey 101 is a table-melding Okey variant in which players open with point thresholds and build sets and runs toward cumulative scoring targets.

games.name: Okey Turkish
games.description: Okey is the quintessential social game of Turkey, a tile-based Rummy variant played with 106 wooden or plastic tiles numbered 1-13 in four colors. A face-up indicator tile determines which tiles act as wild jokers. Players draw and discard to form sets and runs; the first to complete a valid 14-tile hand wins the round. Ubiquitous in Turkish kahvehanes (coffee houses).
games.deck: 106 tiles (1-13 in four colors, 8 each; 2 false jokers)

games.name: Oklahoma 10-point Pitch
games.description: Oklahoma Ten Point Pitch is a partnership trick-taking variant of Pitch using a 52-card deck plus two jokers. Points come from High, Low, Jack, Off-Jack, High Joker, Low Joker, Game, and optionally the Three of trumps. First team to 21 wins.

games.name: Old Maid
games.description: Old Maid is a timeless children's card game focused on matching and evasion. Using a standard deck with one card removed (or a specialized deck), players aim to pair up all their cards and discard them. The tension lies in the final unmatchable card—the 'Old Maid'. The player left with this card at the end of the game loses. It is a game of simple mechanics, bluffing, and luck.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (with 1 Queen removed) or dedicated Old Maid deck

games.name: Omaha
games.description: Omaha is a community-card poker variant where each player receives four hole cards and must use exactly two of them with exactly three of the five board cards to make their best five-card hand. The constraint makes hand-reading and drawing significantly different from Texas Hold'em.
alsoKnownAs: Omaha Hi-Lo Eight or Better Poker

games.name: Omben
games.description: Omben (Javanese) or Minuman (Indonesian)â€”both meaning 'drink'â€”is a two-player Go Fish variant from Indonesia. Players ask for ranks; the opponent gives all cards of that rank or the asker 'drinks' by drawing until they find one. First to discard all cards wins.

games.name: Omi
games.description: Omi is a Sri Lankan partnership plain-trick game of the Whist type. Four players in fixed partnerships bid trumps after seeing only their first four cards, then receive four more. Play is counter-clockwise. The 20 unused cards (2-6) serve as scoring tokens; the first team to collect 10 tokens wins.

games.name: One Arm Joe
games.description: One Arm Joe (One-Armed Pete) is a one-card variant of Indian Poker. Each player receives one card face-down, holds it to their forehead so everyone else can see it but they cannot, then bets. Highest card at showdown wins the pot. A game of pure deduction and bluff.

games.name: One Hundred
games.description: One Hundred (or Hundred) is a classic 'adding' card game where players collectively build a running total. The goal is simple: avoid being the person to push the count over 100. It is a game of mental arithmetic, risk management, and tactical use of special ability cards that can reverse, double, or reset the total.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (One or two decks depending on players)

games.name: One-Eyed Jack
games.description: One-Eyed Jack is a card-and-board game played in the Eastern USA. A 10x10 board has spaces corresponding to playing cards. Players use cards from hand to place chips on matching board spaces; the goal is to form rows of five chips. Two-eyed jacks (clubs, diamonds) are wildâ€”place a chip on any empty space. One-eyed jacks (hearts, spades) remove an opponent's chip from the board.
games.deck: Two standard 52-card packs (104 cards); board from second deck with jokers, jacks removed (50 spaces)

games.name: Open Face Chinese Poker (OFCP)
games.description: Open Face Chinese Poker is a partition game where players receive 13 cards over several rounds and place them face-up into three hands: Back (5), Middle (5), and Front (3). Hands must be in descending strength (Back â‰¥ Middle â‰¥ Front) or the player fouls. Players score by winning hand comparisons and earning royalties for premium hands. Fantasyland rewards QQ+ in Front with 13 cards dealt at once next hand.

games.name: Open Rummy
games.description: Open Rummy is an Indian partnership rummy game popular in Rajasthan and among Marwari families. Played with 3-4 standard decks plus printed jokers and sliding jokers (Twos). Players draw from an open discard pile (like 500 Rummy); only Aces and Threes can form equal-card groups. First team to 1,500 points wins.
games.deck: 3-4 standard 52-card decks plus 3 printed jokers per deck (220 cards for 4-player standard)

games.name: P'yanitsa (Russian Drunkard)
games.description: P'yanitsa (The Drunkard) is the most popular children's card game in Russia, acting as the Eastern European equivalent to the western game of 'War'. It is a game of pure chance and endurance where players aim to capture the entire deck. Its unique characteristic is the '6 beats Ace' rule, which prevents the highest card from being invincible. It is exceptionally simple, making it a staple of Russian childhood and social gatherings.

games.name: Paco
games.description: Paco is a Mexican gambling rummy closely related to Conquian. Players meld runs and identical-card sets, use forcing to block opponents, and pay the winner based on 'pay cards' (1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 12) melded. A massive 200-card deck made of five Spanish packs allows for sets of identical cards, a key departure from standard rummy.

games.name: Page One
games.description: Page One is a traditional Japanese card game that combines follow-suit trick-taking mechanics with a shedding objective. Players must follow the led suit or draw from the stock until they find a playable card. The game is known for its mandatory 'Page One!' declaration when a player is down to their final card, with failure to declare resulting in a severe five-card penalty.

games.name: Page One (Japanese)
games.description: Page One is a traditional Japanese shedding game where players must follow suit or draw until they can. It features a unique trick-taking loop where the objective is not to win tricks, but to empty your hand. The Joker acts as an invincible trump, and players must declare 'Page One!' when down to their final card to avoid heavy penalties.

games.name: Pai Gow
games.description: Pai Gow is an ancient Chinese gambling game played with a specialized set of thirty-two Chinese domino tiles. Each player is dealt four tiles which they must partition into two separate pairs: a high-ranking hand and a low-ranking hand. The objective is to outrank both of the banker's corresponding pairs, requiring deep knowledge of the complex and non-numeric tile ranking hierarchy.

games.name: Pai Gow Poker
games.description: Pai Gow Poker is a popular casino game that combines elements of the traditional Chinese game Pai Gow with American poker. Players are dealt seven cards and must divide them into a five-card high hand and a two-card low hand. The goal is to beat both of the dealer's corresponding hands, requiring strategic balancing of card strength between the two partitions.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck plus one Joker (53 total)

games.name: Pai Hong
games.description: PÃ¢i HÃ´ng à¹„à¸žà¹ˆà¸«à¹‰à¸­à¸‡ is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Paiute
games.description: Paiute is a Hawaiian draw-and-discard game similar to Knock Poker. Players draw and discard to form five- or six-card poker combinations. A turn-up card sets the wild rank. Unique: a player can call with a six-card hand (Three Pairs, called Paiute) on their first draw only.

games.name: Palace (Karma, Shed)
games.description: Palace is a shedding game with a three-layer setup: hand cards, face-up palace cards, and face-down cards. Play cards equal to or higher than the pile top; 2s reset, 10s burn the pile. Last player with cards loses.

games.name: Palatinusz Tarokk
games.description: Palatinusz (Illustrated) Tarokk is a Hungarian Tarokk variant from the 1920s. It adds six extra bonuses to Paskievics Tarokk. 4-5 players, 42-card tarot pack. Bidding, announcements (trull, centrum, birds, pagÃ¡t ultimÃ³), and trick play.

games.name: Pan (Polish)
games.description: Pan is a Polish shedding game with a 24-card pack. The 9 of hearts starts the play pile. Players play cards equal to or higher than the top, or pick up. Last player holding cards gets a letter (P-A-N); first to spell the word loses.

games.name: Pandoeren
games.description: Pandoeren is a Dutch trick-taking Jass game for four with variable partnerships and a wide choice of contracts. A 33-card pack is used. Declarer bids a contract (points, piccolo, misère, solo, etc.) and calls a partner via an ace or king.

games.name: Panguingue
games.description: Panguingue (Pan) is an American gambling rummy game popular in the Southwest. Played with eight 40-card decks (320 cards; 8sâ€“10s removed). Players meld sets and runs; first to meld 11 cards goes out. Conditions (valle cards, ace/king sets) earn immediate chip payouts.

games.name: Panjpar
games.description: Panjpar (Five Cards) is a two-player Afghan beating game related to Durak. Players attack with 1, 3, or 5 cards; the defender beats or picks up. Draw to five from stock. First to empty hand wins. Featured in Khaled Hosseini's The Kite Runner.

games.name: Papillon (French Fishing)
games.description: Papillon (Butterfly) is a classic French fishing-type card game, conceptually similar to Scopa but with its own distinct bonus system and 'Talon' (stock) mechanics. Players use cards from their hand to capture cards from the table, either by matching ranks or sums. It is beloved for its evocative bonus names ('Grasshopper', 'Little Beetle') and its emphasis on being the first to 'fly away' by emptying one's hand. It is primarily a game of observation and tactical capturing.

games.name: Partner Dominoes Jamaican
games.description: Jamaican Partner Dominoes is the Jamaican variant of Latin Partnership Dominoes. Four players in partnerships, double-six set, all tiles dealt. Same base rules as Partnership Dominoes with Jamaican/ Caribbean conventions.

games.name: Partnership Dominoes
games.description: Partnership Dominoes is a four-player line domino game. All 28 tiles are dealt, seven each. Partners sit opposite. The double-six tile leads first; the match ends by playing out or by block. First team to 100 wins.

games.name: Partnership Okey
games.description: Partnership Okey is a team variant of Okey where opposite players cooperate through discard signaling and shared outcome scoring.

games.name: Pas Seul
games.description: Pas Seul is a Klondike-variant patience game for one player. Only one pass through the deck is allowed. Build from Aces to Kings in suit on four foundations; six tableau piles build down in alternating colors. Turn cards from stock to waste; only the top card of the waste is playable. The name refers to a dance sequence for one person.

games.name: Paskahousu
games.description: Paskahousu (Finnish for 'shit pants') is a Finnish shedding game related to Shithead. Play cards equal or higher than the pile; 2s, 10s, and Aces have special effects. Last player with cards loses.

games.name: Paskievics Tarokk
games.description: Paskievics Tarokk is a 4-player Hungarian tarot game. Partners chosen by calling the XX. Objectives include catching the XXI, pagÃ¡t ultimo (last trick with tarokk I), trull, and point scoring. Base game for Palatinusz (Illustrated) Tarokk.

games.name: Pass the Trash
games.description: Pass the Trash is a stud poker variant in which each player receives seven cards, posts antes, and after a betting round passes three unwanted cards to the next active player to the left. After a second betting round players discard two cards, order the remaining five face down, then reveal them one at a time with betting between each reveal. The highest five-card hand at showdown wins the pot.

games.name: Passing Dominoes
games.description: Passing Dominoes is a variant of Draw Dominoes in which players may pass instead of playing or drawing. Play to the train; lowest pip total wins the hand. First to 101 (2p/partnership) or 61 (3-4p) wins.

games.name: Paston
games.description: Paston is a highly localized and strategically deep trick-taking game played primarily in Armenia and the Armenian diaspora. Played by three players with a 32-card deck, it belongs to the family of games like Preferans and Belote. The game is known for its unique suit terminology (e.g., 'Paston' for Spades) and the 'Prikup' (two face-down cards given to the declarer). It is a game of skill, involving intense bidding for the right to name the trump suit and reach a target score of 121.

games.name: Paston
games.description: Paston (Armenian for 'spades') is a 3-player Preference-style trick game from Gyumri, Armenia. 32 cards, prikup, bidding (paston = spades). Declarer chooses trump, must take at least 6 tricks or surrender.

games.name: Pasur
games.description: Pasur is an Iranian fishing game where captures are made by exact rank pairing or by making sums of 11. Players score for aces, jacks, key cards, most clubs, and table-clearing surs, racing to 62 points.

games.name: Paublillo
games.description: Paublillo is a Colombian trick-taking game from Tolima. 2-8 players (best 6), 40-card Spanish deck. Three-card hands, betting; win at least two of three tricks. Trump 4 (monja) and 3 (paublillo) are special. 12 stones to win.

games.name: Pawnee Pitch
games.description: Pawnee Pitch is a call-partner Pitch variant. Four players bid for trump; high bidder calls for a partner (by naming a card). Play follows standard Pitch: high, low, jack, game. First team to 10 points wins.

games.name: Pedro
games.description: Pedro (Cinch, High Five) is an American Pitch variant. The trump 5 (pedro) and the other 5 of same colour (low pedro) are each worth 5 points. 4p partnerships, 9 cards each, bidding 7-14. Discard non-trumps, refill to 6. First to 62 wins.

games.name: Pedro Sancho
games.description: Pedro variant (also called Nine-Five) for four to seven players. Six cards each; one round of bidding (0–18). High bidder names trumps; the 5 (pedro) and 9 (sancho) of that suit score 5 and 9 points. First to 100 wins. Bidder must lead trump; follow suit when trump is led.

games.name: Peeso (Estonian Horns)
games.description: Peeso is a popular Estonian social game, often described as a regional folk variant of the game '6 nimmt!'. Players simultaneous play cards into four rows on the table, following strict rules of ascending order and 'smallest difference'. If a player is forced to place the 6th card in a row, they must take the entire row as penalty points (called 'Sarved' or Horns). It is a game of risk management, psychological anticipation, and avoidant scoring.
games.deck: Specialized numbered deck (1-104), or standard cards modified

games.name: Pegs and Jokers
games.description: Pegs and Jokers is a highly social, strategic board-and-card hybrid game, often described as 'Pachisi on steroids'. Players or teams race to move their pegs around a physical board (often made of interlocking wooden segments) using cards instead of dice. The game is famous for its 'Mean' mechanics, particularly the Joker, which allows a player to swap positions with an opponent, potentially undoing dozens of moves in a single turn. It is a staple of RV communities and family gathering 'Game Nights'.
games.deck: Multiple 52-card decks (1 deck per 2 players) + Jokers

games.name: Pegs and Jokers
games.description: Pegs and Jokers is a North American partnership race game. Cards move pegs (or marbles) around a board. 4, 6, or 8 players; each player has 5 pegs. First team to move all pegs from START to HOME wins. Derived from Pachisi/Sorry.

games.name: Pei
games.description: Pei is a Ceki-family game that uses the same money-card deck structure and combination play found across Peranakan communities.

games.name: Pelmanism
games.description: Pelmanism is a simple memory game in which players turn over two cards at a time from a face-down layout to find matching pairs. Also known as Concentration or Memory; in Japan as Shinkei-suijaku. The British name comes from the Pelman Institute (London, 1899).

games.name: Pelmanism (Concentration)
games.description: Pelmanism (known globally as Concentration, Memory, or Shinkei-suijaku in Japan) is the definitive card game for testing visualization and spatial memory. Played with a standard 52-card deck spread face-down, players take turns flipping two cards to find matches. It is a universal game played by all ages, from toddlers to memory champions, and serves as the foundation for countless themed 'Memory' games.

games.name: Penneech
games.description: Penneech is a 17th-century British 2-player trick game. Trump changes each trick (turned from stock). The 7â™¦ (Peneech) is highest when diamonds are trump and scores 7. Ace/K/Q/J of trumps score 5/4/3/2. First to 61 wins.

games.name: Pennies from Heaven
games.description: Pennies from Heaven is a Hand and Foot Canasta variant. 6 players, 4 packs+8 jokers. Four canasta types: natural(500), mixed(300), wild(1000), sevens(1500). Draw 2 per turn. Must complete one of each canasta type to go out. 13 hand + 11 face-down foot. 20,000 to win.

games.name: Pepper
games.description: Pepper is a Bid Euchre variant from Iowa and Ohio. 24 cards (9-A), right/left bowers. Bid 1-5, little pepper (6), or big pepper (6, doubled stakes). 4p partnerships, 6 cards each.

games.name: Perevodnoy Durak
games.description: Perevodnoy Durak (Transfer Fool) is a Durak variant where the defender can transfer the attack to the next player by playing a card of the same rank. Otherwise like Podkidnoy Durak: 36 cards, attack/defend, last with cards = Fool. Works well with 2 players.

games.name: Perlaggen
games.description: Perlaggen is a card game card game that involves gameplay, scoring, strategy. The game originated in Various and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Perudo (Card Variant)
games.description: Perudo (also known as Liar's Dice when played with dice) is a world-famous game of bluffing, probability, and nerve. This card-based adaptation replaces the dice cups with hidden hands of cards. Players must guess how many cards of a certain rank (e.g., 'Five Kings') are held collectively by everyone at the table. It is a game of extreme deception where you can win with the worst hand if you can successfully convince others you have the best.

games.name: Petit Paquet
games.description: Petit Paquet (also known as 'Turkish Packets' or 'Paquets Turcs') is an 18th-century French game of pure chance and high-stakes gambling. It pits a single 'Banker' against a group of players. The game is played with several small piles (packets) of face-down cards. Players bet on specific piles, and the top cards are revealed one by one. It is a precursor to modern casino games like Baccarat and Pharaoh, known for its elegant simplicity and rapid wealth transfer.

games.name: Petrangola
games.description: Petrangola is a card game from the Italian provinces of Marche and Romagna, also known as 31. Players have three cards each and improve their hands by exchanging with three face-up table cards; aim is high total in one suit (max 31) or a petrangola (three equal or three of a suit in sequence).

games.name: Petteia
games.description: Petteia (also known as Poleis or 'Cities') is an ancient Greek board game of pure strategy and military logic. Featured in the writings of Plato and Aristotle, it is one of the world's first 'Pure Reason' games, containing no elements of chance. Players command 'Stones' on a grid, attempting to capture the opponent's forces by surrounding them from two sides (Custodian Capture). It is the direct ancestor of the Roman 'Ludus Latrunculorum' and is celebrated as a training tool for soldiers and philosophers alike.

games.name: Pick a Partner Poker
games.description: Pick a Partner is a stud poker variant for an even number of players. Everyone antes and receives five cards face down. All players simultaneously expose one card (roll). The highest card holder picks a partner; then the highest unpartnered player picks, until all are paired. Each partnership combines their eight remaining cards and selects three to use with their two upcards to form a five-card hand. Three betting rounds follow, with one of the three chosen cards turned face up after each round. Partners bet as individuals; the team with the best hand shares the pot, or one partner wins the whole pot if the other folded.

games.name: Piedicavallo Tarocchi
games.description: Piedicavallo Tarocchi is a rare and highly localized variant of Italian Tarot played exclusively in the Valle Cervo of the Piedmont region. It uses a modified 62-card 'Tarocco Piemontese' deck. The game is famous for its 'Open Communication' system, where partners are legally allowed to speak to each other and signal their cards (using taps and code words) as long as the information is audible to the opponents. It is a game of deep tactical coordination, memory, and traditional heritage.

games.name: Pig
games.description: Pig is a chaotic, high-energy reaction game that turns a standard deck of cards into a test of observation and speed. Played without turns, players rapidly pass cards in a circle to collect a four-of-a-kind. The game's defining feature is the 'Stupid Pose': as soon as one player completes their set and discreetly touches their nose, everyone else must follow suit. The last person to react is the 'Pig' and loses the round. It is a close relative of the game 'Spoons'.

games.name: Pig
games.description: Pig is a simple collecting card game of American origin in which players pass one card at a time to the left and try to collect four cards of the same rank; the first to get four of a kind touches their nose and the last to do so loses the deal. Often played with three lives (letters P-I-G) or as Spoons using tokens.

games.name: Pilotta
games.description: Pilotta is a Greek point-trick game of the Jass family, popular in Cyprus. Similar to Belote. 4 players in partnerships. Ace-ten scoring. Ioannis Zapitis published rules; WebPilotta available at gamesfair.com.

games.name: Pinochle
games.description: Pinochle is a classic card game that combines two distinct phases: **melding** (showing combinations of cards for points) and **trick-taking** (winning individual tricks to score additional points). Played with a unique 48-card deck containing two copies of each card from 9 to Ace, Pinochle offers deep strategic gameplay centered around the auction/bidding phase where players compete to name the trump suit.

games.name: Pinochle Double Deck
games.description: Partnership trick-and-meld game for four players using two 40-card pinochle packs (80 cards, nines removed). Bid to name trump, meld for points, then play 20 tricks; first team to reach the target score (e.g. 1500) wins.

games.name: Pinochle Single Deck Partnership
games.description: Pinochle with single 48-card deck; four players in partnerships. Melding and trick-taking.

games.name: Pinochle Three Player
games.description: Three-player Pinochle: each plays for themselves. Deal 15 cards each and a 3-card kitty. Auction to name trump (min 20, or 19 for dealer); high bidder takes the kitty, declares trump, and all meld. Fifteen tricks; follow suit, trump when void. First to 100 points wins. Must take at least one trick to count meld; fail contract costs the bid amount.

games.name: Pinochle Two Player
games.description: Pinochle for two players. Melding and trick-taking with 48-card deck; two-player rules (e.g. dummy hand or special deal).

games.name: Pip-Pip
games.description: Pip-Pip is an English Marriage game for 4-10 players. Each marriage sets a new trump (like 1000, Marjapussi). Two packs (104 cards). 7 cards each; draw after each trick. Point values: 2=11, A=10, K/Q/J=5/4/3. All marriages score 50.

games.name: Piquet
games.description: Piquet is one of the oldest, most sophisticated, and strategically deep card games in Western history. Originating in France as a game for the nobility, it is a two-player trick-taking and melding game played with a 32-card deck. It is celebrated for its 'Rubicon' scoring system and the delicate balance between the 'Elder' and 'Younger' hands. It is a game of skill, psychological maneuvering, and card-counting that has remained unchanged for over 500 years.

games.name: Piquet
games.description: Piquet is a classic 2-player game with 32 cards (7-A). 12 each, 8 talon. Exchange, declarations (Point, Sequence, Set), then tricks (no trump). Partie = 6 deals. Rubicon: loser <100 pays sum+100; loser â‰¥100 pays difference+100.

games.name: Pirate's Bridge
games.description: Pirate's Bridge is a fascinating and revolutionary variant of Bridge that replaces 'Fixed Partnerships' with a dynamic, shifting alliance system. Conceived by R.F. Foster and popularized by Aleister Crowley, it allows players to choose their partner for each specific hand based on the bidding. This removes the 'Bad Partner' frustration of standard Bridge and introduces a layer of individual competition. It is Bridge with an 'Every Player for Themselves' mentality.

games.name: Pishe Pasha
games.description: Pishe Pasha is a two-player competitive patience game played in Jewish communities in North America since at least the mid-twentieth century. Each player has a face-down stock of 26 cards. Players get rid of cards by building foundation piles (Ace through King in each suit) or by playing onto the opponent's discard pile (next higher or lower rank). The first to empty their stock and discard wins.

games.name: Pişti
games.description: Pişti (pronounced 'Pish-tee') is one of the most beloved card games in Turkey. It is a fishing game where players capture cards from a central pile by matching ranks or playing a Jack (which captures any pile). The name means 'cooked' and refers to the pişti bonus: capturing a single card with a matching rank scores 10 extra points. Fast-paced, with observation and memory.

games.name: Pitch
games.description: Pitch is a card game card game that involves gameplay, scoring, strategy. The game originated in Various and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Pitch with Fives
games.description: Pitch with Fives (Catch Five) is a Pitch variant with only one scoring five: the trump 5 (5 points). Nine points total per hand: high, low, jack, game, five. 4p partnerships, 6 cards, purge non-trumps, refill. Must follow suit. 31 to win.

games.name: Pitty Pat
games.description: Pitty Pat is a rummy-like game from Belize. Object: make three pairs. No melding to table; players collect pairs in hand. Draw one, discard one. First to show three pairs wins. Simple, fast.

games.name: Pizzichino
games.description: Pizzichino (Spizzichino) is Tressette for two. 40-card Italian pack. 10 hand + 2 packets of 5 (only top visible). Play from hand or top of packet. Buongiochi (honours: 4Ã—3/2/A, 3Ã—3/2/A, Napoletana) score extra. 51 to win. Alternately: a MetÃ  Mazzo (10 each, draw from monte after trick).

games.name: Plait Solitaire
games.description: Plait Solitaire (also known as 'Plaits' or 'The Braid') is a double-deck solitaire game of significant complexity and visual appeal. It is distinguished by the 'Plait'â€”a central reserve of 13 cards arranged in a braid-like pattern, where only specific cards are accessible at any time. Requiring the player to manage two sets of foundations and eight tableau piles, it is a game of foresight, sequence planning, and careful reserve management.

games.name: Plus-Minus Jass
games.description: Plus-Minus Jass is a Swiss Jass variant for 3 or 4 players. Cards are dealt equally and played as in Mittlere or Molotow. Scoring is by sticks only (no potatoes). The first player to score 7 sticks wins. If everyone scores under 100 card points, the players with most and least points each score one stick; if someone takes 100 or more, only the player with least points scores a stick.

games.name: Poch
games.description: Poch is a 500-year-old German game with a special board. Three stages: (1) Pay suitâ€”A/K/Q/J/10, Marriage, Sequenceâ€”collect from pools. (2) Pochenâ€”bet on best pair/triple/quartet. (3) Stopsâ€”play cards in sequence; first out wins centre pot. 3-6 players, 32 cards.

games.name: Poch (Pochen)
games.description: Poch (or Pochen) is an ancient German family game documented as far back as 1441. It is widely recognized as one of the primary ancestors of modern Poker, particularly for its 'Pochen' (vying or betting) phase. Played with a specialized board (Pochbrett), it combines elements of luck, betting, and strategic card-shedding. It is a 'Three-in-One' game where a single deal is used to play three distinct sub-games, rewarded by different portions of a central pot.
games.deck: 32-card German or Piquet deck (7s to Aces)

games.name: Podkidnoy Durak (Durak Podkidnoy)
games.description: Podkidnoy Durak (historically translated as 'Throw-in Fool') is the most popular and strategically intense variant of the traditional Russian game Durak. Unlike the basic variant where an attack consists of a single card, Podkidnoy allows all other players to 'Throw In' cards that match the rank of any attacking or defending card on the table. It is a game of shifting alliances, brutal resource management, and the unique goal of simply NOT being the loser.

games.name: Podrida
games.description: La Podrida is the Spanish/Latin American equivalent of Oh Hell!. Exact bidding: predict tricks. Key difference: if you cannot follow suit you must play a trump. 'Podrida' = putrid; spoiling others' contracts by giving too many or too few tricks. Argentina, Mexico variants.

games.name: Point Tarock
games.description: Point Tarock is a three-player Austrian tarock game in the Industrie und Glueck family. It is closely related to Tapp Tarock but adds announcement and scoring emphasis around point capture and contract value.

games.name: Poker Bull
games.description: Poker Bull is an Indian Poker variant in which each player is dealt one card and holds it to their forehead without looking, so others can see it. Players ante and bet in a round of poker; highest card at showdown wins the pot (ties split). In the bull variant, highest and lowest cards share the pot.

games.name: Pokerize
games.description: Pokerize is a rummy variant in which play follows basic draw-and-discard rummy (draw one, meld sets or runs, lay off on melds, discard one) and the result or scoring is interpreted using standard poker hand rankings (high card, pair, two pair, flush, full house, etc.).

games.name: Polignac
games.description: Polignac (also known as 'Jacks') is a classic French trick-avoidance game, a direct ancestor to modern games like Hearts. Played with a 32-card deck, the objective is to avoid capturing any Jacks, particularly the Jack of Spades, which is the 'Polignac'. It is a game of simplicity and social penalty, often played in French cafes as a quick gamble or a penalty game where the loser 'treats' the table.

games.name: Polignac
games.description: Polignac is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Polish Bank
games.description: Polish Bank (also simply known as 'Bank' or the 'Russian' variation) is an intense, high-stakes comparing game purely designed for gambling. It belongs to the same family of games as 'Red Dog' and 'Slippery Sam'. Players bet against a central pool that they hold a higher card of a specific suit than a revealed target. It is known for its strict 'Blind Betting' rules, where touching your cards before wagering is a penalized offense.

games.name: Polish Red Dog
