games.description: Banking game: players bet without seeing their cards or the dealer's card that they hold a same-suit card higher than the dealer's upcard; winner is paid twice the bet from the pot. Also Stitch, Polski Pachuck.

games.name: Pollack
games.description: Pollack is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Pontoon
games.description: Pontoon is the British version of Twenty-one; players buy or twist cards aiming for 21 or less, beating the banker without going bust.

games.name: Pope Joan
games.description: Pope Joan is a quintessentially English historical card game that was immensely popular in the 18th and 19th centuries. A 'Stops' game played with a specialized rotating board, it blends sequence-building with 'Lucky Card' rewards. The game centers on the 'Pope Joan' cardâ€”the Nine of Diamondsâ€”which serves as a permanent wild card. It is a game of social interaction, anticipation, and the thrill of clearing a 'Stakes' board.

games.name: Porrazo
games.description: Porrazo (Parosso, Parear) is a fishing game from Mexico/Southwest USA. Play a card; if it matches a table card, capture it and any cards in ascending sequence. Matching the previous player's card = porrazo (bonus). First to 61 wins.

games.name: Pöytäpaska
games.description: Pöytäpaska (Spanish Shitpants) is a Finnish beating game variant where players have face-up and face-down cards on the table in addition to their hand. The goal is to get rid of all cards: hand cards first, then face-up table cards, then face-down cards.

games.name: Prefa
games.description: Prefa is the Greek form of Preference. 3 players, 32-card pack. Like Russian Preference: bidder can contract for more than 6 tricks. Trick-taking with bidding, talon, and declarer play. Eric Ball, Prefadoros, Thanos program.

games.name: Preferans
games.description: Preferans (derived from the French 'PrÃ©fÃ©rence') is the quintessential card game of the Russian intelligentsia and one of the most intellectually demanding games in existence. Played by 3 or 4 players with a 32-card deck, it is a bidding-based trick-taking game where players compete for contracts, including the dreaded 'Misere' (taking zero tricks). It is famous for its complex 'Pula' (pool) scoring system involving 'Bullets', 'Whists', and 'Mountains', making it a game of long-term strategy and cold mathematical calculation.

games.name: Preferans Russian
games.description: Preferans Russian is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Preferánsz Donauschwaben
games.description: PreferÃ¡nsz Donauschwaben is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Preference
games.description: Preference is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: President
games.description: President is a card game card game that involves gameplay, scoring, strategy. The game originated in Various and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Price is Right, The Poker
games.description: Price is Right Poker is an American poker variant themed on the TV game show. Players use a standard 52-card deck and standard poker hand rankings; gameplay combines hand-building with guessing or bidding on prices. Two to six players compete to form the best hand.

games.name: Primero
games.description: Primero is a 16th-century Italian vying/showdown game. Players receive four cards. The prime (one card of each suit) gives the game its name. Card values: 7=21, 6=18, A=16, 5=15, 4=14, 3=13, 2=12, pictures=10. Reconstructions by Mark Waks, Jeff Suzuki; Berni and Cardano described variants.

games.name: Primiera
games.description: Primiera (often confused with the related Spanish 'Primero') is a prestigious 16th-century Italian card game that is mathematically and strategically recognized as a direct ancestor of modern Poker. It is a betting and card-comparing game where players aim to form combinations from a 4-card hand. Known for its unique 'Primiera' combination (one card of each suit) and its high-stakes 'Vying' (betting) system, it was a game of status and intellect across Renaissance Europe.

games.name: Prostoy Durak
games.description: Prostoy Durak (Simple Fool) is a Durak variant with 5-card hands. Attacker plays 1, 3, or 5 cards (single; pair+1; two pairs+1 or four+1). Defender beats each or picks up. No throwing-in. 36 cards. Last with cards = Fool. Poland: DureÅ„ PiÄ…tkowy.

games.name: Proter
games.description: Proter is a card game commonly played with 2-6 using 52 cards. The core rules emphasize variant-specific tactical timing, legal action sequencing, and scoring control.

games.name: Psycho Poker
games.description: Psycho Poker is a poker variant in which players wager over which hand is best according to the game's rules, with psychological or unusual rule twists typical of home-game variants. Standard poker hand rankings apply.

games.name: Púkk
games.description: Púkk (often spelled 'Pukk') is a traditional Icelandic card game that belongs to the ancient 'Poch' family. It involves a unique betting layout (traditionally a series of dishes or a special mat) and three distinct phases of play: Dressing the Board, Vying (the 'Púkk' phase), and Shedding (the 'Play' phase). It is famous for its 'Pamfíll' (Jack of Clubs) which acts as a powerful wild card. Púkk is a game of social interaction, bluffing, and sequence-building that has been an Icelandic family staple for centuries.

games.name: Pulle Dominoes
games.description: Pulle is a four-player block domino game from Austria using a double-8 set of 36 tiles (doubles removed). Players contribute an equal stake to the pool (Pulle). Each round, unplayed pip counts are added to running scores; players exceeding 100 are eliminated. Last survivor wins the pool. Buy-back and broken-pool rules apply.
games.deck: Double-8 domino set of 36 tiles (nine doubles removed).

games.name: Push Poker
games.description: Push is a five-card stud poker variant in which players may pay an agreed price to reject an upcard offered by the dealer and receive the next card from the deck instead. Four rounds of card-offer and pushing are followed by betting; highest hand wins.

games.name: Put
games.description: Put is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Pyramid
games.description: Pyramid is a poker card game that involves betting, hand rankings, bluffing. The game originated in USA and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Pyramide
games.description: Pyramide (The Pyramid) is a popular French social card game, often played in festive or party settings. It is a game of memory, deduction, and high-stakes bluffing. Players are dealt a private hand of cards which they must mÃ©morise and then place face-down. A central 'Pyramid' of cards is then revealed layer-by-layer. If a player claims to have a card matching a revealed one, they can penalize an opponentâ€”but if they're caught bluffing, the penalty is doubled. It is a game of 'Who can keep a poker face while forgetting their own hand?'

games.name: QiuQiu
games.description: QiuQiu is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Quadrille
games.description: Quadrille is a four-player trick-taking game adapted from the Spanish Ombre. The winner of the bidding becomes Hombre, names trump, and may call a King for a partner. The declarer aims to win six of ten tricks using a 40-card pack with inverted red-suit ranking and special matadors (Spadille, Manille, Basta).

games.name: Quan Dui
games.description: Quan Dui (全對, translating to 'Complete Pairs') is a traditional Rummy-style game from Southern China, primarily played with 'Dong Guan Pai' (Chinese Money Cards) or occasionally Mahjong tiles. The goal is to collect exactly eight pairs to win the round. It is a game of high priority claiming, where certain combinations (identical 'True Pairs') allow players to jump the turn order. It is deeply rooted in Cantonese gambling culture.

games.name: Quan Dui
games.description: Quan Dui (Quán Duì 全對) means "complete pairs". It is a simple Rummy-like draw-and-discard game played with Chinese money cards (Dongguan Pai). The object is to collect a 16-card hand of eight pairs; identical pairs (dui) or same-number different-suit pairs (ka). Played in Dongguan, Guangdong, China; observed in Chinese clubs abroad.

games.name: Quartett
games.description: Quartett is a German and Austrian matching game where players collect complete quartets (families of four cards) by asking others for specific cards. You must hold at least one card of the quartet to ask. If the asked player has it, they give it and you continue; if not, they say 'not at home' and their turn begins.
games.origin: Germany / Austria (from British Happy Families, mid-19th century)

games.name: Quatre Sept
games.description: Quatre Sept is a French-Canadian four-player partnership point-trick game with no trumps, descended from Italian Tressette. Players use a 32-card pack (10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7). Holding all four sevens wins the game immediately; winning three consecutive tricks with 10-9-A of a suit (La Politaine) scores an 11-point bonus.

games.name: Quatre Valets
games.description: Quatre Valets (Four Jacks), also widely known as Polignac or 'The Jacks Game', is a classic French trick-avoidance game. It is the direct ancestor to the modern Hearts family. Players compete to be the one taking the FEWEST Jacks in their captured tricks. The Jack of Spades (known as the Polignac) is the most heavily penalized card. It is a game of cautious leading, suit-bleeding, and protective play where every trick is a potential trap.

games.name: Quebec Rummy
games.description: Quebec Rummy (Rami QuÃ©bÃ©cois) is a regional variation of Contract Rummy played extensively in French-speaking Canada. It is characterized by its specific sequence of 7 or 11 rounds of 'Contracts' and its unique rules regarding 'Buying' from the discard pile (The 'Pige'). Like other contract variants, players must fulfill exactly what the round calls forâ€”sets or runsâ€”before they can expand their melds. It is a social game often played at family dinners (les grandes tablÃ©es) with multiple decks to accommodate large groups.
games.deck: Two decks of 52 cards plus 4 Jokers

games.name: Queen's Slipper 500
games.description: Queen's Slipper 500 is the definitive Australian version of the card game 500, played using specialized decks produced by the iconic Queen's Slipper brand. While standard 500 exists, the Australian variant is unique for its use of 11s, 12s, and 13s, allowing for 4, 5, or even 6-player games with expanded decks. It is a trick-taking game that evolved from Euchre, featuring a complex bidding system, the 'MisÃ¨re' (no-trick) contract, and the inclusion of a Joker as the ultimate trump card.

games.name: Quinientos
games.description: Quinientos (500) is a rummy-style card game played to 500 points with matching and scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Racehorse Pitch
games.description: Racehorse Pitch is a Pitch variant where the dealer bids and leads; players race to reach the target (e.g. 21) with bid and trump mechanics as in Pitch. High-Low-Jack-Game scoring. See Pitch for base rules.

games.name: Racing Demon
games.description: Racing Demon is a patience card game that involves tableau, foundations, stock. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: RÄƒzboi
games.description: RÄƒzboi (Romanian for 'War') is a classic, high-energy card game of chance played primarily by children and families in Romania. While globally known as 'War', the Romanian variant features specific point-values for face cards (often treated as 10s) and a unique 'Escalation' rule for ties, where the number of cards laid down during a conflict depends on the rank of the card that triggered the war. It is a game of pure persistence and endurance.

games.name: Rainbow
games.description: Rainbow is a vibrant, strategic card game that focuses on completing a spectrum of colors while avoiding 'Clouds'. Players place cards into a shared central line to build a six-color rainbow. It is a game of careful hand management and risk assessment: if you add a duplicate color or a cloud card to the line, you are forced to collect all the cards currently on the table (which is bad for scoring). The winner is the player who collects the most 'Natural' rainbows or the fewest penalty cards, depending on the variant.
games.deck: Specialized color deck (Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Violet + Wilds/Clouds)

games.name: Ramchi
games.description: Ramchi is a partition card game for 3 players. Each player forms up to five combinations of three cards (trips, straight flush, straight, flush, unrelated). Players compete round by round; winner of round N wins N chips from each opponent. Four of a kind wins the hand immediately. Target: most chips.
games.origin: Pakistan (popular among Afghan refugee communities); variant of Afghan Chor Voli

games.name: Ramino Pokerato
games.description: Ramino Pokerato is an Italian Rummy game that combines draw-and-discard melding with poker-style betting. Players receive 10 cards from a double deck with four Jokers; after an optional blind and betting round, play proceeds with draw from stock or discard, then discard, until a player goes out by melding 10 cards in sets and runs and discarding the 11th.
games.deck: Double deck of 52 cards plus four Jokers (108 cards).

games.name: Ramsli
games.description: Ramsli is a Hungarian trick-taking game related to French Rams and Croatian Raub. 4-card hands. Donauschwaben (German Danube settlers) version documented by Rick Heli. Declarer vs defenders; bidding; trump.

games.name: Rang Milanti
games.description: Rang Milanti (Bengali for 'Suit Matching') is a spirited children's game from Bengal that is part of the 'War' and 'Slap' family of card games. Unlike Western War which compares rank, Rang Milanti is purely about the visual recognition of suits. Players race to match the suit of the previously played card to claim the entire central pot. It is a game of luck, speed, and endurance, often used to introduce young children to the four suits of a standard deck.

games.name: Rangoon
games.description: Rangoon (Rangoon Gaps) is a solitaire card game. Four rows of 13 cards with a gap in front of each. Move cards to gaps: a card may move only if it matches suit and is one rank lower than the card in front of the gap. Kings move to front gap. Goal: each row is one suit in order.

games.name: RÃºssi
games.description: RÃºssi (Icelandic for 'Russian') is a unique and strategic two-player variation of Whist played in Iceland. It distinguishes itself from standard 'Russian Whist' (Vint) by its hybrid layout: players have cards in their hand AND a collection of face-up and face-down cards on the table. It is a game of information asymmetry, where winning depends on managing visible threats and uncovering your own hidden resources.

games.name: Raub
games.description: Raub is a Croatan trick-taking game. 2-4 players. 32 cards (7-A). Declarer must make at least 2 of 4 tricks; each defender must make 1 or drop. Dealer can say 'Raub' (take face-up trump, make 2) or 'Trick' (7 up, make 1). Bidding: 'I lead'. Refusal (Refa) doubles next. Start 21; lose points for failures.

games.name: Razz
games.description: Razz is 7-Card Stud played for low. A-5 lowball: Aces are low; straights and flushes don't count; best hand is 5-4-3-2-A (the wheel). Betting as in Stud. Fixed-limit or spread-limit. Popular in HORSE.

games.name: Red Dog High Card Pool
games.description: Red Dog High Card Pool is a one-card Indian Poker variant. Each player is dealt one card and holds it to the forehead without looking, so opponents can see it. After a round of poker betting, the highest card among those who stayed in wins the pot; ties split the pot.

games.name: Reversis
games.description: Reversis is an ancestor of Hearts from around 1600, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries. Trick avoidance: avoid taking penalty cards (hearts, queen of spades). David Parlett documents rules and history.

games.name: Rikken
games.description: Rikken is a trick-taking game from the Netherlands and Belgium. Four players; 52 cards (2 low to A high). Multiple contracts: Rik (8 tricks with called Ace partner), Rik Beter (hearts trump), 8-13 Alleen (solo), MisÃ¨re, Piek (exactly 1 trick). Cards never shuffled between hands.

games.name: Ristiklappi
games.description: Ristiklappi (Ristikontra variant) is a Finnish Sedma-group game for 4 in partnerships. Tricks won by last card of same rank as led. 5 cards each; stock. Point cards: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2. 'Clean' rule: if team took a queen before stock empty, must later win a trick with a king (not won by queen) to clean. First to 7 game points wins.

games.name: Ristikontra
games.description: Ristikontra is a Finnish Sedma-group game for 4 in partnerships. Tricks won by the last card of same rank as led (no suit hierarchy). 6 cards each; stock. Point cards: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2 (120 total). 61+ points = 1 game point. First to 7 wins. May play top stock 'in the dark'.

games.name: Rıfkı
games.description: Rıfkı (also known as Turkish King) is a compendium trick-taking game for four players, widely played in Turkey. It is the Turkish variation of King (Barbu). Twenty hands are played; each player declares five contracts (two trump, three negative). Rıfkı refers to the King of Heartsâ€”which scores -320 to the player who wins it in that contract.

games.name: Roll Your Own Poker
games.description: Roll Your Own is a strategic 'style' of Stud Poker (most commonly Seven-Card Stud) where the dealer provides cards face-down, and players choose which ones to reveal to their opponents. This shifts the game from a test of luck into a nuanced game of information management and bluffing. 'Dakota' is a specific high-low variation of this style featuring personal wild cards based on the lowest hidden card.

games.name: Ronda
games.description: Ronda is a Moroccan fishing game played with a 40-card Spanish pack. Players capture cards by playing matching ranks or ascending sequences. Ronda (pair) and Tringa (three of a kind) announced at deal score 1 and 5 pts. Este/caida (matching last played) scores 1-11. Target 41.

games.name: Rook
games.description: Point-trick family using the Rook deck: four colors (black, red, green, yellow), ranks 1–14 per color plus the Rook bird card. Popular in Mennonite communities and Eastern Kentucky. This entry models the common form: four in fixed partnerships, bid for nest and trump, first team to 500 wins.
games.deck: Rook 56-card deck (four colors 1–14 plus Rook bird card)

games.name: Roppyakken
games.description: Roppyakken is a Hanafuda game where players race to reach a cumulative point target, typically 600, by capturing month cards and scoring combinations.

games.name: Round the World Poker
games.description: Round the World Poker is a poker variant in which the required hand to win changes each deal: the first deal is won by high card, the second by pair, then two pair, three of a kind, and so on up through royal flush. Each deal is played like five-card draw with betting; only the hand type that wins the pot changes round by round.

games.name: Royal Casino
games.description: Royal Casino is Casino with picture cards having numerical values: Jacks 11, Queens 12, Kings 13, Aces 1 or 14. Players capture cards from a layout by matching number or sum. Dominican version: 4 cards each, 4 face up on table; capture, build, or trail. Target 21. Counter-clockwise.

games.name: Rubamazzo
games.description: Rubamazzo (Steal The Pile) is an Italian Scopa-style fishing game. 40-card pack. Capture table cards by matching value or sum. Must capture if possible. Sweep (scopa) = take all from table. Multiple deck styles (Bergamo, Neapolitan, etc.). Fast-paced; strategy and basic math.

games.name: Ruff and Honours
games.description: Ruff and Honours was a 17th-century English ancestor of Whist. Trick-taking with trump and honours. Reconstructions at WAKS Medieval Games, TrapApps online.

games.name: Rufmariasch
games.description: Rufmariasch is an Austrian four-player Mariage variant. 32-card German pack (hearts, bells, acorns, leaves). Bidder calls a card (Ace or King) to choose partner. Aces, tens, last trick = 10 pts. King+Over (Queen) = mariage: 40 trumps, 20 other. Point-trick with called partner.

games.name: Rummikub
games.description: Tile rummy for 2–4 players using 106 tiles (numbers 1–13 in four colors, two of each, plus two jokers). Players draw from the pool or meld groups and runs on the table; first to empty their rack wins. Sabra is the main version with table manipulation.

games.name: Rummy
games.description: Rummy is a classic draw-and-discard matching game. Players form melds (sets of three or four of a kind, or runs of three or more in suit) and try to dispose of all cards. Draw one, meld and lay off optionally, discard one. First to go out wins; others count deadwood points.

games.name: Russeln
games.description: Russeln (Ramscheln/Ramsch variant) is a German Rams-family game for 3-5 players. 32-card German pack. Dealer antes; 5 each; widow. Bid: play, pass, or ramsch (take all 5 tricks). Follow suit; trump; head trick. 1/5 pot per trick. Successful ramsch wins pot + 5 from each. Players may drop if they expect to fail.

games.name: Russian Bank
games.description: Russian Bank is a competitive patience game for two players, played with two standard 52-card packs (one per player). Each player has a reserve, hand, and waste pile; they build eight shared foundations (Ace to King by suit) and an eight-column tableau in descending alternating colors, and may load cards onto the opponent's reserve or waste. First to play off all cards wins; opponents may call Stop on an illegal or omitted compulsory move.

games.name: Russian Poker
games.description: Russian Poker is a casino game (not traditional poker). Player vs house. Ante, 5 cards dealt. Dealer must qualify with A-K or better; if not, bets cancelled. Player bets on beating dealer. Payout table. Option to exchange cards or buy 6th. Unusual: two different combinations from 5 or 6 cards can be paid. 1990s Russian casinos.

games.name: Saat-Aath
games.description: Saat-Aath is a two-player Indian trick-taking game in the 3-2-5 family. A 30-card pack is used, the non-dealer calls trumps, and players contest 15 tricks with quotas of 7 for the dealer and 8 for the non-dealer.
games.deck: 30-card stripped deck (8-A in all suits plus 7 of hearts and 7 of spades)

games.name: Sab'at Al-Deemin
games.description: Sab'at Al-Deemin (7 of Diamonds) is a domino partition game where players divide dominoes into groups of seven with the 7 pip as the central pivot. Strategic play involves managing your hand and outmaneuvering opponents.

games.name: Sakura
games.description: Sakura is a hanafuda matching game played with the standard 48-card flower pack, emphasizing suit memory and scoring combinations.

games.name: Sam Sip
games.description: Sam Sip (Pa-Som Sip) is a draw-and-discard game from Thailand and Burma. Players draw from the stock or the previous player's discard, then discard one card. The aim is to be the first to hold three pairs: two cards totalling 10 (Ace=1), two 10s, or two equal picture cards (J, Q, K). Wild cards (jokers and cards matching the turned-up rank) can substitute for any card. The Thai name means "mixing tens".

games.name: Samba
games.description: Samba is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in USA/UK and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: San Francisco Poker
games.description: San Francisco: 7-card stud variant where all Queens are wild. Same deal and betting as 7-card stud; any Queen counts as any card. USA; dealer's choice.

games.name: Sancagna
games.description: Sancagna is a four-player point-trick game using a 52-card Venetian pack, played on Burano in the Venice lagoon. Two teams of two (partners opposite) play anticlockwise; trump is determined by a turned card. Players must follow suit or play trump. The aim is to be the first team to collect 21 or more card points in tricks won; excess points carry to the next game.

games.name: Sang Krip
games.description: Sang Krip is a card game that involves gameplay, scoring, strategy. The game originated in Malaysia and has become popular in the region.

games.name: Sap Ng Wu
games.description: Sap Ng Wu (十五湖) is a climbing game for three or four players using an 84-card Chinese domino pack. Players in turn beat the previous play with a higher card or combination or pass; the player who played the highest takes the cards as wu (winning cards). The first to collect 15 or more wu declares a win (sik wu) and receives chip payments from the others.

games.name: Sasaki
games.description: Sasaki is a North Korean climbing card game for four players. Players try to get rid of all cards; temporary partnerships are determined by the two red 10s. The game is named after the combination 44A (two Fours and one Ace).

games.name: Saskop
games.description: Saskop (also known as Lambapea) is an Estonian trick-taking card game for four players. It is the Estonian member of the prestigious Schafkopf group of games. It distinguishes itself with a 36-card deck (removing 5s and lower) and a complex ranking system where the 6s and Kings occupy the highest tiers of the trump suit. It is a partnership game that emphasizes card counting and aggressive bidding to secure the 61-point victory threshold.

games.name: Saskop
games.description: Saskop is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Satat
games.description: Satat is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Mauritius (related to Indian Seven Hands); name from Hindi "saat hant" (seven hands). Objective: win at least seven of 13 tricks.

games.name: Scala Quaranta
games.description: Scala Quaranta is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in Italy and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Scarto
games.description: Scarto is a Piedmontese tarot trick-taking game from northwestern Italy. It is played with the full 78-card Tarocco Piemontese family and emphasizes careful discard, trump timing, and partnership coordination over multiple deals.

games.name: Schafkopf
games.description: Schafkopf (Bavarian for 'Sheep's Head') is the soul of Bavarian social culture and one of Germany's most important trick-taking games. Played with a 32-card German deck, it is a game of hidden partnerships, high-impact bidding, and mandatory suit-following. It is famous for its tiered trump system where Obers and Unters are permanent trumps, and its 'Rufspiel' (Calling Game) where you choose your partner by calling an Ace you don't possess. It is as much a social ritual as it is a card game.

games.name: Schafkopf
games.description: Schafkopf is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Schembil
games.description: Schembil is a six-player partnership trick-taking game and variant of Briscola, played in Northern Africa and Southern Italy (especially Sicily). Two teams of three choose a captain (rais) who may direct partners; 36 cards (40-card pack minus twos), three cards each, replenish from stock after each trick.

games.name: Schieberamsch
games.description: Schieberamsch is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Schwimmen
games.description: Schwimmen (31) is a Commerce-group card game in which players hold three cards and improve their hand by exchanging with a central pool of three face-up cards. The aim is to collect cards of one suit totalling as high as possible (maximum 31) or three of a kind. Played with chips; the loser of each hand loses a chip and the last survivor wins. Popular in Germany and Austria.

games.name: Scopa
games.description: Scopa is an Italian fishing card game where players capture table cards by matching rank or sum; points for sweeps, most cards, coins suit, sette bello and prime. First to 11+ points wins.

games.name: Scopa Bazzica
games.description: Two-player Scopa variant from Italy in which players capture table cards by matching value or sum, score for scope, most cards, most coins, settebello, and primiera, plus optional Bazzica (three cards summing to 9 or less) or Bazzicotto (three of a kind) declared after each three-card deal. First to 21 or 31 points wins.

games.name: Scopa con le Scalette
games.description: Scopa variant with Scalette scoring: play as normal Scopa (or Scopa d'Assi) with extra points for sequences in coins/diamonds. Scaletta bassa (A-2-3) scores 3 points; Scaletta alta (K-Q-J) scores 5; taking all coins wins the game outright.

games.name: Scopa Corse
games.description: Scopa Corse is the Corsican variant of Scopa, played with a 36-card Italian deck (no 2s). Players capture table cards by matching rank or by sum; unlike basic Scopa, capturing is optional. First to 21 points wins.

games.name: Scopa d'Assi
games.description: Scopa d'Assi is an Italian fishing game and variant of Scopa. Like Asso Pigliatutto, an Ace captures all table cards; unlike that variant, clearing the table with an Ace does not count as a sweep (scopa). Play and scoring match basic Scopa: capture by matching value or sum, score for sweeps, most cards, most coins, settebello, and primiera. Often played by four in partnerships with 9 or 10 cards each (Scopone style), or with optional Napola points.

games.name: Scopa di Quindici
games.description: Scopa di Quindici is an Italian Scopa variant in which capture is allowed only when the played card plus one or more table cards sum to 15. Deal and play as basic Scopa; scoring for sweeps, most cards, coins, settebello, and primiera. First to 11 wins.

games.name: Scopone
games.description: Scopone is a skilful Italian four-player partnership card game in which cards or sets of cards are captured from the table by playing cards of equal value. It is closely related to Scopa.

games.name: Sebastopol
games.description: Sebastopol is a cross domino game for four players (or three in variants) using a double-six set. Players build four arms from the double-six spinner; the first to play all tiles scores the pips in opponents' hands. Game is played to 60 points.

games.name: Second Hand High
games.description: Second Hand High: 7-card stud variant where at showdown the second-highest hand wins the pot. Same deal and betting as 7-card stud; if all but one player fold, the survivor wins. USA; dealer's choice.

games.name: Sedma
games.description: Sedma is a Czech trick-and-draw card game in which tricks are won by matching ranks; sevens act as wild cards. The game originated in Bohemia and became one of the most popular games in Czechoslovakia, and is played in partnerships or by 2–3 players.

games.name: Sedma Dominoes
games.description: Connecting domino game named after the Czech word for seven. Four players receive seven tiles each; no boneyard. Lead rotates; the leader must set a double. Players in turn extend the train from one side only or pass. Points for setting doubles; game to 60.

games.name: Sedmice
games.description: Sedmice is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Seep
games.description: Seep is a four-player partnership fishing game played in the Punjab and other parts of India and Pakistan. Players capture cards from a layout; building piles called houses and scoring for sweeps. Related to Casino and Royal Casino.

games.name: Selection or Rejection
games.description: Selection / Rejection is a poker card game that involves betting, hand rankings, bluffing. The game originated in USA and has become popular worldwide.
alsoKnownAs: Want it Want it Got it

games.name: Seotda
games.description: Seotda is a traditional Korean two-card game played with 20 Hwatu cards; players form ranked combinations (GwangTtaeng, Ttaeng, Geut) and bet. LA Seotda is a modern variant with a 52-card deck and poker-style elements.

games.name: Sequence Poker
games.description: Poker variant where hands include sequences. Combines poker with sequence-building mechanics.
games.deck: Standard 52-card French deck; four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades), thirteen ranks per suit (Ace through King). Used for five-card hands and standard poker hand rankings including straights.

games.name: Sergeant Major
games.description: Sergeant Major is a trick-taking card game that involves tricks, trump, following suit. The game originated in Europe and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Sette e Mezzo
games.description: Sette e Mezzo (Italian for seven and a half) is an Italian comparing card game similar to blackjack. Players compete against the dealer to get as close as possible to 7½ without exceeding it. Popular in Italy (especially at Christmas), Spain (Siete y Media) and Brazil (Sete e Meio).

games.name: Seven Card Stud
games.description: Seven Card Stud is a poker card game that involves betting, hand rankings, bluffing. The game originated in USA and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Seven Rocks
games.description: Seven Rocks is a four-player partnership domino game in the Fives family. Players build a cross-shaped layout, score when open ends total a multiple of five, and race to 250 points.

games.name: Seven Twenty-Seven
games.description: Seven Twenty-Seven is an American vying game, often used in dealer's-choice sessions, where players build card totals as close as possible to 7 and 27 while betting between draws.

games.name: Seven Twenty-Seven
games.description: Seven Twenty-Seven is an American vying game, often used in dealer's-choice sessions, where players build card totals as close as possible to 7 and 27 while betting between draws.

games.name: Seven-Toed Pete Race Horse
games.description: Seven-Toed Pete is a fast Fives-family domino game for four players. Players score on multiples of five and gain extra turns whenever they score or play a double.

games.name: Sevens Dominoes
games.description: Sevens is a domino layout game where players build a triangular pattern from doubles and sequential non-doubles, trying to be first to play all tiles.

games.name: Shanghai Rummy
games.description: Shanghai Rummy is a contract-rummy style game played across ten hands with changing meld requirements. Players draw, meld sets/runs, and try to go out while minimizing penalty points.

games.name: Sheepshead
games.description: Sheepshead is a trick-taking game derived from Schafkopf and widely played in Wisconsin and other German-American communities. Standard play uses five players, a 32-card piquet deck, a two-card blind, and a hidden partner mechanic where the picker and partner try to reach 61 card points.
games.deck: 32-card piquet deck (7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A in each suit)

games.name: Sheng Ji
games.description: Sheng Ji (Tractor / Level Up) is a Chinese point-trick game family with dynamic trump rank and suit each round. The standard form uses four players in fixed partnerships and two decks with jokers.
games.deck: Two 54-card decks (including jokers) in the common four-player form

games.name: Shenyang Mahjong
games.description: Shenyang Mahjong is a northeast China Mahjong variant associated with Shenyang and Liaoning region play. It keeps the core draw-discard meld structure while applying local table conventions for win validity and scoring emphasis.

games.name: Shichi Narabe
games.description: Shichi Narabe is a Japanese layout shedding game related to Fan Tan/Sevens. Players lay out all sevens first, then extend each suit outward toward Ace and King while managing a limited number of passes.

games.name: Shithead
games.description: Shithead is a shedding card game in which players try to get rid of all cards while avoiding being the last player left with cards. It is also known as Karma or Palace and has many regional rule variants.
games.origin: Modern international folk game (popularized in Europe and backpacker circles)
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (plus optional jokers in some variants)

games.name: Shlla'at
games.description: Shlla'at is a Sudanese fishing card game in which players capture cards from the table and from opponents' capture piles. A turn continues with a new draw after each capture until no capture is made. The Arabic name means 'uprooted'.

games.name: Shoot
games.description: Shoot is a banking betting game in the Red Dog family. The dealer maintains the pot while each player bets that their hidden hand contains a card of the same suit and higher rank than the dealer's turned-up card.
games.origin: Traditional gambling variant (documented in Red Dog family)

games.name: Sì Sè Pái
games.description: Sì Sè Pái (Four Color Cards or Si Se Pai) is a Chinese card game similar to Rummy or Mahjong. It uses a deck of 112 cards divided into 4 colors (Red, Green, Yellow, White), featuring Chinese Chess pieces (General, Advisor, Elephant, etc.). The goal is to meld cards into sets (Commanders/Generals can be melded singly, Pairs, Triplets/Pongs, Quads/Kongs) to reach an odd number of points (usually 21 cards total).
games.deck: 112 cards (4 Suits x 7 Ranks x 4 Copies per Card).

games.name: Sichuan Mahjong
games.description: Sichuan Mahjong is a Chinese regional Mahjong variant known for fast hand tempo, aggressive discard pressure, and regional rule profiles that emphasize dynamic tactical exchange.

games.name: Sidi Barrani Jass
games.description: Swiss Jass variant for four players in fixed partnerships. Each deal starts with an auction to set trump (or Obenabe/Undenufe) and the point target the bidders must make. Play is anticlockwise; declarer leads first. Points from tricks, last trick, Weis and Stöck; first team to 2000 wins.
games.deck: 36 cards (Jass pack; Swiss or French suits)

games.name: Simultaneous Solitaire
games.description: Competitive patience in which two or more players each play the same solitaire layout (typically Klondike) at the same time; the first to complete their layout wins.

games.name: Singaporean Mahjong
games.description: Singaporean Mahjong is a Southeast Asian Mahjong profile with animal bonus tile rules and local scoring conventions. It uses an expanded 148-tile composition and keeps the standard draw-discard claim rhythm.

games.name: Sink-Sink
games.description: Sink-Sink is a card game commonly played in Niger; a variant of Agram with five cards per player instead of six, dealt in sets of three and two. Players follow suit; the winner of each trick leads to the next. The player who wins the fifth and last trick wins the game.

games.name: Siwweschr M Eifel Poker
games.description: Siwweschr M Eifel Poker is the same regional game family as Siwweschroom: a Toepen-style, no-trump last-trick game where knocks raise risk and players are eliminated after seven points.
games.deck: 32-card French pack (10, 9, 8, 7, A, K, Q, J in each suit)

games.name: Siwweschroom
games.description: Siwweschroom is an Eifel and Rhineland variant of Toepen, a no-trump last-trick game played with four-card hands and aggressive knocking. Players who accumulate seven penalty points are eliminated; the last remaining player wins.
games.deck: 32-card French pack (10, 9, 8, 7, A, K, Q, J in each suit)

games.name: Sixty-Three
games.description: 63 (Sixty-Three): four players in two partnerships. 9 cards each then bid (40-63); 4 more cards then discard to 6. Only trump cards score (A=1, K=25, 9=9, 5=5, 3=15, etc; total 63). Make bid to score; first to 152 or 250 wins.

games.name: Sjavs
games.description: Sjavs (pronounced 'Shows' or 'Shavs') is a popular card game in the Faroe Islands and parts of Denmark. It is a derivative of the German game Schafkopf, played with a stripped deck of 32 cards (standard Skat/Piquet deck). The game involves bidding, trump calling, and trick-taking, with a unique scoring system based on 'Rubbers' (first to reach 0 points from 24). It is highly strategic and social.

games.name: Skat
games.description: Skat is widely regarded as Germany's national card game and one of the best 3-player trick-taking games ever devised. It features complex bidding based on 'Game Value', a unique trump hierarchy (Jacks are highest), and three main contract types (Suit, Grand, Null). The 'Soloist' plays against two defenders. The game combines luck, skill in hand evaluation, and precise card play.
games.deck: 32-card Skat deck (A, 10, K, Q, 9, 8, 7, J - Wait, J is high. Rank: J, A, 10, K, Q, 9, 8, 7)

games.name: Skin
games.description: Skin (or 'Georgia Skin') is a legendary high-stakes gambling game from the American South. It is a banking game, but not in the traditional sense where the bank has an edge; the edge comes purely from chance, nerve, and 'side bets'. Cards are dealt from a shoe one by one. Players bet on their card being matched by a card from the deck. If your card is matched (falls), you lose. The last card standing ('The Skin') is the winner unless all bets are resolved earlier. It is famous for its slow, tension-filled reveal ('Skinning').
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (often multiple decks in a shoe for large games)

games.name: Skitgubbe
games.description: Skitgubbe (Swedish: 'Shit Old Man', also known simply as 'Skit' or 'Mattis') is a traditional Swedish card game for 3 players. It is divided into two distinct phases: Phase 1 (Trick-Taking/Collection) where players try to gather good cards, and Phase 2 (Shedding/Battle) where the goal is to get rid of all cards. The loser is the last player holding cards and is declared the 'Skitgubbe'.
games.deck: Standard 52-card pack without joker. Three cards each; remainder forms the stock. Rank A (high) down to 2 (low).

games.name: Skruuvi
games.description: Skruuvi is a Finnish trick-taking card game for four players, a descendant of the Russian game Vint and a distant cousin of Bridge. It features bidding, misère contracts, and card exchange between partners.

games.name: Slabberjan
games.description: Slabberjan is a traditional Dutch elimination game, specific to Zeeland, where players swap 'pieces' (originally cards, now custom tiles/tokens called 'Doppen') to avoid holding the lowest rank at the end of a round. It is remarkably similar to the card game 'Gnav' or 'Cuckoo'. The game involves bluffing, special 'Matador' pieces that block swaps (Knight, Bird, Cat, Inn), and a pot that the loser must pay into. The last player with chips wins.
games.deck: 42 unique 'Doppen' (2 sets of 21 designs) or adapted 42-card deck

games.name: Slapjack
games.description: Slapjack (or 'Slaps') is a children's card game that tests speed and reflexes. Players take turns flipping cards onto a central pile. When a Jack appears, the first player to slap the pile wins all the cards in the center. The goal is to collect the entire deck.

games.name: Slippery Sam
games.description: Banking game: dealer puts up a stake; dealer deals three cards face-down to each player (players do not look), then turns cards face up until a six or lower appears; each player in turn bets on having a higher card of the same suit than that spot card; after betting, the hand is exposed and the player wins from or pays into the pot.

games.name: Slosh
games.description: Slosh is a four-handed British domino game from the Trains family, played with a double-six set. The engine tile is placed in the center; each player has a train (a line of tiles) extending from the engine toward them. On your turn you add a tile to your own train if you can; if you cannot, the next player may slosh (play on your train) then play on their own. The round ends when someone dominoes or the game is blocked; lowest pip count in hand wins the round. Scoring is with poker chips or pencil.

games.name: Smear
games.description: Smear (also spelled 'Schmier' or 'Schmear') is a card game played in the northern Midwest of the USA (Minnesota, Wisconsin), closely related to Pitch and High-Low-Jack. It is a trick-taking game typically played with 4 players in partnerships. The objective is to score points for High, Low, Jack, and Game (the 'Smear'), with bids usually starting at 2 or 3. The term 'Smear' also refers to the act of playing a high-point card (like a 10 or Ace) on a partner's winning trick.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (or stripped deck A-10-K-Q-J-9? Usually full deck, but only specific trumps count).

games.name: Snap
games.description: Snap is a classic children's card game that tests mental reaction speed and pattern recognition. Players take turns flipping cards from their personal piles onto a central pile or their own discard pile. When two cards of the same rank (e.g., two 7s) appear consecutively or simultaneously on top of piles, the first player to shout 'Snap!' wins the cards. The goal is to win the entire deck.

games.name: Sniff
games.description: Sniff is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Sökö
games.description: SÃ¶kÃ¶ (also known as Scandinavian Stud or Canadian Stud) is a popular Finnish variant of Five Card Stud poker. Its defining feature is the addition of two hand rankings: the Four-Card Flush and the Four-Card Straight, which rank above a pair and below two pairs. This increases the frequency of playable hands and encourages more aggressive action.

games.name: Soko Stud Poker
games.description: SÃ¶kÃ¶: Five Card Stud variant from Finland. Special rules for low cards and scoring; distinct from standard 5-card stud.

games.name: Solo
games.description: German Solo (often just called Solo) is a trick-taking game for 4 to 6 players, descended from l'Hombre. It is played with a 32-card pack (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 in each suit). Players bid for the right to choose trump and to play alone or with a called partner. The highest trump is always the Queen of Clubs, second is the 7 of trump, third is the Queen of Spades. The game survives in parts of the USA though little played in Germany today.
games.deck: 32 cards (French suits; A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7 per suit)

games.name: Solo (German)
games.description: German Solo (often just 'Solo') is a trick-taking card game for 4 players that evolved from Quadrille and L'Hombre. It uses a 32-card deck (Aces down to 7s). It is distinct from Solo Whist. The unique feature is the 'Color' ranking (Clubs/Spades are black, Hearts/Diamonds are red) which affects the card order, and the presence of fixed top trumps called 'Matadors' (Spadille, Manille, Basto) regardless of the named trump suit.

games.name: Solo Whist
games.description: Solo Whist (or simply 'Solo') is a British trick-taking card game derived from Whist but incorporating bidding elements from Boston and Quadrille. Unlike Partnership Whist, players bid individually to achieve specific goals, such as making 5, 9, or 13 tricks alone ('Solo', 'Abundance', 'Abundance Declared') or losing every trick ('Misere'). It is a game of high skill and nerve.

games.name: Spades (Standard)
games.description: Spades is a trick-taking card game devised in the United States in the 1930s. It is played by four players in partnerships, using a standard 52-card deck. Spades are always the trump suit. The object is to score points by winning at least the number of tricks bid in each hand. Bids are made before play begins. 'Bags' (overtricks) and 'Nil' bids add strategic depth.

games.name: Spades Partnership
games.description: Spades Partnership (often just 'Partnership Spades' or 'Cutthroat Spades' depending on context) refers to specific variations of Spades that emphasize the partnership aspect or introduce specific bidding constraints like 'Suicide' (one partner must bid Nil), 'Mirrors' (bid exactly your Spades), or 'Whiz' (Nil or Spades). It is played with the standard 4-player setup but with modified bidding rules.

games.name: Spanish 21
games.description: Spanish 21 (known internationally as Pontoon in Australia, not UK classic Pontoon) is a variant of Blackjack played with 'Spanish' decks (48 cards, removing the 10s). The removal of 10s increases the house edge, but this is compensated by extremely player-friendly rules such as 'Player 21 always wins', 'Surrender after Double', and special bonus payouts for specific 21 combinations (6-7-8, 7-7-7). It is highly popular in casinos.
games.deck: Spanish Deck (48 cards: Remove 10s from Standard 52. J, Q, K are still 10 value). Often 6-8 decks.

games.name: Spar
games.description: Spar is the most popular card game in Ghana. It is a trick-taking game without trumps in which the object is to win the last trick. Played by 2 to 4 players (up to 7 possible) with 35 cards from a standard pack. Similar games are played in Benin as Jeu de Carte and in Togo as Sipa. Often played for money or for enjoyment.
games.deck: 35 cards from a standard 52-card pack: each suit has 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A (Ace high). The Ace of Spades is normally not used, so the highest spade is the King.

games.name: Speculation
games.description: Speculation is a historical gambling game popular in the 18th and 19th centuries, famously depicted in Jane Austen's novels. The game revolves around players buying and selling the right to the 'Highest Trump' currently revealed. It is not trick-taking but a game of chance and negotiation, where the winner is the holder of the highest trump when all cards are revealed.

games.name: Speed
games.description: Speed is a frantic two-player shedding card game where players race to get rid of all their cards onto two central piles. Play is simultaneous and real-time. Cards can be played if they are one rank higher or lower (e.g., 6 on 5, or 6 on 7) than the card on the pile. There are no turns. The first player to exhaust their hand and draw pile shouts 'Speed!' to win.

games.name: Spider (Solitaire)
games.description: Spider is one of the most popular two-deck solitaire games. The goal is to assemble 13 cards of a suit (K down to A) on the tableau, which then automatically removes itself from play. It is typically played with two decks (104 cards). The difficulty varies massively depending on the number of suits used (1 Suit = Easy, 2 Suits = Medium, 4 Suits = Hard).

games.name: Spit
games.description: Spit (or 'Slam') is a fast-paced two-player shedding card game related to Speed. Unlike Speed, each player maintains five small 'stock piles' in front of them (similar to Solitaire layout) and races to empty these piles onto two central discard stacks. Play is simultaneous and chaotic. The winner of a round gets to choose the smaller pile for the next round, aiming to start with fewer cards.

games.name: Spit in the Ocean Poker
games.description: Draw poker with one shared community card dealt face up. That card and all cards of the same rank are wild. Players get four private cards plus the community card to make a five-card hand, with a draw round and two betting rounds.

games.name: Spite and Malice
games.description: Spite and Malice (also known as Cat and Mouse) is a competitive patience game for two or more players, traditionally played with two or more standard decks of cards. It is the direct ancestor of the commercial game Skip-Bo. The objective is to be the first to move all cards from your personal 'pay-off pile' onto center 'build piles'. Kings are wild (or Jokers), and Aces start the piles.
games.origin: United States (derived from Russian Bank / Crapette principles)

games.name: Spitzer
games.description: Four-player trick-taking game of the Schafkopf group (ace-ten family), played mainly in north-eastern Michigan, USA. Temporary partnerships each hand (two vs two or one vs three). Trumps are all queens, jacks, and diamonds; the diamond 7 (Spitzer) ranks second-highest. First to 42 game points wins.

games.name: Spizzichino
games.description: Spizzichino (or 'Pizzichino') is a complex two-player Italian card game played with a 40-card deck (Italian suits). It combines elements of Briscola (trick-taking) and Scopa (capture/fishing) with meld-making (similar to Bezique/Pinochle). The name likely refers to 'picking' or 'nibbling' at points in small increments. The game is highly strategic and lesser-known outside Italy.

games.name: Spoons
games.description: Spoons (also known as Tongue or Pig) is a fast-paced shedding and elimination game played with a standard card deck and a set of spoons (one less than the number of players). The objective is to collect four of a kind (e.g., four 6s) and then grab a spoon. As soon as one spoon is taken, everyone else must grab a spoon. The person left without a spoon is eliminated or receives a letter (S-P-O-O-N).

games.name: Spot (Irish Rummy)
games.description: Spot is a traditional Irish rummy game for 4 players, played for small stakes in pubs and homes. It uses an 8-card hand and a standard 52-card deck (Ac-10-K-Q-J-9 is NOT used, standard A=1, 2-10, J-K=10). The goal is to 'Drop' melds (sets of 3+ or sequences of 3+) to reduce the spot value of remaining cards. A player cannot drop more than 4 cards at once.

games.name: Spot Hearts
games.description: Spot Hearts is a trick-taking variant where each heart scores its pip value (2 through 10 face value, jack 11, queen 12, king 13, ace 14; queen of spades 25). Players avoid winning tricks containing penalty cards; the game is played to a higher target (e.g. 500) and the lowest score wins.

games.name: Staekske Rape
games.description: Staekske Rape (Limburgish: 'Pick Up the Stock') is a Dutch Jass game played in Maastricht and surrounding areas. It is played by four players with a 32-card deck (7s through Aces), featuring a bidding process where the winner takes the 4-card 'Stock' and names trumps. It combines trick-taking with meld declarations ('Stoek' and 'Vier' - 4 of a kind, sequence of 3+).
games.deck: 32 cards (Standard Piquet deck or Dutch/French suits).

games.name: Steal War
games.description: War variant where players can steal cards from opponents. More strategic than classic War.

games.name: Stealing Bundles
games.description: Stealing Bundles (also known as Stealing the Old Man's Bundle) is a simple fishing card game for two or more players, popular with children. It is similar to Casino but simplified. Players capture face-up cards from the table by matching their rank. Captured cards are stacked in a 'bundle'. The unique twist is that players can steal an opponent's entire bundle by matching the top card.

games.name: Stop the Bus
games.description: Stop the Bus is a fast-paced commerce game played with 3 cards, similar to Commerce and 31. Players start with 3 lives (tokens) and aim to *not* have the worst hand when someone calls 'Stop the Bus'. The game is elimination-based, with the last surviving player winning.

games.name: Stortok
games.description: Stortok (Swedish: 'Big Fool') is a Swedish card game related to the Russian game Durak. The primary goal is to get rid of all your cards. The winner is the first player out, and the last player holding cards is the 'Stortok' (Fool). It features attacking and defending mechanics, but with fewer complex card interactions than Durak.
games.deck: Standard 36-card deck (A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 - remove 2, 3, 4, 5).

games.name: Stovkahra
games.description: Stovkahra (Slovak: 'Hundred Game' or 'Hundreth') is a trick-taking card game for 4 players in fixed partnerships. It is played with a 32-card German or French-suited deck (7-Ace). The goal is to reach 100 points first by winning point cards (Ace, Ten, King, Queen, Jack) and melding combinations.

games.name: Strafperlaggen
games.description: Strafperlaggen is a variant of Perlaggen, a traditional Tyrolean card game, typically played by 3 players. It uses a 33-card German-suited deck (Weli is the 33rd card). Similar to Perlaggen, players aim to win 'figures' (Gleich, Hanger, Spiel). The 'Straf' (Penalty) aspect likely refers to stricter rules or penalty points for failures.

games.name: Streets and Alleys
games.description: Streets and Alleys (also known as Gaps or Lane) is a solitaire game played with a single 52-card deck. It is similar to Beleaguered Castle but with a different layout. The entire deck is dealt into 8 tableau piles (wings). The goal is to build up the four foundations from Ace to King by suit.

games.name: Strip Poker
games.description: Poker variant where losers remove clothing. Social/stakes variant of standard poker.

games.name: Strohmandeln
games.description: Strohmandeln is a two-player Austrian tarock game in the Industrie und Glueck family. It uses a 54-card deck and distinctive strawman packets that create open and hidden information shifts through the deal.

games.name: Stýrivolt
games.description: Stýrivolt is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from the Faroe Islands, belonging to the Karnöffel group. A 48-card pack is used (tens removed from a standard French deck). Each player receives 9 cards in batches of three; 12 cards remain as stock. The dealer determines two chosen suits from the stock; cards in those suits have special powers (stikkar, lambs, taking cards). There is no requirement to follow suit. The team that wins at least five of the nine tricks wins the hand. Winning the first five tricks (vol) scores a bonus.
games.deck: Standard 48-card deck (tens removed from French pack). Nine cards each, 12-card stock.

games.name: Sueca
games.description: Sueca (Portuguese: 'Swedish') is the most popular card game in Portugal and Brazil. It is a trick-taking game for 4 players in two partnerships. The game uses a 40-card deck and is notable for its Ace-Seven-King-Jack-Queen hierarchy (similar to Briscola or Tressette, but with 7 as 10 points). The goal is to take more than half the points (61+) in tricks. No talking is allowed.

games.name: Sviten Special
games.description: Sviten Special (also called Drawmaha) is a Swedish split-pot poker game that combines 5-Card Draw and Pot-Limit Omaha. Each player is dealt 5 cards. There is a Flop, Turn, and River. After the Flop betting, players can discard and draw new cards to their hand (Draw Poker rules). The twist: If you draw ONE card, it is dealt face-up (or you can reject it and take a face-down one). The pot is split between the best 5-card hand (private) and the best Omaha hand (2 private + 3 board).

games.name: Svoi Kozyri
games.description: Svoi Kozyri (Russian: 'My Own Trumps' or 'Your Trumps') is a Russian card game where players have their own personal trump suit. It is a shedding game for 2-4 players. The objective is to get rid of all your cards. The twist is that if you lead a card of your own trump suit, it is powerful for you, but attacking others with their trumps forces them to defend heavily.

games.name: Sweet Chariot Poker
games.description: Sweet Chariot is a lowball variant of Swingo Poker. Players receive five cards, choose two as hole cards and three as board cards, then use their board cards plus one shared river card and one card from any opponent's board to make their best five-card hand. The lowest hand wins the pot. Played with blinds and pot limit betting.

games.name: Swingo Poker
games.description: Poker variant in which players bet on the best five-card hand, using their own five cards (three exposed), one shared face-up river card, and one exposed card from any other player.

games.name: Swoop
games.description: Swoop is a multi-deck shedding game (3-5 decks) similar to Crazy Eights or Palace, played by 3-8 players. It features 'Mystery Cards' (face-down) and 'Swoop Cards' (Tens/Jokers) that clear the pile. The goal is to get rid of all cards in your hand, then your face-up pile, then your mystery pile.
games.deck: 2-4 standard 52-card packs with two jokers each (3-4 players: 2 decks; 5-6: 3 decks; 7-8: 4 decks)

games.name: Ta Gou Ta Doi 搭九搭对
games.description: Ta Gou Ta Doi (搭九搭对, 'making nines and pairs') is a Malaysian rummy-like game played with 32 Chinese chess (Xiangqi) pieces used as cards. Each turn: draw one, discard one. Win by collecting three valid sets of two: Gou (two pieces summing to 9) or Doi (pair of same value). Easy and hard variants differ in what counts as a set.
games.deck: 32 Xiangqi (Chinese chess) pieces used as cards; values 1–8, two colours (red and black).

games.name: Tablić
games.description: Tablić (or Tablanette) is a fishing-style card game popular in the Balkans (Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia). Players capture face-up cards from the table by matching their value or summing to their value. Points are awarded for capturing specific high-value cards (face cards, 10s, Aces) and for having the most cards. The game is similar to Casino.

games.name: Tahiti
games.description: Tahiti is an alternative name for Big Two (also known as Cho Dai Di, Big Deuce, and Top Dog). It is a popular climbing card game of Chinese origin where players try to be the first to get rid of all their cards by playing singles or combinations (pairs, triples, poker hands) that beat the previous play. The Two is the highest rank.
games.origin: China (often called Tahiti in Western circles)

games.name: Tahoe
games.description: Tahoe (also known as Wichita Hold'em) is a community card poker game similar to Texas Hold'em and Pineapple. Players receive three hole cards (sometimes two, but usually three in the Tahoe variant) and share five community cards. The key restriction is that players may use zero, one, or two of their hole cards to form a handâ€”never all three. It is often played High-Low Split.

games.name: Tàihé A Bāo 泰和A包
games.description: Tàihé A Bāo (泰和A包) is a Chinese climbing game from Taihe county, Jiangxi province. Four players: one declarer vs the other three each hand. 40-card deck (remove 2s, 3s, 8s); rank A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 7, 6, 5, 4. Cards drawn from deck counterclockwise (not dealt). Bidding: declare or pass; if all pass, second round—call for a card (exchange); last caller is declarer. Play: declarer leads combinations; others beat or pass. Combinations: singles, pairs, sequences, double sequences, three-of-a-kind, four-of-a-kind (bombs beat any non-bomb). First out wins; if declarer wins they collect stakes from each opponent. Often played for money.

games.name: Taiwanese Mahjong
games.description: Taiwanese Mahjong is a four-player regional Mahjong variant known for local table conventions and expanded tactical tempo compared with some other forms. It keeps classic draw-discard meld structure and fan-based outcome evaluation.

games.name: Tapp Tarock
games.description: Tapp Tarock (German: Tapp-Tarock), also called Viennese Tappen or Tappen, is a three-player Austrian tarot trick-taking game using the 54-card Industrie und Glück deck. Each player receives 16 cards and 6 form the talon. Players bid (Dreier, Unterer, Oberer, Solo); the declarer may exchange with three talon cards in lower contracts or play alone in Solo. Play is anticlockwise; follow suit or trump; declarer needs 36 card points to win.
games.deck: 54-card Industrie und Glück Tarot (22 trumps plus 32 suit cards)

games.name: Tarneeb
games.description: Tarneeb (Arabic for 'Trump') is a popular trick-taking card game in the Middle East (Levant, Egypt). It is a partnership game for 4 players. Teams bid on how many tricks they can take (starting from 7 up to 13). The highest bidder names the trump suit (Tarneeb). The objective is to fulfill the bid.

games.name: Tarocchi Bolognesi
games.description: Tarocchi Bolognesi (or Tarocchino Bolognese) refers to the family of games played with the specific 62-card Tarot deck from Bologna. The most common variant is Ottocento, but the term covers the deck and system itself. The deck removes ranks 2-5 from each suit of a standard Tarot pack.
games.duration: Typically 30–60 minutes per session depending on variant and number of deals.

games.name: Tarocchi Siciliano
games.description: Tarocchi Siciliano (Sicilian Tarot) is a traditional card game played with a unique 63-card deck. It features ranks and suits distinct from other Tarot decks (Portuguese-style pips). The game is a point-trick game, often played by 4 players. Features the 'Fugitive' (Fool) and 'Miseria' (low trump).

games.name: Tarock Königrufen (Austrian)
games.description: KÃ¶nigrufen (Call the King) is the 'queen of card games' in Austria. It is a 4-player Tarot game with a 54-card deck. The defining feature is the 'calling' mechanic where a declarer chooses a partner by calling a King suit. There are numerous contracts ranging from simple games to complex negative bids (Bettel) and high-value solos.

games.name: Tarock Lungau Königrufen
games.description: Lungau Königrufen is a regional variant of Austrian Königrufen played in the Lungau region of Salzburg. It is known for being a faster, sharper game with fewer, more decisive contracts and a streamlined counting process.

games.name: Tarock TÃ¼bingen
games.description: TÃ¼bingen Tarock is a historical 4-player German tarot game, a version of Tarok-Quadrille documented by Guntram Kommerell from a variant played by students in TÃ¼bingen around 1890. Four players use a 78-card French-suited pack (21 numbered tarocks, Fool/Ski, 14 cards per suit with Cavalier). Play is counter-clockwise. After deal the dealer discards two cards; then either a player bids Raus (solo vs three) or in Rufen the dealer or others call a Kingâ€”the holder is the caller's secret partner. Total card value 91 points; teams count to 23 then again; declarer's side wins by scoring more than half of the remaining 45. Bonuses (Strafen) for families, kingdoms, tarock sequences, pagÃ¡t last trick.
games.deck: 78 French-suited cards (21 tarocks, Fool/Ski, 14 per suit with Cavalier)

games.name: Tarok Danish
games.description: Danish Tarok (Grosstarock) is a three-player trick-taking game using a 78-card tarot deck (21 trumps, Fool, 4 suits of 14). Primary objective: win the last trick with the lowest trump (trump 1) or a King. Secondary: win tricks and capture counting cards. Alliances form during play. Each player gets 25 cards (dealer gets 3 extra then discards to 25). Declarations at start: trump holdings, matadors (Fool, lowest trump, 21), court combinations. Two pots (king pot, lowest-trump pot). Card values: 4 for trump 21, lowest trump, Fool, Kings; 3 Queens; 2 Knights; 1 Jacks. Closely related to German Grosstarock; survives mainly in Denmark.

games.name: Tarok Romanian
games.description: Romanian Tarok is a point-trick game played mainly around Suceava in Moldavia. Introduced from Austria in the 19th century; uses 54-card Austrian tarok pack (22 trumpsâ€”taroaceâ€”plus four suits of eight). Highest trump skiz, then luna (XXI), lowest trump (I). Card values: skiz, luna, lowest trump and Kings 5, Queens 4, horses 3, Jacks 2, others 1. Objective: win tricks with valuable cards. Follow suit; must trump if unable. Cards in tricks counted in groups of three with 2 points subtracted per group. Phases: deal, bidding, calling a king, talon use, trick play, bonuses, declarations. Three-player variant Taper and other regional forms exist.

games.name: Tarok Slovenian
games.description: Slovenian Tarok is the most popular parlour game in Slovenia, a point trick-taking game with bidding closely related to Austrian Tarock. 54 cards: 8 per suit (Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds) plus 22 trumps (taroks). Highest trump Å kis, then Mond (XXI), lowest trump (I). Black suits K-Q-Knight-J-10-9-8-7; red K-Q-Knight-J-1-2-3-4. Kings, Å kis, Mond, lowest trump 5 pts each; Queens 4, Knights 3, Jacks 2, others 1. Four players; dealer gives 12 cards each in two batches of 6 (counter-clockwise), 6 in talon. Bidding from Three up to Valat Without. With three/two/one declarer calls a King for secret partner. Declarer's side wins by taking more than half the card points.

games.name: Taroki Polish, call king
games.description: Taroki z królami (Taroki call king) is a four-player Polish tarot game from Kozy near Bielsko Biała. Bidder chooses partner by calling a King (not the XIX). 54-card pack, 22 trumps; highest skiż, then XXI down to I, the lowest trump. Objective: bidder's side wins by taking more than half the card points in tricks. Bonuses for all kings, last trick with lowest trump, etc. Card values: skiż/XXI/kings 5, queens 4, cavaliers 3, jacks 2, others 1. From Austrian Tarock tradition in Galicia/Silesia.

games.name: Taroki Polish, call XIX
games.description: Taroki z dziewiÄ™tnastkÄ… (Taroki call XIX) is a Polish tarot game played around Zabrzeg and Czechowice-Dziedzice. Four players; partner is chosen by calling the XIX (19) tarokk. Similar to Czech Taroky. Uses 54-card pack with 22 trumps. Descended from Austrian Tarock variants when the region was part of Austrian Galicia and Silesia.

games.name: Tarokk Hungarian
games.description: Hungarian Tarokk (HÃºszashÃ­vÃ¡sos tarokk, Paskievics tarokk) is a four- or five-player tarot game with 42-card pack (22 tarokks, 5 cards per suit). Partners change each hand and are chosen by calling a tarokkâ€”usually the XX. Besides winning majority of the 94 card points, players pursue bonuses: all honours or all kings, pagÃ¡t ultimo (last trick with I), catching XXI with skÃ­z (mayor's hat). Bidding: three, two, one, solo (number of talon cards declarer takes). Declarer calls partner after talon exchange; announcements and kontra. Developed in 19th century from Austrian Zwanzigerrufen; favoured by Hungarian establishment.

games.name: Taroky Czech
games.description: Taroky is a tarot game for 4 players played mainly in the Czech Republic (especially Moravia) and Slovakia. 54-card pack: 22 permanent trumps (taroky)â€”Å¡kÃ½z, XXI (mond) down to I (pagÃ¡t)â€”plus four suits of eight cards each. Twelve cards each, six in talon; play anticlockwise. Teams are one vs three or two vs two by bidding. Bidder often calls XIX for partner. Point-trick game: follow suit, trump if void; count card points in tricks. Bonuses for declared combinations and last trick with pagÃ¡t. No-bid game VarÅ¡ava: avoid winning points.

games.name: Taroky Nebraska
games.description: Nebraska Taroky is a four-player trick-taking game played mainly by people of Czech descent in Nebraska. 54-card Tarok pack: 22 trumps (Skies/Å kÃ½z highest, then 21 down to 1) and four suits of 8. Play is clockwise (unlike European Taroky). Bidder chooses partner by calling a King (not trump XIX). Object: win tricks with valuable cards. Follow suit; trump if void. Count cards in packets of three, subtract 2 per packet. Bonuses for declared combinations. Typically played for money with settlements after each hand.

games.name: Tarot
games.description: French Tarot is a trick-taking game for 3â€“5 players (usually 4) using a 78-card deck: 21 numbered trumps (atouts), the Excuse (Fool), and four suits of 14 cards (King, Queen, Knight, Jack, 10â€“1). Six cards form the Dog. Deal 18 each (4-player). Bidding: Petite, Garde, Garde Sans (without Dog), Garde Contre. Taker plays alone vs three defenders. Card points: bouts (21, 1, Excuse) and Kings 4.5 each; Queens 3.5; Knights 2.5; Jacks 1.5; others 0.5. Taker needs 56/51/41/36 points depending on number of Oudlers (bouts) in tricks.

games.name: Tarot of the Abbé de Marolles 1637
games.description: Three-player trick-taking Tarot recorded by the Abbé de Marolles in 1637 at Nevers. Played with a 66-card pack (Italian-suited Tarot with lowest three of each suit removed). Players score for declaring card combinations, for winning or losing Tarots (Kings, Fool, Trump I, XXI), for card points in tricks, and for Ultimo (last trick with King or Trump I).
games.deck: 66-card Tarot (Italian-suited, lowest 3 of each suit removed)

games.name: Tartli
games.description: Tartli (FelsÅ‘s) is a two-player trick-and-draw game from Hungary, played with a 32-card German-suited deck (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Gourds). Part of the Jass family; the Over-Knave (FelsÅ‘) is the highest trump (unlike most Jass where Under-Knave is highest). Players declare combinations at start and during playâ€”sets of equal cards and sequences in suit. Popular in Hungary around the turn of the 19thâ€“20th century (e.g. SÃ¡ndor BrÃ³dy); declined by mid-1920s. Austrian version called Tartl.

games.name: Tau Ngau
games.description: Tau Ngau (Bull Fighting) has two main forms. Domino version: 3â€“6 players, banker deals five tiles each; discard three that total a multiple of ten (tiles 4-2 and 2-1 are wild); remaining two tiles give score (mod 10); beat the banker. Card version (Ngau/Gnau): 52-card deck, 2+ players; five cards each; choose three that sum to a multiple of 10 or are three-of-a-kind to be scoring-eligible; two remaining cards give Ox power (face=10, 3s and 6s can be 3 or 6). Hand ranks: Five Dukes, All-Small, Double-Ox, etc. Played in Southeast Asia as casual or gambling game.

games.name: Tausendeins
games.description: Tausendeins (1001, Kiautschou) is a German two-player point-trick game. First to 1001 points wins. 24 cards (9 through Ace per suit). Rank: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9. Points: A=11, 10=10, K=4, Q=3, J=2, 9=0. No trumps initially; a player on lead with King-Queen in the same suit may declare marriage (Hochzeit) by playing one and naming that suit trump. Similar to Sixty-Six; fast, free play. First published 1930 by Robert HÃ¼lsemann; likely devised by soldiers in German Kiaochow (1898â€“1914).

games.name: Teen Do Panch
games.description: Teen Do Panch (3-2-5, 5-3-2) is a three-player trick-taking game popular in India, Pakistan, and Nepal. 30-card deck (remove 2â€“6, keep only 7â™¥ and 7â™ ). Rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7. Each player has a trick quota: right of dealer 5, left 3, dealer 2. Deal 5-3-2 to each; first player chooses trump or next 3 cards decide. Follow suit, trump or discard. Ten tricks; score = tricks won minus quota. Card-pulling: players who exceeded quota steal one card per extra trick from those short.

games.name: Teen Do Panch (3-2-5)
games.description: 3-2-5 (Teen Do Panch, also 2-3-5 or 5-3-2) is a trick-taking card game played in India, Pakistan, and Nepal. Three players use a 30-card deck. Each has a trick quota: dealer 2, player to dealer's right 5, player to dealer's left 3. The 5-trick player chooses trump and leads. Players above quota can 'pull' cards from those below in the next deal.
games.deck: 30 cards (remove 2s–6s from 52; keep 7s of hearts and spades). Rank: A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7.

games.name: Tehonbiki
games.description: Tehonbiki is a traditional Japanese gambling game where players guess a hidden number chosen by the banker using specialized numbered card sets and stake tiers.
games.deck: Specialized Tehonbiki numbered card sets (commonly 1-6 formats)

games.name: Teka
games.description: Teka is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from Afghanistan. 52 cards, 13 each. First to 104 points wins. Ace high to 2 low. Bidding: pass, ter, behi ter, or 8â€“13 tricks (or Double 13â€”win all tricks solo). Highest bidder is declarer, chooses trump, leads first trick with a trump. Follow suit; else any card. Declarer scores tricks won; Double 13 scores 26 or 52 to opponents if lost. New deal if a hand has no card above 10.

games.name: Telefunken
games.description: Telefunken is a contract rummy game popular in South America (Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia). 2â€“4 players, two 52-card decks plus four jokers (108 cards), 7 chips per player. First to empty hand by forming required melds across seven deals; lowest penalty wins. Melds: sets (3+ same rank), runs (3+ same suit). Each deal has a specific contract. Draw and discard; buy discards with chips before initial meld.

games.name: Telesina
games.description: Telesina (Teresina) is the Italian 5-card Stud. Variable deck (e.g. 5 players: 6â€“A, 36 cards). Ante; one face-down, one face-up each; highest face-up starts betting. Deal up to four face-up, one down; betting after each round. Flush ranks above full house. Variants: Con Vela (community card), with Joker (pokerissimo).

games.name: Terrace
games.description: Terrace is a two-deck solitaire for one player. Shuffle two decks; 11 cards face-up reserve, 8 foundation piles, 9 tableau piles. Deal 3 to three tableaus, choose one for first foundation (only that rank to foundations). Build foundations up in alternating colours (A between K and 2); tableaus down in alternating colours. Reserve: only top card to foundations. Empty tableau filled from stock or discard. Goal: move all 104 cards to foundations.

games.name: Texas 42
games.description: Texas 42 is a four-player partnership trick-taking game using a double-six domino set (28 tiles). Each draws 7; bid 30â€“42 (points the team will take). High bidder names trump (blanks, 1sâ€“6s, doubles, or no-trump) and leads. Follow suit; else any tile. 42 points per hand: 1 per trick plus count tiles (5-5 and 6-4 = 10 each; 5-0, 4-1, 3-2 = 5 each). Meet bid to score; else opponents get bid plus points. First to 250 (or 7 marks) wins.

games.name: Texas 88
games.description: Texas 88 is a six-player version of Texas 42 using two double-six sets. Two teams of three, alternating seats. Each gets 9 tiles; 2 in kitty. Bid from 60 in steps of 2 up to 88 (or 176, 264, 352). High bidder may exchange with kitty. Follow suit; count tiles (5 or 10 pips) and 2 per trick = 88 points per round. First to 500 (or 7 marks) wins. No Nel-O, Plunge, or Forced Bidding.

games.name: Texas Hold'em
games.description: Texas Hold'em is the world's most popular poker variant. Each player receives two private hole cards, and five community cards are dealt face-up on the table. Players make the best five-card poker hand using any combination of their hole cards and the community cards. The game features four rounds of betting and combines skill, strategy, and psychology.

games.name: Thats It
games.description: That's It! is a western domino game played with a double-15 set, providing a very large tile pool for longer sessions and larger tables. Players use standard matching placements while managing mobility and pip exposure with higher-number tiles that increase blocking complexity and swingy end control.

games.name: The Bitch
games.description: The Bitch is a Seven Card Stud poker variant where the Queen of Spades (the 'Bitch') is a game-disrupting card. If the Qâ™  is dealt face-up to any player, the deal immediately stops â€” all cards are thrown in, reshuffled, and redealt to only those players who had not yet folded. At showdown, the entire pot is split between the best high hand and the player holding the Qâ™  face-down in the hole (if anyone has it). If the Qâ™  was never dealt, the best hand wins the whole pot.

games.name: The Great Dalmuti
games.description: The Great Dalmuti is a shedding game by Richard Garfield (Wizards of the Coast, 1995) for 4â€“8 players. 80 cards: one 1, two 2s â€¦ up to twelve 12s, plus two Jesters (wild).
