Get rid of all cards; first out is Greater Dalmuti next round. Play sets of equal rank; each new play must be lower rank; pass if unable. When all but one pass, that player leads next. Seating by draw: Greater/Lesser Dalmuti, Greater/Lesser Peon. Peons give lowest cards to Dalmutis (who return any). Reseat after each hand by finish order.

games.name: Thirty-One (Greek)
games.description: Thirty-One (often called '31' or 'H τριανταμία' in Greek) is a simple draw-and-discard game popular in Greece and worldwide. Players try to collect a hand of three cards in the same suit totaling 31 points (Ace=11, Face=10). The player with the lowest score loses a life.
games.origin: Europe (possibly France or Germany, very popular in Greece)

games.name: Thirty-One (Scat)
games.description: Thirty-One, also known as Scat or Blitz, is a classic accumulation game for two or more players. The goal is to obtain a hand with a point total as close to 31 as possible in a single suit. It is widely played in Northwest Europe and North America and is a staple of pub culture.

games.name: Three Card Monte
games.description: Three Card Monte is not a true game but a confidence trick: the dealer shows three cards (one is the queen), throws them face-down, and the punter bets on which is the queen. The dealer uses sleight of hand so the punter loses. Known as Find the Lady in Britain and Bonneteau in France.

games.name: Three Card Poker
games.description: Three Card Poker is a popular casino table game based on poker. Players compete against the dealer. It features two modes of play: Ante/Play (playing against the dealer) and Pair Plus (betting on the hand value alone). It is known for its speed and simplicity.

games.name: Three Nought Four
games.description: 304 is a trick-taking partnership game for four. 32-card deck. Card values: J=30, 9=20, A=11, 10=10, K=3, Q=2, 8=7=0. Total 304 points. Bid from 160 in tens; highest bidder sets trump face-down then remaining cards dealt. Follow suit; bidding team must make bid in points. Popular in Sri Lanka and India.

games.name: Three-Thirteen Rummy
games.description: Rummy variant with eleven rounds. In round 1 three cards are dealt to each player, in round 2 four cards, and so on up to thirteen in round 11. Each round has a different wild card: round 1 threes are wild, round 2 fours, up to kings wild in round 11. Players draw one card from the stock or top of the discard pile, then discard one. Object is to form all cards into sets of three or more of the same rank or runs of three or more in the same suit; aces rank low. Lowest total penalty after eleven rounds wins.

games.name: Thunee
games.description: Thunee (or Thuni) is a popular trick-taking card game in South Africa, particularly among Indian South Africans in Durban. It is related to the Jass family of games (like 304). The name 'Thunee' means 'water' in Tamil (though the connection is debated) or refers to a specific call. Unusually, the Jack and Nine are the highest cards. The game involves bidding and 'ball' scoring.

games.name: Thuni (Nigerian)
games.description: Nigerian Thuni is a trick-taking game related to South African Thunee but played as a plain-trick game (no card points). The objective is winning tricks rather than counting card values, though the unusual ranking (J-9 high) remains.

games.name: Tianjin Mahjong
games.description: Tianjin Mahjong is a Chinese regional Mahjong variant associated with Tianjin and commonly played without flower tiles. It uses a compact classical tile base and emphasizes local validity and scoring conventions.

games.name: Tiddly-Wink American
games.description: Tiddly-Wink American is a domino connecting game from the Block game family. Each player is dealt three tiles from a double-six set; play forms a single arm. Playing a double grants an optional second play. The player who dominoes wins the pool, or the lowest pip count wins if blocked.

games.name: Tiddly-Wink British
games.description: Tiddly-Wink British is a domino connecting game in the Block family. Players receive tiles from a double-six set (or double-nine or double-twelve for more players), the holder of the largest double leads, and tiles are played on either end of the line with matching ends. Playing a double gives the option of a second tile in the same turn. The winner is the player who dominoes, or the player with the lowest pip count if the game is blocked.
games.deck: Double-six domino set (double-nine or double-twelve for more players)

games.name: Tien Gow
games.description: Tien Gow (Heaven Nine) is the oldest and most prestigious Chinese domino game. It is a trick-taking game played with a single set of 32 Chinese domino tiles. Players lead tricks with single tiles, pairs, triples, or quadruplets, and others must follow with higher-ranking tiles of the same group (Civil or Military). It is a game of deep tactical complexity and cultural heritage.

games.name: Tien Len
games.description: Tien Len (Tiáº¿n LÃªn), often called 'Thirteen' or 'Killer 13', is the national card game of Vietnam. It is a climbing/shedding game similar to Big Two and President. Players race to empty their hands by playing combinations that beat the previous play. The Two (Heo) is the highest card, and special 'bombs' can beat Twos.

games.name: Tile Matching Solitaire
games.description: Solitaire game using around 144 tiles (traditionally Mah Jong). Tiles are stacked in layers with horizontal rows; each row rests on the row below. Remove all tiles by taking matching pairs of exposed tiles (a tile is exposed when at the end of a row and not covered).

games.name: Tile Rummy
games.description: Tile Rummy is a rummy card game that involves melding, sets, runs. The game originated in USA/UK and has become popular worldwide.

games.name: Tiu-U
games.description: Tiu-U é‡£é­š is a domino card game that involves tiles, matching, scoring. The game originated in China and has become popular worldwide.
games.deck: Two sets of Chinese dominoes (64 tiles)

games.name: Tjuv
games.description: Tjuv (Swedish for 'Thief') is a fishing card game for two or more players. It is sometimes known as Tattare. Unlike traditional Casino, capturing is based on suit and rank hierarchy rather than numerical value. A unique feature is the ability to 'steal' captured piles from opponents if you have a matching card of higher rank.

games.name: Tod und Leben
games.description: Tod und Leben (Death and Life) is a simple German card game for two players, similar to War. It is distinct in that players have their own draw piles and must win cards to stay 'alive'. The game ends when one player loses all their cards (Death) and the other has all of them (Life).

games.name: Toepen
games.description: Toepen is a Dutch no-trump last-trick game for 3-8 players. Stakes increase through knocking, which forces fold-or-stay decisions and turns each four-trick hand into a bluffing and risk-management contest.
games.deck: 32-card French pack (10, 9, 8, 7, A, K, Q, J in each suit)

games.name: Tong Its
games.description: Tong Its is a popular Rummy-style game from the Philippines for three players. It involves drawing, melding sets/runs, and discarding. Players aim to empty their hands ('Tong Its') or minimize points. It features a mechanism to 'Draw' (fight) where players compare scores to end the hand early.

games.name: Tonk
games.description: Tonk (or Tunk) is a fast-paced matching card game popular in the USA. It combines features of Rummy and 'Knock' games (like Gin). Players aim to form spreads (books/runs) or 'Drop' (knock) with a low point count.

games.name: Top Trumps
games.description: Top Trumps is a comparison card game in which each player holds themed cards showing one item (e.g. a car, a dinosaur) and several numerical attributes. The starting player names an attribute; everyone reveals that attribute's value from their top card; the highest (or best) value wins the round and the winner takes all those cards. The winner then chooses the next attribute. Play continues until one player has won all the cards. The game was first published in the UK in 1978 and is popular with families and children.
games.deck: Themed pack (typically 30, 32, 48 or 50 cards per deck)

games.name: Toruro
games.description: Toruro is a Spanish trick-taking gambling game for 5+ players using a 40-card Spanish deck. There are three pots (Cabeza, Barriga, Cola), one for each trick. Players decide whether to 'go' (ir) or pass, and those who go must win at least one trick or pay a penalty (Lulo). The card ranking features the unusual A-3-K order common in L'Hombre games.

games.name: Tractor (Sheng Ji)
games.description: Tractor (拖拉机 Tuō Lā Jī), also known as Sheng Ji (升级, 'Level Up'), is one of the most popular card games in China. It is a 4-player partnership trick-taking game using two standard decks (108 cards). The unique feature is a dynamic trump system where the trump rank changes as teams 'level up' from 2 through Ace. Point cards are K=10, 10=10, 5=5.

games.name: Trains
games.description: Trains is a simultaneous-play card game where players race to form a 'Train' â€” a complete ascending sequence using all cards in their hand, starting from a 2. The game is played over 4 rounds with decreasing draw piles.

games.name: Traversone
games.description: Traversone (also Rovescino, CiapanÃ², Tressette a Perdere) is an Italian reverse trick-taking game where players try to AVOID taking point cards. It uses the Tressette ranking (3-2-A high) and scoring system, but the goal is inverted â€” whoever accumulates the MOST points loses. A 'Cappotto' (sweep) reverses the penalty to opponents.

games.name: Trees Poker
games.description: Poker variant with a tree-themed or environmental twist. Players receive five cards face-down, post an ante, and play one round of betting (check, bet, call, raise, or fold) before showdown; highest standard poker hand wins the pot.

games.name: Treikort
games.description: Treikort is a unique Icelandic trick-taking game for exactly three players using a specially selected 27-card deck. The game features 'BÃ­sefarnir' (Sevens) that are unbeatable when led but worthless when following. A 'Pope' title is earned by winning 13 tricks across 3 consecutive games, granting card-swapping privileges.

games.name: Tres y Dos
games.description: Tres y Dos (Three and Two) is a simple Rummy-style game from the Dominican Republic, Cuba, and Puerto Rico. Players draw and discard to form a 'Full House' â€” three cards of one rank plus two cards of another rank. First to complete this hand wins.

games.name: Tresillo
games.description: Tresillo (also Rocambor) is a historic Spanish trick-taking game for three players. It is the Spanish descendant of L'Hombre (Ombre), which was once the most popular card game in Europe. The 'declarer' (El Hombre) plays alone against the other two. Uses a 40-card Spanish deck with the unusual A-3-K ranking.

games.name: Tressette
games.description: Tressette is one of the great Italian card games. It is a partnership trick-taking game for 4 players using a 40-card Italian deck. The unique ranking (3-2-A high) and the lack of trumps create a pure suit-following game where communication and memory are paramount. There are 11 points per deal.

games.name: Tri Palki
games.description: Tri Palki (Ð¢Ñ€Ð¸ Ð¿Ð°Ð»ÐºÐ¸, 'Three Sticks') is a Russian card game where players try to avoid busting past 31 points. Each player holds 4 cards and plays one card per turn, adding to a running total. If your card pushes the total over 31, you earn a 'palka' (stick). Three sticks and you're out.

games.name: Tribello
games.description: Tribello is a 3-player trick-taking game from Illinois, USA with 4 distinct rounds over 12 deals. Each round changes the trump rules and objectives: Round 1 (cut trump), Round 2 (dealer picks trump), Round 3 (no trump), Round 4 (Nullo â€” avoid tricks). Players have positional trick quotas and score +/- based on performance vs quota.

games.name: Trijumf
games.description: Trijumf (Croatian Triumph) is a popular trick-taking game played along the Croatian coast and islands. It combines elements of Briscola and Tressette using a 40-card Italian deck. Features A-3-K ranking, trump suits, AkuÅ¾anje (declarations for bonus points), and plays to 401 or 501 points.

games.name: Trionfetti
games.description: Trionfetti is a four-player partnership game from the rural area between Venice and Padua, played with an Italian suited 40- or 52-card deck. It is a relative of Truc and Put: the aim is to win at least two of three tricks per hand. The cutter (to dealer's left) freely chooses and announces the card ranking (comanda) for each smazzata; four consecutive hands are played from the same deck so players gain information across hands. First team to 20 points wins a game; first to 3 games wins the match.

games.name: Trionfo Beccaccino
games.description: Trionfo Beccaccino (also Marafone Beccaccino) is a 4-player partnership trick-taking game from Romagna, Italy. It combines Tressette scoring (3-2-A ranking) with a trump suit (Trionfa). The 4â™¦ holder chooses trump. The Maraffa/Cricca (A+2+3 of trumps) earns 3 bonus points. Game to 41.

games.name: Tripoli
games.description: Tripoli (Tripoley) is a multi-phase card game combining Pay Cards, Poker, and a Michigan Rummy (Stops) phase. Players ante chips onto a board with labeled sections. Holders of specific Heart cards collect from those sections. Then a Poker round is played, followed by a Stops/Shedding phase. Descended from the 500-year-old German game Poch.

games.name: Trips to Win (5 Card Draw)
games.description: Trips to Win: Five Card Draw variant. To win at showdown you must hold at least three of a kind (trips). Otherwise the hand is a push and the pot carries over.

games.name: Trix
games.description: Trix (Trex) is a popular Middle Eastern compendium card game for 4 players. Each player 'owns a kingdom' of 5 contracts, choosing the order. 4 contracts are trick-avoidance (avoid Kâ™¥, Queens, Diamonds, or Tricks). The 5th contract 'Trix' is a shedding game where players play to a layout starting from Jacks. 20 deals total (4 kingdoms x 5 contracts).

games.name: Trjámann
games.description: Trjámann is an Icelandic trick-taking game for 3 players using a 48-card deck (no 2s). Features 4 contract types (Nullo, Grand, Spades, Other) chosen in rotation. The contract chooser exchanges with a 4-card 'Manni' (widow). Each player must play all 4 contracts once over 12 rounds. First to 10+ points wins.

games.name: Troccas
games.description: Troccas is a traditional Swiss Tarot game played in the Romansh-speaking Surselva region of Grisons. It uses a 78-card Swiss 1JJ Tarot deck with Italian suits. Notable for the 'King and Jack Rule' (King demands Jack surrender) and coded signals (Tschintschar). Partnership play for 4.

games.name: Troefcall
games.description: Troefcall is a 4-player partnership trick-taking game from Suriname, also popular in the Netherlands. The 'trump caller' gets 5 cards first and declares trump. Teams try to win 7+ tricks. Winning first 7 in a row = 'Kap Partij' (5 pts). All 13 = 'Baunie' (15 pts). If Baunie attempted but failed, opponents score 2.

games.name: Troeven
games.description: Troeven is a Dutch/Flemish trick-taking game where players start at a score (e.g., 7) and work down to zero. Uses a 32-card deck (7-A). The trump caller picks trump from first 4-5 cards. Win more card-value points (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1) than opponents to reduce score by 1. If trump caller loses, their team gains a point (penalty).

games.name: Troggu
games.description: Troggu (Trogga) is a Swiss Tarot game from the German-speaking Valais. Uses a modified 62-card Tarot deck. 3-8 players. Features bidding (Normal/Solo), Tapp exchange, the unique Fool as highest trump, and Misere when all pass. The secret partner mechanic (calling a trump card) adds intrigue in 7-8 player games.

games.name: Truc
games.description: Truc is a 15th-century bluffing trick-taking game from France and Spain. Players get 3 cards and try to win 2 of 3 tricks. NO TRUMP and NO suit obligation â€” highest card wins regardless of suit (7 is highest in French version). Equal cards spoil the trick. Major bluffing component: players can propose to raise stakes at any point.

games.name: Truco
games.description: Truco (Argentine) is the national card game of Argentina and one of the most popular in South America. 2-6 players with 40-card Spanish deck. 3 cards each, win 2/3 tricks. Unique card hierarchy (Aâ™  > Aâ™£ > 7â™  > 7â™¦). Three betting lances: Envido (hand value), Truco (trick stakes), and Flor (3 same suit). Heavy bluffing.

games.name: Truf
games.description: Truf is an Indonesian trick-taking game for 4 players. Unique bidding: each player simultaneously places a card face-down â€” the rank indicates how many tricks they bid (court cards = 0, A = 1, numbers = face value). Highest bidder's card suit becomes trump. Trump cards are played face down and revealed later. Exact bid = points; over/under = penalty.

games.name: Tsung Shap
games.description: Tsung Shap (Disputing Tens) is a Chinese domino game adapted for cards. 2 players capture pairs of identical cards and sets of 3 cards summing to multiples of 10 from the ends of a row. Pairs score 10x pip value. Sweeps score 40 bonus. Can be played with standard card deck using Fishing mechanics.
games.deck: 32 Chinese dominoes or adapted standard deck

games.name: Tunkhannock 14-point Pitch
games.description: Tunkhannock 14-point Pitch is a Pennsylvania cutthroat or partnership Pitch variant using a 54-card deck (52 plus two jokers). Six cards each, then bid 3 to 15 (smudge); after bidding, discard three and replenish. Off-jack and jokers rank as trumps below the jack. Fourteen points (high, low, jack, off-jack, jokers, game, last trick, high spade, five) to win.

games.name: Tuong
games.description: Tuong (TÆ°á»›ng) is a Vietnamese climbing/shedding card game closely related to Tiáº¿n LÃªn (Thirteen). 4 players, 52-card deck, 13 cards each. 2 is highest. Goal: shed all cards first. Singles, pairs, triples, straights, double-sequences all valid. 'Bombs' (four-of-a-kind, long double-sequences) can beat 2s.

games.name: Tuppenny Ha'penny Loo
games.description: Tuppenny Ha'penny Loo is a simple matching/penalty card game. Players hold 5 cards and 5 buttons. Cards are played face down in turn; if the next player matches the rank, the previous player pays buttons to the pot. Consecutive matches escalate the penalty (1, 2, 3 buttons). Player who runs out of buttons loses.

games.name: Turbo Hearts
games.description: Turbo Hearts is an American Hearts variant introduced at Upenn in the 1980s by Richard Garfield, based on the Chinese game Gong Zhu. Four players receive 13 cards each, pass three in rotation, then may turbo-charge one of four special cards (Ace of Hearts, Queen of Spades, Jack of Diamonds, Ten of Clubs) to multiply its effect. Lowest score when someone reaches 100 wins.

games.name: Turkish Poker
games.description: Türk pokeri (Turkish Poker) is a five-card draw variant played with a short deck of 24 to 36 cards depending on player count. Each player receives five cards; up to four may be exchanged in the draw. Opening requires a pair of Kings; hand rankings differ from international poker (flush beats full house, three of a kind beats straight).

games.name: Turnover Bridge
games.description: Turnover Bridge is a 2-player trick game (more related to Whist than Bridge). 52-card deck, 26 each. Layout: 12 face-down in row + 12 face-up on top + 2 secret hole cards. Spades permanently trump. Play face-up cards or hole cards. When face-up played, turn over card beneath. Win 14+ of 26 tricks. Information warfare: visible cards vs hidden cards.

games.name: Tute
games.description: Tute is one of Spain's most popular card games, played with a 40-card Spanish deck. Named from Italian 'tutti'. Features A-3-K ranking, strict follow-suit/trump rules, and 'Cantes' (declaring K+Kt of same suit for bonus). Collecting all 4 Kings or 4 Knights = instant Tute win. 10 bonus for last trick.

games.name: Tute americano
games.description: Tute americano: Tute variant with American deck (52 cards) or 40-card strip. Same point-trick and Cantes logic; variant rules.

games.name: Tute arrastrado
games.description: Tute arrastrado is a Tute variant for three or four players (with four, the dealer sits out each hand). Thirteen cards each from a 40-card Spanish pack; last card turned for trump. Follow suit and overtake or trump; after winning a trick you may sing 20 or 40 (40 before 20); tute (four kings or four horses) wins the hand outright. Chip payments: 100 or 200 from each opponent, plus 40 or 20 per declaration.

games.name: Tute cabrero
games.description: Tute cabrero is a point-trick elimination game for 3 to 6 players, popular in Argentina and Uruguay. Each deal you aim either to take no tricks or to finish with the highest or lowest point total; middle totals lose. Four losses eliminate a player; the last one or two remaining win. Uses the standard 40-card Spanish deck with follow-suit and optional singing (declaring king-horse for 20 or 40 points after winning a trick).

games.name: Tute corriente
games.description: Tute corriente is the oldest two-player form of Tute from Spain. Six cards each, 13th face up for trump, rest as stock. No follow suit until stock is empty; then must follow and beat or trump. First to 101 points or tute (four kings or horses) wins.

games.name: Tute gana-pierde
games.description: Tute gana-pierde: win-lose Tute variant. First to reach target wins; or lose condition. 40-card Spanish.

games.name: Tute habanero
games.description: Two-player Tute variant with eight cards each and a stock; same as Tute corriente except capote (announce to take all last eight tricks). 40-card Spanish.

games.name: Tute individual
games.description: Tute for two players; no partnerships. Standard 40-card Spanish deck. Ten cards each, stock with face-up trump; follow suit and overtake; Cantes (40/20) after winning a trick; Tute (4 Kings or 4 Knights) wins the deal. Most points in the deal wins that game; session is multiple deals.

games.name: Tute subastado
games.description: Tute subastado: auction Tute. Trump or contract determined by auction/bidding. 40-card Spanish.

games.name: Tuxedo
games.description: Tuxedo is a card-capturing game invented by George Parker, played with a 56-card Rook deck (no Rook card). 4 cards per player + 4 face-up in the 'pond'. Capture by matching number or matching sums. Sweeps (clearing the pond) score bonus. 'Orange' call bonus for capturing red+yellow together. First to 100 wins.

games.name: Twenty-Five
games.description: Twenty-Five is the national card game of Ireland. 2-10 players, 52-card deck, 5 cards each. Unique ranking: 5 of trumps is HIGHEST, then J of trumps, then Aâ™¥ (always 3rd trump). Black suits rank low-to-high (A-2-3...10), red rank high-to-low (K-Q-J...A). 'Rob the pack' if dealt A of trumps. Each trick = 5 pts, first to 25 wins.

games.name: Twenty-Four
games.description: 24 is a mathematical card game: use four numbers (from four cards) and only +, Ã¢Ë†â€™, Ãƒâ€”, ÃƒÂ· (and parentheses) to make exactly 24. All four numbers must be used once. First to call a correct solution wins the four cards (or they go to opponent); play until one player has no cards. Popular in China since at least the 1960s (Shanghai); also played in North America.
games.deck: 40 cards (AÃ¢â‚¬â€œ10 only; remove face cards and jokers)

games.name: Twenty-Nine
games.description: Twenty-Nine is a trick-taking card game for four players in partnerships. Played with 32 cards; Jack and Nine rank high in every suit. Popular in India, Bangladesh, and Nepal; descended from the European Jass family.

games.name: Twenty-Six
games.description: Twenty-Six is a trick-taking round game in the Cucumber/Twenty-Two family. Suits irrelevant; rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. Players lead single cards or sets of equal rank; others must equal or beat the highest played, or play lowest. Winner of the last trick is penalised (e.g. keeps losing card or gets penalty points). For 2-6 players, 52 cards.

games.name: Twenty-Two
games.description: Twenty-Two (also known as 22) is a trick-taking card game where the winner of the last trick is penalised. Players try to avoid taking the final trick; the losing card is kept as penalty points (Aces 11, face cards 10, others face value). First player to reach 22 or more points is eliminated; last player remaining wins. Suits are irrelevant; cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2.

games.name: Twist'em
games.description: Twist'em (Double-Hand Dominoes) is a casino banking game played with a double-six domino set. Each player and the banker receive three tiles and arrange them into a top hand and a bottom hand (pip totals mod 10, nine high). Players bet against the banker; both hands must outrank the banker's two hands to win. Based on Pai Gow but with Western dominoes.

games.name: Two Hundred
games.description: 200 (Deux Cents) is a point-trick partnership card game from Canada, especially popular in New Brunswick. Four players use a 36-card deck (2s, 3s, 4s, 6s removed). Teams bid in increments of 5 (50-100); highest bidder names trump and must make their bid. First team to 200 points wins.

games.name: Two Hundred and Twenty
games.description: 220 is a bidding variant of Twenty-Five, Ireland's national card game. Players bid and play tricks; each trick is worth 5 points. First side to reach 220 points wins. Uses standard 52-card deck, 5 cards each, next card for trump. Trump order: 5, J, A, K, Q, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4, 3, 2; Ace of Hearts is always trump.

games.name: Two Plus One Poker
games.description: Guts-style poker variant. Each player is dealt two cards; players declare in or out; those who are in receive a third card. Hands rank as in Three-card Guts (three of a kind, straight flush, straight, flush, pair, nothing). Losers who stayed in match the pot.

games.name: U-G-O
games.description: U-G-O is a combat card game for two or more players where each player uses their own 52-card deck (different backs). Cards are played vertically (attack) or horizontally (defense). Players attack opponents' cards by playing higher-valued cards. Defense cards may be played face-up or face-down. Goal: exhaust your opponent's deck before yours runs out. Special abilities on Aces, Kings, Queens, Jacks, 8s, 9s, and 10s; Equip cards (Diamonds) and suit abilities (Spades, Hearts, Clubs).

games.name: Ugly
games.description: Ugly is an Australian trick-taking/avoidance game similar to Hearts. 3-4 players, 52-card deck. Players choose trumps each round. Jacks are negative. The 7â™¦ (Ugly Card) doubles Jack penalties OR doubles trick scores if no Jacks captured. The 7â™£ (Charm Card) cancels Ugly's doubling. Card passing escalates each round.

games.name: Uke-Shogi
games.description: Uke-Shogi is a Japanese defensive card game inspired by Shogi (Japanese Chess) concepts. The 'Uke' (受け) refers to defense. Players use standard cards to represent chess-like pieces, focusing on defensive positioning and piece capture mechanics. A niche hybrid of card and board game concepts.
games.deck: Goita-related piece-card family (historically cited as 40-42 cards)

games.name: Ulti
games.description: Ulti is a complex 3-player Hungarian card game using a 32-card Hungarian deck. One player (declarer) bids and plays against two defenders. Key bids: Ulti (win last trick with trump 7), Betli (win no tricks), Durchmars (win all tricks). Features talon discard, combinable bids, kontras, and csendes (silent) bonuses.

games.name: Umtali
games.description: Umtali is a 2-player Rummy game from Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe). 10 cards each. Features 5 meld types: sets (no Jacks), runs, marriages (K+Q same suit for double), single Jacks, and single-card extensions. Opponent gets one final turn after someone goes out. Two-card melds allowed in final turn.

games.name: Valepaska
games.description: Valepaska is a Finnish bluffing/shedding game variant of Paskahousu. 3-8 players. Cards played face-down with declarations — players can LIE about what they played. Other players call 'Valepaska!' to challenge. Wrong challenger picks up pile; caught liar picks up pile. Special cards: 2s (supercards), 10s clear pile, Aces clear face cards, four-of-a-kind clears.

games.name: Vändåtta
games.description: VÃ¤ndÃ¥tta is a popular Swedish shedding game similar to UNO/Crazy Eights using a standard deck. 2-5 players, 7 cards each. Match by suit or rank. 8s are wild (choose new suit). Aces force all players to draw 1. Must say 'Lappen!' with 1 card left or draw 3 penalty. Cannot go out on 8 or A.

games.name: Vändtia
games.description: VÃ¤ndtia (Swedish Shithead) is a popular Swedish shedding game. 2-4 players, 52 cards. 9 cards each: 3 face-down, 3 face-up on top, 3 in hand. Must play equal/higher rank. 2=resets pile, 10=burns pile. Four-of-a-kind clears. Must draw to 3 from stock. Endgame plays face-up then blind face-down cards.

games.name: Vatikan
games.description: Vatikan is a Russian Rummy variant using double deck + 2 jokers (106 cards). 2-5 players, 13 each. Key feature: players can REARRANGE existing melds on the table to integrate new cards. First meld must be a sequence from hand. Jokers are wild but can't be moved between melds directly. Draw OR meld each turn (not both).

games.name: Vatra
games.description: Vatra ('Fire') is a card-passing party game for 3-13 players. Each player gets 4 cards (one rank per player). Pass cards to collect four-of-a-kind. First to four-of-a-kind calls 'Vatra!' Loser (last without) gets punishment: winner shuffles deck, loser names a card, cards flipped â€” each suit before that card = specific physical penalty.

games.name: Vazhushal
games.description: Vazhushal ('Wipe') is an Indian Rummy from Chennai (Tamil Nadu). 2-6 players. Unique discard LINE (not pile) â€” all discards visible. Can draw multiple consecutive cards from line if deepest card is used immediately in a NEW meld. First meld must include pure sequence. Players can rearrange own melds. Jokers wild.

games.name: Verish' Ne Verish'
games.description: Verish' Ne Verish' ('Believe It or Not') is the Russian version of BS/Cheat. 2-6+ players. Deal all cards. Play face-down declaring rank. Players call 'Ne Veryu!' to challenge. Wrong challengee picks up pile; wrong challenger picks up pile. Shed all cards to win.

games.name: Video Poker
games.description: Video Poker is a casino card game played on machines (or digitally). Based on Five-Card Draw poker. Player gets 5 cards, chooses which to hold/discard, draws replacements. Payout based on final hand strength. Jacks or Better is most common variant. Perfect strategy yields near 99.5% return.
games.deck: Standard 52-card deck (+ jokers in some variants)

games.name: Vier-Anderle
games.description: Vier-Anderle (Strassenwart) is a German Tarock gambling game from the Black Forest. 2-13 players (best 5-8). Uses 38-card Cego pack (tarocks only). 4 cards each. Win at least 1 trick or pay penalty equal to pot. When pot has money: players opt in/out; each trick wins Â¼ of pot; no tricks = pay pot amount.

games.name: Viersche
games.description: Viersche (Hundert/Hunderte) is a Black Forest German partnership trick-taking game. 4 players in 2 teams. 36-card deck. 9 cards each. Bottom card = trump. Forehand MUST lead trump first trick (if no trumps, lead face-down). Race to 100+ card points. First to claim 100 wins; erase 4 'rungs' to win session.

games.name: Vietnamese Mahjong
games.description: Vietnamese Mahjong is a Southeast Asian Mahjong profile commonly played with expanded bonus and joker-style tiles. It uses a larger 160-tile composition and regional scoring conventions.

games.name: Vint
games.description: Vint ('Screw') is a Russian partnership trick-taking game that influenced Contract Bridge's development. 4 players in 2 teams. 52-card deck. 13 each. Bidding (1-7 tricks over 6) with suit/NT denominations. NO dummy — all play own hands. Both sides score below-the-line for tricks won. First to 500 wins.

games.name: Vira
games.description: Vira is Sweden's historic national card game (19th century). 3-4 players (3 active). 52-card deck. 13 each + 13-card talon. Complex bidding with ~40 contract types. KÃ¶pspel (buy from talon), Solospel (no talon), Gaskspel (take all talon). Declarer vs 2 defenders. Scoring via 'virapulla' (token pot).

games.name: Vitou
games.description: Vitou is a traditional NiÃ§ois (Nice, France) trick-taking/bluffing game related to Truc. 4 players in 2 teams. 32-card deck. 3 cards each. Ranking: 10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7. NO suits, NO trumps. Best 2 of 3 tricks. Signals between partners ALLOWED. Raising stakes. First to 21 points wins.

games.name: Voormsi
games.description: Voormsi (Vorms) is the national card game of Greenland. 4 players in 2 teams. 36-card French deck. Related to KarnÃ¶ffel family (Europe's oldest card games). Features unusual card rankings and special card powers: Jâ™£='Toqutsit' (Executioner, highest), Kâ™¥='Voormsi'. Allows double/triple/quadruple tricks.

games.name: Wall Street Poker
games.description: Wall Street Poker is a Seven-Card Stud variant with buyable community cards. 2-7 players. 52-card deck. Deal 3 hole cards (2 down, 1 up). 4 community cards ('Wall Street') placed face-up with escalating costs (1-4 units). Players can buy a community card (goes to pot) or get a free card from deck. Named after aggressive financial bidding.

games.name: War
games.description: War is a simple children's card game. 2 players. 52-card deck split evenly. Both flip top card simultaneously — higher wins both. Tie = 'War': each plays 1 face-down then 1 face-up; higher face-up wins all. Continue until one player has all cards. Pure luck — no decisions.

games.name: Watten
games.description: Watten is an Alpine trick-taking game from Bavaria/Tyrol. 4 players in 2 teams. 32-card German deck. 5 cards each. Features trump SUIT + trump RANK (Schlag). Rechte (both suit+rank) = highest. Linke (other 3 of Schlag rank) are also top trumps. Criticals: Maxi (K♥), Belli (7♦), Spitz (7♣). NO obligation to follow suit. Secret partner signaling ALLOWED.

games.name: Wenzhou Mahjong
games.description: Wenzhou Mahjong is a Zhejiang regional Mahjong variant associated with Wenzhou play communities. It uses the standard Mahjong draw-discard loop with meld claims and a complete-hand win condition, while table profiles define specific win validity and scoring emphasis.

games.name: Whisky Poker
games.description: Whisky Poker is a poker-style game with widow hand exchange. Multiple players. 5 each + 5-card widow. Options: swap entire hand for widow (old hand becomes new widow face-up), swap 1 card with widow, or knock (triggers final round). Last best poker hand after knock wins. Worst hand pays chip.

games.name: Whist
games.description: Whist is the classic English partnership trick-taking game and ancestor of Bridge. 4 players, 2 teams. 52 cards, 13 each. Last card dealt (to dealer) turned face-up = trump. Eldest hand leads. Follow suit. Each trick over 6 = 1 point. Honours (A-K-Q-J of trump): 3 held = 2pts, 4 held = 4pts. Game to 5 (British) or 7 (American). Rubber = best of 3.

games.name: Whist Israeli
games.description: Four-player exact-bid trick-taking game popular in Israel. No partnerships; each player bids how many tricks they will take. Two-phase bidding sets contract and trick bids; scoring by exact bid (10 plus square of tricks) or penalty for off.

games.name: Whist Minnesota
games.description: Partnership trick-taking game with no trumps. Each hand players secretly choose to play high (Grand: take 7+ tricks) or low (Nula: take 6 or fewer) by laying a red or black card; first side to reach the target score (typically 13) wins.

games.name: Whist Romanian
games.description: Romanian Whist is an exact-prediction trick-taking game for 3 to 6 players. Each player bids how many tricks they will take; the sum of all bids must not equal the number of cards dealt. Players score for making their contract exactly and lose points for over- or undertricks.

games.name: Whist two-player
games.description: Two-player plain-trick game: 13 cards each, trump from the turned card on the stock. First 13 tricks are played with the winner taking the face-up stock card and the loser the face-down one; then 13 tricks without replenishment. The player who wins the majority of the second-stage tricks wins the hand.

games.name: Whot British
games.description: British variant of Whot, a Crazy Eights-style shedding game for two to six players. Use a Whot pack with five symbol suits and wild Whot cards; match suit or number on the play pile or draw from the stock. First to empty hand wins the round; penalty scoring over multiple rounds eliminates players who reach 100 points.
games.deck: Whot deck (54 cards; British packs may have 53)

games.name: Whot Nigerian
games.description: Nigerian variant of Whot: a shedding game in the Eights family. Players match suit or number or play Whot (wild) and special cards (Hold On, Pick Two, Pick Three, Suspension, General Market). First to empty hand wins; penalty scoring over rounds. Popular in West Africa.

games.name: Wiezen
games.description: Wiezen (Belgian Whist) is a Belgian 4-player trick-taking game with bidding and temporary alliances. 52-card deck, 13 each. Last card dealt = trump. Contracts: Troel (3 Aces, 4th Ace holder = partner), Solo (alone), Abondance (9+ alone), Misère (no tricks), Open Misère, Pico (exactly 1 trick), Solo Slim (all 13).

games.name: Woolworth Poker
games.description: Woolworth Poker is a home poker variant where 5s and 10s are wild cards (named after Woolworth's 'five and dime' stores). Any standard poker variant can use Woolworth rules. Wild 5s and 10s can represent any card. Five-of-a-kind becomes possible and ranks above straight flush.

games.name: Wuhan Mahjong
games.description: Wuhan Mahjong is a Hubei regional Mahjong variant associated with Wuhan play communities. It follows the standard draw-discard structure with meld claims and a complete-hand win condition, while the table profile determines which hands qualify and how scoring is evaluated.

games.name: Xeri
games.description: Xeri (Ξερή, 'dry') is a popular Greek fishing card game. 2 or 4 players. 52 cards. 6 each + 4 face-up on table. Match rank to capture entire pile. Jack captures any pile. 'Xeri' = capturing lone card (10pts bonus, Jack Xeri = 20pts). Score: most cards=3pts, A/K/Q/J/10=1pt each, 10♦=1pt extra, 2♣=1pt.

games.name: Xiàng Shí Fù
games.description: Xiàng Shí Fù ('Watching Ten Sets') is a Chinese solitaire domino game adapted for cards. Uses Chinese dominoes or equivalent card representations. Objective: arrange 32 tiles/cards into 10 valid triplets + 1 valid pair. Also known as Cān Chán ('Zen').
games.deck: Chinese domino set (32 tiles) or card equivalent

games.name: Xiangyang Mahjong
games.description: Xiangyang Mahjong is a Hubei regional Mahjong variant associated with Xiangyang play communities. It keeps the familiar Mahjong draw-discard structure with meld claims and a complete-hand win condition, while the table profile defines specific scoring and validity conventions.

games.name: Xoşkîn
games.description: Xoşkîn is a Kurdish trick-taking card game similar to 3-player double-deck Pinochle. Played in eastern/southeastern Turkey (Northern Kurdistan). Features bidding and melds. Also known as Nezere or Pinîkêr. Name possibly derived from English 'Auction' via 'Okşin'.

games.name: Yaniv
games.description: Yaniv is a popular Israeli draw-and-discard card game. 2-8 players. 54 cards (52 + 2 Jokers). 5 each. Goal: lowest hand value. Discard singles/sets/runs, draw 1. Call 'Yaniv!' when hand â‰¤ 5pts. If truly lowest = 0pts. If not = 'Assaf' penalty (+30). Score multiples of 50 = halved. Eliminated at 200.

games.name: Yonin-Kan
games.description: Yonin-Kan ('4-player Kan') is a Japanese trick-taking game from Aomori prefecture. 4 players. 40-card deck (remove 2-4s and 5â™ ). 10 each. Secret partnerships: Joker holder + J of trumps holder = 'kankei' team (revealed when played). Rotating trump sequence: â™£â†’â™¦â†’â™¥. Also called Damari-Kan ('Silent Kan').

games.name: Yukon
games.description: Yukon is a solitaire/patience card game similar to Klondike. 52 cards. 7 tableau columns. Key difference: can move ANY face-up card plus all cards covering it (no sequence required). No stock pile â€” all 52 cards dealt to tableau. Build foundations Aâ†’K by suit. Empty columns = Kings only.

games.name: Yukon Hold'em
games.description: Yukon Hold'em is a Texas Hold'em variant with TWO separate flops. 2 hole cards + 7 community cards (2 flops of 2, 2 turns, 1 river). At showdown, choose ONLY ONE of 2 community card sets to combine with hole cards. Best 5-card hand wins.

games.name: Z Poker
games.description: Z Poker is a little-known community card poker variant with 4 community cards instead of 5. Players get 2 hole cards and use a modified community card structure. Home game variant — unlikely found in casinos.

games.name: Žandari
games.description: Žandari (Pishpirik) is a Serbian/Balkan fishing card game. 2-4 players. 52-card deck. 4 face-up table + hand cards. Capture by matching rank or summing to played card value. Jack clears entire table. Score: most cards=2pts, most clubs=1pt, 2♣=1pt, 10♦=1pt. First to 11.

games.name: Zanga
games.description: Zanga is a Spanish trick-taking game related to Hombre/Tresillo. 4 players in 2 teams. 32-card Spanish deck. 8 each. Permanent trumps: Ace of Swords (highest), Ace of Clubs, King of Clubs. Trump chooser's team must win 5+ tricks. Winning all = bonus. Extra points for holding top 3+ trumps.

games.name: Zecchinetta
games.description: Zecchinetta (Lansquenet) is an Italian banking/gambling game. Banker vs players. 40-card Italian deck. Banker deals 2 player cards + 1 banker card face-up. Players bet on player cards. Banker draws cards: match player card = banker pays; match banker card = banker wins all bets. New unmatched cards become additional betting options.

games.name: Zhào Péngyou
games.description: Zhào Péngyou ('Finding Friends') is a Chinese multi-player trick-taking game. 5-12 players. Multiple decks + jokers. Trump maker 'calls' specific cards — holders become secret partners (kankei). Point cards: 5=5pts, 10/K=10pts (100 total). Teams level up through ranks. First to Ace level wins.

games.name: Zhēng Fēn
games.description: Zhēng Fēn ('Competing for Points') is a Chinese climbing/point-trick hybrid. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Shed cards through ascending combinations. Point cards: 5=5pts, 10/K=10pts. 100 total per hand. First out gets LAST player's tricks + remaining cards. Last out scores 0. Play to 500/1000.

games.name: Zhēng Shàngyóu
games.description: Zhēng Shàngyóu ('Struggling Upstream' / 'Climb to the Top') is a Chinese shedding/climbing game similar to President. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Play ascending combinations (singles/pairs/triples/sequences/bombs). First out wins. Ranking: 3-A-2-BlackJoker-RedJoker. Bombs beat any combination.

games.name: Zifuli
games.description: Zifuli is a 5-player variant of Cöch (Cucco), an Italian partnership trick-taking game from Bergamo. Uses the special 40-card Cucco deck (20 pairs). 8 cards each. Bidding phase determines secret partnerships: bid by naming a card you hold, the holder of the other copy becomes your partner (hidden until card is played). Can bid both copies = play alone. Overcall only by lower card of same suit. Win by capturing more card points (19 total).

games.name: Zole
games.description: Zole (Zolīte) is Latvia's national card game. 3 players (4-5 with dealer out). 26-card deck. 8 each + 2-card talon. Permanent trumps: Queens > Jacks > Diamonds. Declarer: take talon, discard 2, win 61+ of 120 card points. Solo = no talon. Mazais = lose every trick. Table game = fewest points.

games.name: Zsírozás
games.description: Zsírozás ('Greasing') is a traditional Hungarian trick game. 2-4 players. 32-card Hungarian deck. Suits are IRRELEVANT. Win trick by matching rank of led card (last match wins). Sevens are WILD. Capture 'zsír' (grease) cards: Aces + Tens (10pts each, 80 total). 40+ pts wins hand.

games.name: Zung Jung
games.description: Zung Jung is a modern Mahjong ruleset designed around transparent balanced scoring while preserving traditional draw-discard meld play. It is widely used when players want a structured alternative to many divergent house systems.

games.name: Zwanzig ab
games.description: Zwanzig ab ('Twenty Off') is a German trick game. 2-4 players. 32-card Skat deck. 5 each (2+3). Start at 20pts, subtract 1 per trick won. First to 0 wins. Forehand chooses trumps. Can exchange up to 3 cards. May drop out (except trump chooser). Hearts trumps = double scoring.

games.name: Zwanzigerrufen
games.description: Zwanzigerrufen ('Call the Twenty') is an Austrian Tarot game. 4 players. 40-card deck (from 54-card Industrie und Glück). 20 Tarocks + 20 suit cards. Declarer calls Tarock XX to find secret partner. Win 45+ of 88 card points. Simpler than Königrufen. Trull cards: Pagát(I), Mond(XXI), Sküs = 5pts each.

games.name: Zwicker
games.description: Zwicker (Zwickern) is a German fishing card game from Schleswig-Holstein. 52 cards + Jokers. Capture table cards by matching rank or summing values. 'Zwick' bonus for clearing entire table. Builds allowed (add/subtract to create target values). K=14, Q=13, J=12, A=11/1. More entertaining than Casino.
